paragraphs: Ding.
System Practiced the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique. - As a result of repeated practice, Sinews and Meridians and Muscles and Bones each increase by 1.
“Whew.”
I opened my eyes with a deep exhale. In the predawn gloom, the candlelit room shimmered amber.
Failed again.
My fist clenched in the silence.
How many attempts had that been? Twenty? Thirty? The result was what mattered. Once again, I had failed to draw out the hardened mass of internal energy.
Should I take comfort in the fact that I’m getting better?

I was gradually getting used to handling internal energy. If I had been a C-rank Hunter instead of an F-rank—or at least a D-rank—I would have adapted much faster. But reality was cold and unforgiving.
The steady improvement in my Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians must be helping too.

Internal energy flowed through the body’s meridians. The more I practiced my cultivation technique and improved those two attributes, the wider and sturdier the pathways became. Compared to when I had started, I could circulate far more internal energy at a much faster speed.
It’s all thanks to the Skill Points.
The ten Skill Points awarded with every level-up were doing their job. Nothing nourished my Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians better.
Open Skill Window.

System Skill Window Lv. 17 Jin Taekyung Cultivation Technique: Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique (Fourth Stage) Martial Arts: Jin Family’s Spear Technique (Fifth Stage) / Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique (Fifth Stage) Muscles and Bones: 105 Remaining Points: 0
I can see a chance.
The impregnable fortress was gradually shrinking and growing flimsier. If I kept hammering away at it, I felt as though the gate would soon open.
Fortunately, I might lack talent, but I had persistence.
I’ll keep trying until it works.
I was about to sit cross-legged again and circulate my qi when my senses, sharpened by the many earlier attempts, picked up an unusual sound.
This is...
A low, droning hum. At first, it sounded like a swarm of bees, but it was actually the murmur of many people.
What’s going on?
I channeled internal energy into my ears. Perhaps because of the distance, it still wasn’t nearly enough to make out everything clearly.
But it was enough.
One word stood out among the indistinct voices.
Battle!
The Mount Heng Sword Sect. The battle had finally begun.
I hurriedly uncrossed my legs and sprang to my feet. Then I leaped through the half-open window.
I landed like a cat. Before me, lights came on across the pavilions one by one.
So, in the end...
It had begun.
Twenty-five.
That was the number of corpses laid out in orderly rows.
When I saw them lying there like dead trees, every trace of life gone, I was left speechless.
“This is...”
I was a Hunter. I had fought countless battles and witnessed countless deaths.
Poisoned, cut apart, crushed, blown to pieces...
The manner of death varied wildly depending on the monster involved. But all those deaths had one thing in common.
Every victim had been an adult.
Adulthood was one of the basic conditions for awakening. No one knew what the exact standard was or why it existed. It was simply a rule accepted as naturally as the existence of Gates.
That was why none of the countless deaths I had witnessed had ever involved a child.
This is a game. It’s just a game.
I kept repeating the words to myself. But the sight before me was too horrific to dismiss so easily.
BLOOD
The character had been carved into their foreheads. Torchlight reflected off the dried blood.
More than ten children had gone cold like that.
The oldest could not have been more than middle-school age. Some looked even younger.
Every single one of them was dead.
“Urgh!”
One of the martial artists holding a torch in a trembling hand doubled over. Soon, the sound of retching rang out from all around us.
Then a hand reached down and picked up the torch he had dropped.
“Somi. Yes, that was her name. On the day I became acting Family Head, the Branch Leader of Eung-hyeon bragged about her until his mouth ran dry, calling her his treasure.”
It was Jin Wikyung. His eyes dim and lifeless, he raised the torch and shone it over the children’s faces.
One by one.
Each time another face was revealed, he spoke the child’s name without fail.
After naming the last child, Jin Wikyung looked at me.
“Do you know who these children are?”
“They were members of our family sent to the branches in Eung-hyeon, Saneum, and Sakju.”
I didn’t know where those places were. But I could guess what fate the children’s parents had met.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect’s intentions made me sick.
Fucking psychotic bastards.
Look. We can slaughter even children this young. Soon, you’ll end up the same way.
I could almost hear the voice of the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, a man whose face I had never even seen.
“This is all my fault. Even children who knew no martial arts were slaughtered so cruelly...”
Jin Wikyung was blaming himself in a trembling voice when—
“That is the essence of war, Lesser Family Head.”
The Head Elder appeared, stroking his silver beard. His gaze remained calm as it swept over the corpses.

“Victory and defeat—neither comes without death. The Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect... Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, was it? As one would expect of a former wandering martial artist, he understands war well. These children alone make that clear.”
The casual way he said it sent a chill through me.
What the hell is wrong with this AI?
This NPC was missing something. That made him seem all the more dangerous.
I kept my mouth shut. Jin Wikyung’s face twisted as he spoke.
“...Please choose your words carefully. They are members of our family.”
“No. Those children are casualties of war. Countless more will die from now on. Perhaps even at this very moment.”
“Head Elder. I told you to watch your words.”
Jin Wikyung growled. Had we been alone, he would have been ready to start something right then and there.
But the Head Elder remained calm.
“Did you not anticipate this?”
He had suddenly switched to informal speech, yet it came so naturally that neither Jin Wikyung nor I even registered the change.

“Saneum, Eung-hyeon, Sakju. All three lay within the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s reach. When you sent messenger pigeons to each branch the day before, did you truly never consider that something like this might happen?”
“That...”
“You knew harm would come to them. Sending those pigeons was nothing more than a way to ease your conscience.”
“Enough. Please, enough.”

“It was an excellent decision. If you had tried to save the branches, you would have had to run for seven days and nights without rest, then fight the enemy while utterly exhausted. Isn’t that right?”
Jin Wikyung stared at the Head Elder with a pale face. Fresh blood flowed between his tightly clenched fingers.
“Everything comes with a sacrifice. Look at the bigger picture. You are the Lesser Family Head responsible for the hundreds of family members of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
Jin Wikyung’s body trembled. The anger and sorrow drained from his face, leaving behind a strange emptiness.
“Sacrifice...”
“The war has only just begun. Isn’t that so, Lesser Family Head?”
The Head Elder offered a fist-and-palm salute. I bit down hard on my lip.
What an impossible old man to figure out.
The Head Elder was clearly dangerous. His position in the family, his utterly unreadable motives, even the psychopathic way he could look at the corpses of children without twitching an eyebrow...
But...
He’s right.
From my perspective, Jin Wikyung was a good Lesser Family Head. He was deeply humane and sharp-minded.
But the moment he saw the corpses, he had been shaken more than anyone. Without the Head Elder’s cold rebuke, it would have taken him a long time to regain his composure.
He helped him. The Head Elder, of all people...
Are they enemies in peacetime but united during war?
If so, that’s a relief.
I was looking at the Head Elder with a mixture of suspicion and relief when he spoke.
“So the Third Young Master is here as well.”
My heart dropped at the sight of those shrewd gray eyes. It was the first time the Head Elder had spoken to me.
“Greetings, Head Elder.”
I did my best to hide my surprise, but the Head Elder regarded me with a strange smile.
“I’ve been hearing an interesting rumor within the family lately. Something about... the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
I never expected to hear that ridiculous nickname from the Head Elder.
“I’ve also heard that you are acquainted with Yama Whip. They say you joined forces with him to defeat the Heavenly Axe.”
“Cough. Cough.”
“Are you ill?”
“N-no. I’m just feeling a little chilly.”
“Oh dear. That won’t do for someone who is about to accomplish great things.”
My awkward smile slowly froze.
“What do you mean?”
“Someone capable of helping eliminate a formidable fiend like the Heavenly Axe is a valuable asset in battle. Surely that rumor isn’t false.”
“Therefore, as a direct-line member of our family, I believe it is only natural that you fight at the forefront. What do you think, Lesser Family Head?”
The Head Elder smiled faintly. Jin Wikyung stared at that smile for a moment, then asked me, “What do you think?”
Checkmate.
The moment the word came to mind, a familiar notification rang out.
Ding.

System Quest Mission You have been appointed captain of a White Tiger Hall reconnaissance squad. From now on, lead the subordinates assigned to you on missions and build merit! Grade: Repeatable Quest Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Earn 100 Merit Points (0 / 100) Reward: Changes according to the degree of success. Failure: Changes according to the degree of failure.
I closed the Quest Window. I had already seen it several times, and besides, the White Tiger Hall martial artist who had stepped away earlier had just returned.
“These are the supplies issued to captains.”
A sword.
A black martial uniform with a crude white tiger embroidered on it.
And a smooth wooden plaque that smelled strongly of fresh wood.
That was everything.
“The newly assigned members are waiting at the reconnaissance squad’s quarters. The location is...”
Fortunately, I knew the place. A pavilion I had passed several times had been assigned as the reconnaissance squad’s quarters.
After leaving White Tiger Hall, I first ducked into an empty alley.
Open Inventory.
Ten seconds was enough to put on the entire uniform. I changed clothes, shoved the sword deep into my Inventory, then pulled out the Sharp Spear.
Until now, I had thoroughly enjoyed the privileges of being the Third Young Master in a lavish private pavilion.
But things were different from here on out.
It’s communal living, right?
We would eat together and sleep together. I couldn’t exactly perform the magic trick of making a two-meter iron spear pop out of thin air whenever I needed it.
Once I hung the wooden plaque engraved with Captain at my waist, I felt like I’d become Ordinary Martial Artist #1 of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Not just an ordinary martial artist. I’m a reconnaissance squad captain.
Captain of a White Tiger Hall reconnaissance squad.
I had never expected to receive a position like this.
Of course, there had been some fierce disagreement over it. The Head Elder wanted to place me in a combat unit aligned with the Council of Elders, while Jin Wikyung had vehemently opposed him.
In the end, they compromised.
I would serve as a reconnaissance captain, a position whose duties were not especially difficult—but under the command of the White Tiger Hall Master, who belonged to the Council of Elders’ faction.
Before I knew what was happening, the position was mine.
I never imagined this was how I’d get dragged into the war.
I could have just told them to do whatever the hell they wanted, but I held back. The first reason was the Head Elder’s eyes, which flashed every time Yama Whip was mentioned.
The second reason was...
The children.
It’s a game. It’s all graphics, nothing more than an illusion.
No matter how many times I repeated that to myself, the corpses and the character carved into their foreheads kept flickering before my eyes.
Part of my decision had been emotional.
This wasn’t good.
Don’t get too invested. I can’t confuse reality with the game.

Things like this had been happening more and more often lately. At first, I had treated the NPCs like people for fun. But these days, I was actually thinking of them as real people and forming relationships with them.
Every time I caught myself doing it, I was startled.
Maybe it was a side effect of playing the game for too long.
“Is this it?”
Before I knew it, I had reached the reconnaissance squad’s quarters. My mouth fell open.
Cracked wood and a musty smell.
Good lord, there was even a beehive under the eaves. I had never seen one that big before.
Just like a company that treats you like family...
Look at those benefits.
Or maybe this was a mean-spirited prank by the White Tiger Hall Master, who disliked me. Perhaps he couldn’t openly give me grief yet, so this was his way of telling me to eat shit.
All right. Let’s give it a shot.
I took a deep breath, opened the door, and stepped inside.
Creeeak.
The old floor wailed beneath my foot, the sound especially ominous.

chapters.title: Chapter 22
paragraphs: The smell of mold hit me the moment I stepped into the room. The place reminded me of an army barracks, and the members of the reconnaissance squad were waiting inside.
Ten people.
I activated Qi Sense and looked them over.
As my gaze passed from one unfamiliar face to the next, Level displays popped into view.
Level 14. Level 15. Level 14...
Most of them were around the same level. Then I reached the ninth man.
System Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin
The number jumped sharply. His face was familiar, too.
Hyuk Mujin?
It was the same Hyuk Mujin who had picked a fight with me when I first arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan a few days ago. When our eyes met, his lips curled into a smirk.
“What a pleasure to see you again, Third. Young. Master.”
I stared at his openly hostile smile.
“From now on, call me Squad Leader.”
“...As you wish.”
Ignoring Hyuk Mujin’s piercing stare, I turned to the tenth member of the reconnaissance squad. The young man who had been beaming ever since I arrived shot to his feet.
“Young Master—no, Squad Leader! I look forward to serving under you.”
System Lv. 13 Han Yeop

It seemed the war had forced some people into new assignments. The White Tiger Hall clerk I’d met earlier had said the reconnaissance squads were made up of martial artists drawn from several different posts.
Hyuk Mujin originally belonged to the Gate Guard Pavilion, too.
Maybe that was why the atmosphere in the room felt so unsettled.
The squad members watched me with a mixture of awkwardness toward the strangers around them, anxiety about the war, and a hint of anticipation.
I spoke first.
“I’m Jin Taekyung, the newly appointed leader of this White Tiger Hall reconnaissance squad. I look forward to working with you.”
Clap, clap, clap.
Someone’s lonely applause died out within a few seconds, and Han Yeop lowered his hand with an embarrassed expression.
The atmosphere was even stiffer than I’d expected.
But that’s not necessarily a bad thing.
We were at war. It was better for them to stay tense than to laugh and socialize like we were all here to make friends.
Of course, too much tension could become poisonous. Easing it at the right time was also part of my job as squad leader.
That much, I’m used to.

Newbie Hunters froze the moment they entered a Gate for the first time. Real combat was different from practice. Everything they had learned and trained for at the Hunter training center flew off into outer space, and they were overwhelmed by the primal scent of death.
That was why Guild veterans helped the rookies keep their heads together. I’d been one of those veterans.
Though I was assigned exclusively to F-ranks.
The power levels were similar, too. From what I’d seen, a second-rate martial artist in Murim fell somewhere between an E-rank and an F-rank Hunter.
In other words, I was now leading a ten-man F-rank party. I’d never actually been a party leader, but I’d watched other people do the job until I was sick of it.
“Anyone with combat experience, raise your hand.”
At the abrupt question, every member of the reconnaissance squad raised a hand. They all looked confused.
“Keep it raised if you’ve fought at least five times.”
Half the hands went down. Han Yeop’s was among them.
Five people with experience in at least five battles. That wasn’t bad. In fact, it was better than I’d expected.
But the most important question remained.
“Keep it raised if you’ve killed someone.”
Four hands dropped weakly. I looked at the only member of the reconnaissance squad who still had his hand raised.
System Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin
“How many?”
He snorted.
“Five. It was during last year’s bandit suppression campaign. One of them was a Deputy Stronghold Lord. He was a pretty strong bastard—”
I cut him off before he could continue.
“Good. You’re the deputy squad leader from now on.”
Hyuk Mujin’s mouth, which had been preparing to ramble on, snapped shut.
“Deputy squad leader?”
“Yeah. Speak up now if you don’t like it.”
In a group full of rookies, experience mattered more than anything.
Hyuk Mujin was the only one who could swing a weapon at the enemy without hesitation.
Black cat, white cat.
White cat, black cat, even an ill-mannered cat—it didn’t matter as long as it caught mice.
Hyuk Mujin considered it with a conflicted expression before answering.
“...Hmph. If it’s an order, I suppose I have no choice.”
He sure had a difficult way of saying he wanted to be deputy squad leader.
“Then Hyuk Mujin is the deputy squad leader. From now on, you’re Number One.”
“Number One? What’s that supposed to mean?”
“It’s your designation. From now on, everyone in the reconnaissance squad goes by number instead of name. Hyuk Mujin is Number One. Next, you sitting over there. Yes, you. You’re Number Two.”
I went around the room, assigning everyone a number from One to Ten.
Hyuk Mujin frowned.
“Why are you doing this?”
“Because it’s convenient. We might end up fighting today. Do you want to spend the whole day memorizing names?”
“That’s—”
“Then do as you’re told. It’s an order.”
Hyuk Mujin glared at me, his expression rigid, but I didn’t look away.
Part of me even hoped he would act as insolent as he had the last time. We could end up in battle within a few days, and his current attitude would be a problem.
If he challenged me, I would have to show him the difference in our strength.
Clearly.
“...I’ll follow your orders.”
“What was that?”
“Number One. I said I’m Number One.”
His voice trembled as he answered. He was more perceptive than I’d expected. Maybe it had something to do with the rumors about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
What mattered was that Hyuk Mujin had fallen in line.
Keeping my expression neutral, I continued.
“What I’m about to say may sound strange and unfamiliar. But bear with it. It’s better than getting stabbed to death, isn’t it? Don’t you agree?”
The other squad members weren’t as open about their displeasure as Hyuk Mujin, but they still watched me anxiously.
All except one.
“I’ll do whatever the Squad Leader says!”
Han Yeop shouted like a fangirl. The only difference was that he had a spear in his hand instead of an idol light stick.
Oh, right.
I grinned at the squad.
“Now, anyone who uses a sword, raise your hand.”
The core of party hunting was assigning positions.
Raid tactics in the real world had been standardized into manuals long ago.
Three tanks. Four damage dealers. Two mages and one healer. For a ten-person party, that was the ideal combination.
Obviously, there aren’t any mages or healers here.
I had to balance the party as well as I could using only tanks and damage dealers, but—
“...You’re telling me no one knows how to use a shield?”
My voice trembled at the horrifying discovery.
Good lord. I had ten damage dealers. Nine used swords, and Han Yeop was the only one with a spear.
What kind of horrifying monoculture is this?
A mixed breed would be better. At least that would have a little of everything.
Hyuk Mujin looked as if he couldn’t understand what the problem was.
“A man ought to wield a sword.”
The sight of everyone else nodding along left me speechless.
You’re too well-fed. Way too well-fed.
Try slamming your head into a pool of blood and see if you still talk like that.
Sword? Spear? There was no such distinction. You bashed people with whatever rock you happened to grab, threw dirt, climbed on top of them, and bit them with your teeth.
When your life was on the line, anything within reach became both a weapon and a lifeline.
These people, who had only ever fought bandits at best, still didn’t understand that.
Do I need to start training them tomorrow?
Not for their sake. For my own survival.
Even teaching them a few tricks would make a real difference in a melee.
I worked like a dog for seven years. I’m not dying because of a bunch of rookies.
That was when it happened.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
A large bell tolled three times.
Since individuals here had no way to tell the exact time, bells rang at set hours. The three tolls marked Mi-si, roughly one to three in the afternoon.
And—
“Get ready. This is our first deployment.”
They also signaled the reconnaissance squad’s first mission.
“He should be doing fine.”
Jin Wikyung looked up at Wipeng’s abrupt comment. Until that moment, he had been staring blankly at a cooling cup of tea.
“What are you talking about?”
“The Third Young Master.”
A full day had passed since the reconnaissance squad led by Jin Taekyung departed from the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Their mission was to scout the nearby county towns.
“They left around noon yesterday, so they should arrive within two days.”
“Ah. Taekyung.”
Jin Wikyung gave a weary chuckle.
“I wondered what you meant. Never mind.”
“Never mind?”
“How long are you going to treat him like a child? He’s a grown man now. I’m sure he’ll manage on his own.”
“...I’m beginning to doubt my ears.”
“I did coddle him quite a bit. He was much younger back then.”
“I agree, to some extent. He’s changed considerably in the past few days.”
“Heroes grow by overcoming adversity.”
“Anyway, I can stop worrying about the youngest now. I’ll be able to focus more on the main family.”
“You should rest for a while. You look exhausted.”
“Wipeng. Members of our family have died.”
Sorrow and resolve weighed on his voice. Wipeng fell silent, and Jin Wikyung returned to his work.
But the silence lasted only two hours.
“What is that...?”
A black speck in the sky drew closer. Spreading its enormous wings, a messenger eagle landed on the office windowsill.
It belonged to the Lower District Sect.
Jin Wikyung sprang to his feet and opened the tube fastened to the eagle’s leg. When he unfolded the letter, he found a message written in tiny characters.
Jopil, One Question, One Kill, has appeared in Jeongyang with a special detachment of twenty men.
“Jeongyang...!”
Beyond Jeongyang lay Honju. Beyond Honju lay Taiyuan. Special detachment or not, he hadn’t expected them to cover hundreds of li in only a few days.
And that wasn’t all.
There were still family members from the branches who had not returned to the main family. What if the enemy was tracking them?
Every moment counts.
It didn’t take Jin Wikyung long to decide.
“Select fifty martial artists immediately and send them to Jeongyang. One Question, One Kill Jopil is a brutal Peak master. Bring our family members—”
The children came to mind.
Their small limbs. Their faces twisted in pain. Their vacant eyes.
Jin Wikyung clenched his teeth.
“Bring our family members home safely.”
“My lord.”
Wipeng’s expression had hardened. Jin Wikyung stared blankly at him, as though a thought had seized him, before speaking.
“Taekyung. Where did you say Taekyung went?”
His voice came out strained.
“...Jeongyang.”

sentences.text: The smell of mold hit me the moment I stepped into the room.
The place reminded me of an army barracks, and the members of the reconnaissance squad were waiting inside.
Ten people.
I activated Qi Sense and looked them over.
As my gaze passed from one unfamiliar face to the next, Level displays popped into view.
Level 14.
Level 15.
Level 14...
Most of them were around the same level.
Then I reached the ninth man.
System Lv.
22 Hyuk Mujin
The number jumped sharply.
His face was familiar, too.
Hyuk Mujin?
It was the same Hyuk Mujin who had picked a fight with me when I first arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan a few days ago.
When our eyes met, his lips curled into a smirk.
“What a pleasure to see you again, Third.
Young.
Master.”
I stared at his openly hostile smile.
“From now on, call me Squad Leader.”
“...As you wish.”
Ignoring Hyuk Mujin’s piercing stare, I turned to the tenth member of the reconnaissance squad.
The young man who had been beaming ever since I arrived shot to his feet.
“Young Master—no, Squad Leader!
I look forward to serving under you.”
System Lv.
13 Han Yeop
It seemed the war had forced some people into new assignments.
The White Tiger Hall clerk I’d met earlier had said the reconnaissance squads were made up of martial artists drawn from several different posts.
Hyuk Mujin originally belonged to the Gate Guard Pavilion, too.
Maybe that was why the atmosphere in the room felt so unsettled.
The squad members watched me with a mixture of awkwardness toward the strangers around them, anxiety about the war, and a hint of anticipation.
I spoke first.
“I’m Jin Taekyung, the newly appointed leader of this White Tiger Hall reconnaissance squad.
I look forward to working with you.”
Clap, clap, clap.
Someone’s lonely applause died out within a few seconds, and Han Yeop lowered his hand with an embarrassed expression.
The atmosphere was even stiffer than I’d expected.
But that’s not necessarily a bad thing.
We were at war.
It was better for them to stay tense than to laugh and socialize like we were all here to make friends.
Of course, too much tension could become poisonous.
Easing it at the right time was also part of my job as squad leader.
That much, I’m used to.
Newbie Hunters froze the moment they entered a Gate for the first time.
Real combat was different from practice.
Everything they had learned and trained for at the Hunter training center flew off into outer space, and they were overwhelmed by the primal scent of death.
That was why Guild veterans helped the rookies keep their heads together.
I’d been one of those veterans.
Though I was assigned exclusively to F-ranks.
The power levels were similar, too.
From what I’d seen, a second-rate martial artist in Murim fell somewhere between an E-rank and an F-rank Hunter.
In other words, I was now leading a ten-man F-rank party.
I’d never actually been a party leader, but I’d watched other people do the job until I was sick of it.
“Anyone with combat experience, raise your hand.”
At the abrupt question, every member of the reconnaissance squad raised a hand.
They all looked confused.
“Keep it raised if you’ve fought at least five times.”
Half the hands went down.
Han Yeop’s was among them.
Five people with experience in at least five battles.
That wasn’t bad.
In fact, it was better than I’d expected.
But the most important question remained.
“Keep it raised if you’ve killed someone.”
Four hands dropped weakly.
I looked at the only member of the reconnaissance squad who still had his hand raised.
System Lv.
22 Hyuk Mujin
“How many?”
He snorted.
“Five.
It was during last year’s bandit suppression campaign.
One of them was a Deputy Stronghold Lord.
He was a pretty strong bastard—”
I cut him off before he could continue.
“Good.
You’re the deputy squad leader from now on.”
Hyuk Mujin’s mouth, which had been preparing to ramble on, snapped shut.
“Deputy squad leader?”
“Yeah.
Speak up now if you don’t like it.”
In a group full of rookies, experience mattered more than anything.
Hyuk Mujin was the only one who could swing a weapon at the enemy without hesitation.
Black cat, white cat.
White cat, black cat, even an ill-mannered cat—it didn’t matter as long as it caught mice.
Hyuk Mujin considered it with a conflicted expression before answering.
“...Hmph.
If it’s an order, I suppose I have no choice.”
He sure had a difficult way of saying he wanted to be deputy squad leader.
“Then Hyuk Mujin is the deputy squad leader.
From now on, you’re Number One.”
“Number One?
What’s that supposed to mean?”
“It’s your designation.
From now on, everyone in the reconnaissance squad goes by number instead of name.
Hyuk Mujin is Number One.
Next, you sitting over there.
Yes, you.
You’re Number Two.”
I went around the room, assigning everyone a number from One to Ten.
Hyuk Mujin frowned.
“Why are you doing this?”
“Because it’s convenient.
We might end up fighting today.
Do you want to spend the whole day memorizing names?”
“That’s—”
“Then do as you’re told.
It’s an order.”
Hyuk Mujin glared at me, his expression rigid, but I didn’t look away.
Part of me even hoped he would act as insolent as he had the last time.
We could end up in battle within a few days, and his current attitude would be a problem.
If he challenged me, I would have to show him the difference in our strength.
Clearly.
“...I’ll follow your orders.”
“What was that?”
“Number One.
I said I’m Number One.”
His voice trembled as he answered.
He was more perceptive than I’d expected.
Maybe it had something to do with the rumors about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
What mattered was that Hyuk Mujin had fallen in line.
Keeping my expression neutral, I continued.
“What I’m about to say may sound strange and unfamiliar.
But bear with it.
It’s better than getting stabbed to death, isn’t it?
Don’t you agree?”
The other squad members weren’t as open about their displeasure as Hyuk Mujin, but they still watched me anxiously.
All except one.
“I’ll do whatever the Squad Leader says!”
Han Yeop shouted like a fangirl.
The only difference was that he had a spear in his hand instead of an idol light stick.
Oh, right.
I grinned at the squad.
“Now, anyone who uses a sword, raise your hand.”
The core of party hunting was assigning positions.
Raid tactics in the real world had been standardized into manuals long ago.
Three tanks.
Four damage dealers.
Two mages and one healer.
For a ten-person party, that was the ideal combination.
Obviously, there aren’t any mages or healers here.
I had to balance the party as well as I could using only tanks and damage dealers, but—
“...You’re telling me no one knows how to use a shield?”
My voice trembled at the horrifying discovery.
Good lord.
I had ten damage dealers.

What kind of horrifying monoculture is this?
A mixed breed would be better.

Spear?

chapters.title: Chapter 23
paragraphs: The Jin Family of Taiyuan.
As its name suggests, its headquarters were in Taiyuan. But like a conglomerate in the real world, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s influence was not limited to a single city.
The family had been established two hundred years ago and had long since expanded its sphere of influence by setting up branches in county towns throughout Shanxi Province.
Scout the area near Jeongyang and return within five days.
That was the reconnaissance squad’s first mission. The squad members’ reactions to the order fell into two camps.
“Doesn’t sound like much.”
Some, like Hyuk Mujin, were disappointed. Others, like Han Yeop, sighed in relief.
Of course, neither reaction pleased me.
Hyuk Mujin was consumed by a pointless hunger for glory, while Han Yeop was afraid to fight.
Still, a safe mission is probably for the best.
The thought of running into the enemy with these guys was horrifying. I’d be safer fighting on the front lines with people I could trust.
Should I apply for a transfer?
Suppressing a sigh, I raised my fist. It was one of the hand signals I had taught them earlier. It meant stop.
Snort.
The eleven horses trotting at a steady pace came to a halt with a chorus of snorts. Hyuk Mujin, riding to my right, spoke irritably.
“Why are we stopping?”
“Rest.”
“Again?”
“Two hours of travel, fifteen minutes of rest. Didn’t I tell you that already?”
“I can keep going!”
“Then go by yourself.”
I jerked my chin toward the rear. The other squad members were breathing hard. Traveling on horseback was faster than going on foot, but it also consumed a considerable amount of stamina.
Hyuk Mujin’s much higher Level allowed him to hold up fairly well, but fatigue was building in the others.
“When I tell you to rest, you rest. That’s an order.”
Ignoring Hyuk Mujin’s scowl, I addressed the squad.
“Fifteen minutes of rest.”
They had been given fifteen minutes to rest, but the reconnaissance squad members didn’t look particularly happy. That was because I immediately pulled out a large leather backpack.
I reached inside and thought,
Open Inventory.
With a clatter, three shields materialized inside the backpack.
They were wooden shields plated with iron, taken from the armory before we left the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Light and sturdy, they were perfectly serviceable.
“Number Seven. Number Eight. Number Nine.”
The three designated squad members accepted the shields with doomed expressions.
They were the tanks I had selected by force.
Seven damage dealers. Three tanks. And me.
It was a party composition that would be wiped out the moment it entered a Gate, but for now, I had to make do.
“Everyone to your positions.”
Next came formation drills.
“Basic formation.”
The three shield bearers formed the front line. Six swordsmen, from Number One Hyuk Mujin through Number Six, made up the second. Han Yeop and I took the rear.
It was a formation focused on threats from the front.
“Spread out. Scatter and assemble. Disperse.”
Their faces were still full of complaints, but by now they followed the commands with reasonable skill. They were much better than F-rank Hunters fresh out of a Hunter training center.
These NPCs are better than real people.
The difference probably came down to whether they could use internal energy.
Unlike F-rank Hunters, who couldn’t manipulate mana at all, Murim’s NPCs could use internal energy, however faintly.
They were simply low-Level and inexperienced.
I moved on to the final stage of formation training.
“All-out retreat.”
The reconnaissance squad members hesitated.
“What?”
“What does ‘all-out retreat’ mean?”
“Exactly what it sounds like. Retreat with everything you’ve got.”
“Then what formation should we—?”
“If it comes to that, formation won’t matter. Just run as fast as you can. Don’t look back, and scatter as widely as possible.”
“Heh. You call that an order?”
The mocking voice belonged, naturally, to Hyuk Mujin.
“I can’t stand this anymore. Third Young Master, do you think war is some children’s game? If you want to make nonsense sound convincing, you should at least read a military strategy manual first.”
“A military strategy manual?”
“Yes, a military strategy manual! Retreating in good order is one of the most basic principles of warfare. What kind of nonsense are you spouting?”
Hyuk Mujin’s open defiance drew hesitant murmurs from the other squad members.
“He’s not wrong.”
“We aren’t government troops. Why are we drilling formations and being forced to carry shields...?”
“I’ve never even heard of an all-out retreat.”
See? Everyone agrees with me.
That was what Hyuk Mujin’s smug face seemed to say.
Then Han Yeop cut in, his voice wavering.
“I-I don’t agree.”
“What?”
“The Third Young Master—I mean, the Captain—must have a reason for doing this... right?”
“A reason?”
Hyuk Mujin glared at him.

“What reason could there be? The Third Young Master spent his youth drinking with women instead of training. He caused every kind of trouble despite being like that. And that’s not all. He was also the one who caused this war—”
“Enough.”
Hyuk Mujin flinched when I cut him off. He seemed to realize that he had misspoken.
But some people were like that. When they needed to back down, they took another step forward instead.
“Wasn’t the Third Young Master the one who caused this war?”
Hyuk Mujin was too proud to stop himself.
Once the words were out, a chilly silence descended.
Gulp.
Someone’s throat bobbed loudly. Nine pairs of eyes turned toward Hyuk Mujin and me.
“D-do you have something to say?”
Something to say? Of course I did.
“Everyone gets another fifteen minutes of rest.”
At the same time, I slapped Hyuk Mujin across the face with an open palm.
Smack!
“One.”
His jaw twisted to the side. It was an ordinary slap, without even a trace of internal energy. His face was still dazed by the sudden turn of events when I struck him a second time.
“What the—!”
He wasn’t completely helpless, at least. He raised an arm to block.
What he had failed to account for was the difference in our strength.
Smack!
“Two.”
Hyuk Mujin’s upper body slammed into the ground. He sprang back up, my palm print stamped on one cheek like a tattoo.
It didn’t take long for his bewilderment to turn into rage.
“You fucking bastard!”
He was properly furious now. As he charged at me, eyes bulging, I hooked his leg and sent him sprawling. At the same time, I put some strength into my left hand and struck him.
Smack.
“Three.”
“Urgh.”
His legs nearly gave out, and he staggered. Three consecutive blows with that much force were bound to rattle his brain.
“What, are you saving your internal energy to make soup?”
That got through to him. Strength returned to his wavering legs, and internal energy surged through his body. He glared at me with venomous eyes.
“You’ll regret this.”
“I doubt it.”
I caught the fist flying toward my face.
Speed, strength, timing.
I could see it all. Compared to Lee Seogeun, Hyuk Mujin was nowhere close.
“Four.”
His head snapped back. Thick droplets of blood sprayed through the air in slow motion. His pupils had lost focus, and his legs hung limp.
Yet somehow, he didn’t fall. He couldn’t—not unless I let go of his fist.
“Five.”
Smack!
That was his limit. Hyuk Mujin finally lost consciousness. As he sprawled on the ground in a bizarre pose, something landed on his body with a soft patter.
Snow?
I looked up. The winter sky was showering us with tiny white scraps of garbage.
“Break’s over. We’re leaving.”
I tossed out the words and turned away. Behind me, the reconnaissance squad members finally released the breaths they had been holding.
When Hyuk Mujin woke two hours later, the first thing he did was charge at me.
“You fucking—!”
Smack. Thud.
“Move him.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
Another crisp slap knocked him out again, and the other squad members dragged him into a corner of the cabin.
A cabin. We got lucky.
According to one squad member who knew the surrounding area well, we should have reached Jeongyang before sunset at the latest.
But there was nothing we could do about the sudden blizzard, and this cabin was the only shelter we had managed to find.
Apparently, it was a hunters’ shelter known only to people familiar with the area.
It’s ridiculously small, but I’ll take it.
The mission might be delayed, but this was a hundred times better than trudging through the snow all night, collapsing from exhaustion, and then running into the enemy.
That was when—
“C-Captain.”
It was Han Yeop. Behind him, the other squad members stole glances at me, gauging my mood.
“What should we do now?”
“Hm? Sleep.”
“N-no, that’s not what I meant...”
Watching them fidget, a thought struck me.
Don’t tell me...
“Do you want to train?”
Nod, nod.
Look at those heads bobbing furiously. Look at those eyes burning with enthusiasm.
Seeing is believing, my ass. One beating beats a hundred explanations.
Beating them once really was better than explaining something a hundred times.
It was around noon.
Sunlight flashed off a sword blade. That was all the martial artist saw.
“Urgh.”
Thud.
His knees buckled, and his face slammed into the frozen ground.
Blood poured from the gaping wound running from his shoulder to his chest. It was beyond recovery. The martial artist knew he was going to die.
“The others... Please, let them live.”
His fading voice cut off abruptly. A middle-aged man clicked his tongue as he stared into the martial artist’s wide-open eyes.
“Good grief, you poor fool.”
How could he charge in like that without warning? The words that followed never reached the dead man. The fifty-odd wandering martial artists surrounding them snickered.
“Of all people, he had to run into the boss. Rotten luck.”
“Only an orthodox-faction bastard would keep playing the hero to the bitter end. What should we do, Boss?”
Their gleaming eyes turned toward the survivors, a group of six or seven women and children.
“Great Hero, please spare the children.”
At the plea from the oldest-looking woman, the middle-aged man—Jopil, One Question, One Kill—smiled gently.
“I’m sorry, but what can I do? I’m no Great Hero.”
“But you’re still human. How can you kill children who can’t even tell right from wrong?”
“Hah. You have quite a bit of spirit for a woman. Wait. I heard the Sakju Branch Leader’s family survived. Could you be...?”
“He is my husband.”
“Ah, I thought so. I never imagined such a pathetic man could have such a virtuous wife.”
Jopil smiled, and the woman’s expression hardened.
“You never intended to spare us.”
“Rest easy. Raping women before I kill them isn’t one of my hobbies.”
“The children...”
“This is a harsh world. How are little ones supposed to survive without their mother?”
“You’re worse than a beast.”
“Last words noted.”
That was the signal.
Swordlight flashed, and screams rang out.
A short while later, the blood-soaked wandering martial artists tossed the corpses into the mountain thickets.
“Only the wild animals will feast tonight.”
The man with the tiny birdlike eyes muttered. He was Jopil’s right-hand man, a first-rate wandering martial artist known by the nickname Black Mountain Blade.
“We should feast, too. If we finish this job properly, what’s a mere thousand pieces of gold?”
Jopil laughed in delight. The payment for this job would be enormous, but more than that, he was enjoying the situation itself.
“I never imagined the day would come when we’d hunt the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
His filthy leather shoe came down on the fallen martial artist’s corpse.
The martial artist had belonged to the Sakju Branch, one of the ten or so branches of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“Was that the last one?”
“No, Boss.”
“They slip away like rats. How many?”
“Three in total. One martial artist and two children. They passed through Jeongyang only a few hours ago and are headed for Honju.”
“That’s troublesome. It’ll take half a day.”
“There’s no need for you to go yourself. I’ll take care of it.”
“Will you?”
A pleased smile spread across Jopil’s lips.
“Good. Take half the men. You have half a day. How does that sound?”
There was only one possible answer. Black Mountain Blade bowed deeply.

Unlike F-rank Hunters, who couldn’t manipulate mana at all, Murim’s NPCs could use internal energy, however faintly.
They were simply low-Level and inexperienced.
I moved on to the final stage of formation training.
“All-out retreat.”
The reconnaissance squad members hesitated.
“What?”
“What does ‘all-out retreat’ mean?”
“Exactly what it sounds like.
Retreat with everything you’ve got.”
“Then what formation should we—?”
“If it comes to that, formation won’t matter.
Just run as fast as you can.
Don’t look back, and scatter as widely as possible.”
“Heh.
You call that an order?”
The mocking voice belonged, naturally, to Hyuk Mujin.
“I can’t stand this anymore.
Third Young Master, do you think war is some children’s game?
If you want to make nonsense sound convincing, you should at least read a military strategy manual first.”
“A military strategy manual?”
“Yes, a military strategy manual!
Retreating in good order is one of the most basic principles of warfare.
What kind of nonsense are you spouting?”
Hyuk Mujin’s open defiance drew hesitant murmurs from the other squad members.
“He’s not wrong.”
“We aren’t government troops.
Why are we drilling formations and being forced to carry shields...?”
“I’ve never even heard of an all-out retreat.”
See?
Everyone agrees with me.
That was what Hyuk Mujin’s smug face seemed to say.
Then Han Yeop cut in, his voice wavering.
“I-I don’t agree.”
“What?”
“The Third Young Master—I mean, the Captain—must have a reason for doing this... right?”
“A reason?”
Hyuk Mujin glared at him.
“What reason could there be?
The Third Young Master spent his youth drinking with women instead of training.
He caused every kind of trouble despite being like that.
And that’s not all.
He was also the one who caused this war—”
“Enough.”
Hyuk Mujin flinched when I cut him off.
He seemed to realize that he had misspoken.
But some people were like that.
When they needed to back down, they took another step forward instead.
“Wasn’t the Third Young Master the one who caused this war?”
Hyuk Mujin was too proud to stop himself.
Once the words were out, a chilly silence descended.
Gulp.
Someone’s throat bobbed loudly.
Nine pairs of eyes turned toward Hyuk Mujin and me.
“D-do you have something to say?”
Something to say?
Of course I did.
“Everyone gets another fifteen minutes of rest.”
At the same time, I slapped Hyuk Mujin across the face with an open palm.
Smack!
“One.”
His jaw twisted to the side.
It was an ordinary slap, without even a trace of internal energy.
His face was still dazed by the sudden turn of events when I struck him a second time.
“What the—!”
He wasn’t completely helpless, at least.
He raised an arm to block.
What he had failed to account for was the difference in our strength.
Smack!
“Two.”
Hyuk Mujin’s upper body slammed into the ground.
He sprang back up, my palm print stamped on one cheek like a tattoo.
It didn’t take long for his bewilderment to turn into rage.
“You fucking bastard!”
He was properly furious now.
As he charged at me, eyes bulging, I hooked his leg and sent him sprawling.
At the same time, I put some strength into my left hand and struck him.
Smack.
“Three.”
“Urgh.”
His legs nearly gave out, and he staggered.
Three consecutive blows with that much force were bound to rattle his brain.
“What, are you saving your internal energy to make soup?”
That got through to him.
Strength returned to his wavering legs, and internal energy surged through his body.
He glared at me with venomous eyes.
“You’ll regret this.”
“I doubt it.”
I caught the fist flying toward my face.
Speed, strength, timing.
I could see it all.
Compared to Lee Seogeun, Hyuk Mujin was nowhere close.
“Four.”
His head snapped back.
Thick droplets of blood sprayed through the air in slow motion.
His pupils had lost focus, and his legs hung limp.
Yet somehow, he didn’t fall.
He couldn’t—not unless I let go of his fist.
“Five.”
Smack!
That was his limit.
Hyuk Mujin finally lost consciousness.
As he sprawled on the ground in a bizarre pose, something landed on his body with a soft patter.
Snow?
I looked up.
The winter sky was showering us with tiny white scraps of garbage.
“Break’s over.
We’re leaving.”
I tossed out the words and turned away.
Behind me, the reconnaissance squad members finally released the breaths they had been holding.
When Hyuk Mujin woke two hours later, the first thing he did was charge at me.
“You fucking—!”
Smack.
Thud.
“Move him.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
Another crisp slap knocked him out again, and the other squad members dragged him into a corner of the cabin.
A cabin.
We got lucky.
According to one squad member who knew the surrounding area well, we should have reached Jeongyang before sunset at the latest.
But there was nothing we could do about the sudden blizzard, and this cabin was the only shelter we had managed to find.
Apparently, it was a hunters’ shelter known only to people familiar with the area.
It’s ridiculously small, but I’ll take it.
The mission might be delayed, but this was a hundred times better than trudging through the snow all night, collapsing from exhaustion, and then running into the enemy.
That was when—
“C-Captain.”
It was Han Yeop.
Behind him, the other squad members stole glances at me, gauging my mood.
“What should we do now?”
“Hm?
Sleep.”
“N-no, that’s not what I meant...”
Watching them fidget, a thought struck me.
Don’t tell me...
“Do you want to train?”
Nod, nod.
Look at those heads bobbing furiously.
Look at those eyes burning with enthusiasm.
Seeing is believing, my ass.
One beating beats a hundred explanations.
Beating them once really was better than explaining something a hundred times.
It was around noon.
Sunlight flashed off a sword blade.
That was all the martial artist saw.
“Urgh.”
Thud.
His knees buckled, and his face slammed into the frozen ground.
Blood poured from the gaping wound running from his shoulder to his chest.
It was beyond recovery.
The martial artist knew he was going to die.
“The others...
Please, let them live.”
His fading voice cut off abruptly.
A middle-aged man clicked his tongue as he stared into the martial artist’s wide-open eyes.
“Good grief, you poor fool.”
How could he charge in like that without warning?
The words that followed never reached the dead man.
The fifty-odd wandering martial artists surrounding them snickered.
“Of all people, he had to run into the boss.
Rotten luck.”
“Only an orthodox-faction bastard would keep playing the hero to the bitter end.
What should we do, Boss?”
Their gleaming eyes turned toward the survivors, a group of six or seven women and children.
“Great Hero, please spare the children.”
At the plea from the oldest-looking woman, the middle-aged man—Jopil, One Question, One Kill—smiled gently.
“I’m sorry, but what can I do?
I’m no Great Hero.”
“But you’re still human.
How can you kill children who can’t even tell right from wrong?”
“Hah.
You have quite a bit of spirit for a woman.
Wait.
I heard the Sakju Branch Leader’s family survived.
Could you be...?”
“He is my husband.”
“Ah, I thought so.
I never imagined such a pathetic man could have such a virtuous wife.”
Jopil smiled, and the woman’s expression hardened.
“You never intended to spare us.”
“Rest easy.
Raping women before I kill them isn’t one of my hobbies.”
“The children...”
“This is a harsh world.
How are little ones supposed to survive without their mother?”
“You’re worse than a beast.”
“Last words noted.”
That was the signal.
Swordlight flashed, and screams rang out.
A short while later, the blood-soaked wandering martial artists tossed the corpses into the mountain thickets.
“Only the wild animals will feast tonight.”
The man with the tiny birdlike eyes muttered.
He was Jopil’s right-hand man, a first-rate wandering martial artist known by the nickname Black Mountain Blade.
“We should feast, too.
If we finish this job properly, what’s a mere thousand pieces of gold?”
Jopil laughed in delight.
The payment for this job would be enormous, but more than that, he was enjoying the situation itself.
“I never imagined the day would come when we’d hunt the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
His filthy leather shoe came down on the fallen martial artist’s corpse.
The martial artist had belonged to the Sakju Branch, one of the ten or so branches of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“Was that the last one?”
“No, Boss.”
“They slip away like rats.
How many?”
“Three in total.
One martial artist and two children.
They passed through Jeongyang only a few hours ago and are headed for Honju.”
“That’s troublesome.
It’ll take half a day.”
“There’s no need for you to go yourself.
I’ll take care of it.”
“Will you?”
A pleased smile spread across Jopil’s lips.
“Good.
Take half the men.
You have half a day.
How does that sound?”
There was only one possible answer.
Black Mountain Blade bowed deeply.

chapters.title: Chapter 24
paragraphs: He ran. It was the only thing he could do.
Even as his father and the people of the Sakju Branch—people who had been like family to him—died one after another, there was only one thing a fourteen-year-old boy could do.
Run.
“Oppa, I’m cold.”
His little sister whimpered in his arms. The boy, Socheon, blew warm breath over her hands, stiff with cold.
“We’re almost there. Just hold on a little longer, okay?”
“When are we going home? Soyul wants to see Mom...”
“She came yesterday, too.”
“You’re lying. Did you see her?”
“Of course I did.”
In my dream.
Socheon swallowed the rest of the sentence.

His mother had appeared in his dream the night before, exactly as she had three days earlier. She had spent a long time stroking and gazing at Soyul, who had fallen asleep from exhaustion, before speaking.
“Survive. You must survive.”
Her voice still rang in his ears, and the sight of her back as she led the others away still hovered before his eyes.
What happened to Mother? Could she have...? No. That can’t be.
It was then, as he struggled to suppress his ominous feelings, that he heard something.
Rustle.
“Who’s there?”
The motion came naturally. He pulled his little sister close and drew the dagger concealed inside his clothes.
After the night his home had burned and he had witnessed countless deaths, the once-cheerful boy had acquired the eyes of a wild beast.
“I’ll count to three. One, two...”
“It’s me.”
The dagger slowly lowered when a face suddenly appeared from the darkness.
“Uncle Gong?”
“Shh. Keep your voice down.”
Uncle Gong was a weary-looking middle-aged man. An old friend of Socheon’s father, the Branch Leader of the Sakju Branch, he was now the young siblings’ guide and protector.
“I was worried. You were gone for more than half a shichen.”
“I should have been more careful. We have a tail.”
“Already?”
“Yes. Every moment counts.”
Socheon rose without hesitation. Uncle Gong hoisted the bewildered Soyul onto his back and led the way through the brush.
“Where are we going?”
“Honju. No matter how vicious those bastards are, they won’t pursue us that far.”
Is that really true?
Socheon had his doubts.
The Sakju Branch had already fallen. The building had burned, and everyone was dead. He did not know who the attackers were, but their purpose was clear.
Extermination.
He blew the word away with his breath and started walking again.
How long had they been walking?
The white snow that had fluttered down like sleet was already up to their calves when—
“Quiet.”
Uncle Gong stopped. Socheon held his breath.
The howling wind. Bare branches clattering against one another...
Nothing else.
Yet Socheon knew instinctively.
“Is it them?”
Uncle Gong’s face went rigid.
“At least ten of them. They’ll catch up soon.”
The situation was bleak. Yet strangely, Socheon’s heart settled into a calm stillness.
“This is my fault. I should have hurried before the snow began... I curse the heavens.”
“You did everything you could, Uncle.”
Socheon drew the dagger from inside his clothes. It had been handed down to him by his father a year ago—the only trace his father had left behind.
“I’ve learned a little martial arts myself. I’ll fight and die like a martial artist.”
“...It’s too soon to give up.”
That was all Uncle Gong could say. They drew on what little strength they had left and set off again.
But their stamina, pushed to its limit by days and nights of nonstop flight, dragged at their feet. Their steps grew slower, and their breathing became labored.
“There they are!”
“We’ve almost caught them!”
Now Socheon could hear them, too. The pursuers’ voices and the glow of their torches were drawing closer.
At that moment, Uncle Gong handed the soundly sleeping Soyul to Socheon.
“I’ll follow behind you.”
“Uncle!”
“Don’t worry. I, Gong Yacheong, am not so easily dealt with.”
“But how can you...”
“Go!”
Socheon left Gong Yacheong behind and started up the mountain again. His stamina was at its limit, but he did not stop.
When he reached a hill on the snow-covered mountain, the clash of weapons and someone’s scream rang out.
Uncle Gong.
Socheon gritted his teeth. He wanted to draw his dagger and throw himself down the slope that very instant.
But...
Hold on. I have to hold on.
He had repeated those words hundreds, thousands of times over the past five days. He had sworn to survive, protect the little sister in his arms, and take revenge on the murderers.
From the hilltop, Socheon stared at the flickering torches with fire blazing in his eyes.
I will survive.
Then he turned and climbed over the hill.
The next moment, his body shook as if struck by lightning.
Ten men in navy martial uniforms stood in the broad clearing atop the hill, staring at him.
A single character had been embroidered prominently across each man’s chest in silk thread.
陳.
Jin.
I sensed something strange just as we were about to begin training.
A sound carried faintly through the howling wind. When I drew up my internal energy, it became clearer.
A human voice?
There had to be more than ten people. They were so close, I couldn’t believe I had only just noticed them.
That many people in this weather...
All right. Decision made.
“Pack your things.”
“Huh?”
The squad members had been standing ready with their weapons, but now they stared at me in confusion.
“Pack up, quickly. One of you, go inside and get Hyuk Mujin—”
“Captain. There’s a kid over there.”
Damn it. There really was one.
A little boy carrying an even smaller child on his back was staring blankly at us.
“Who’s that?”
“No idea. Does he own this cabin?”
Please let that be it.
But why did I find it so hard to believe that the men following him were members of one big, happy family?
“He’s crying.”
As someone had pointed out, the boy was crying. Sobbing his heart out as he ran.
The problem was the direction he was running in.
“Uh, he’s coming this way... Captain, where are you going?”
Suspicious gazes turned toward me. I had already backed well away from them.
“I’m going to ride a horse. We should be leaving soon.”
“In this weather? The horses won’t even be able to move.”
“Really? Then we’ll leave them behind.”
“What?”
“That’s how missions work. Snow or rain, we still have a job to do. Shut up and pack your things.”
“But still...”
“Pack your things! Wake Hyuk Mujin!”
The admiring looks they had given me barely fifteen minutes ago had turned into the sort reserved for a lunatic.
“What’s gotten into you all of a sudden?”
What’s gotten into me?
I had a really bad feeling about this.
By now, I knew the signs. The closer the kid came, the stronger the stench of a giant fuck-you grew.
I could already see exactly how this would play out. There was only one way out.
“Then I’ll head down first by my—”
At that moment, our uninvited guests appeared over the hill amid a chorus of shouts.
More than twenty men.
Oh, fuck.
Ding.

System A Sudden Quest has been created! Quest Survivors of the Sakju Branch You have encountered survivors from the Sakju Branch of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Rescue the survivors from the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s merciless pursuers! Grade: Sudden Quest Limit: Jin Taekyung Task: Rescue the survivors — Incomplete Reward: Chain Quest ??? Failure: ???
We stared at them. They stared at us.
A deathly silence settled over the frozen clearing.
I knew it. I knew this was going to happen.
But it was too late for regrets. What could I do about my shitty luck?
I heaved a deep sigh and shouted.
“Attack formation! Form up!”
Clack-clack-clack.
Caught off guard, the squad members nevertheless moved as they had been taught. By the time they had formed up, the enemy had realized who we were and started shouting.
“They’re brats from the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
“There aren’t many of them! Wipe them out!”
Brats. Outnumbered.
Those two facts hit me right in the chest.
I hadn’t even finished teaching these guys. Their martial arts were weak, they had no real combat experience, and they were complete rookies...
If this goes bad, should I run for it by myself?
With a growing sense of dread, I used Qi Sense. Blue waves of qi, visible only to me, swept over the enemies charging toward us with wild shrieks.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System Level 12 - Level 11 - Level 12
The reconnaissance squad members shouted, their faces deathly pale.
“What do we do?”
“They’re coming! They’re coming!”
“Captaaaain!”
Thirty meters. Twenty...
I watched the enemy close in at terrifying speed and opened my mouth.
“Don’t worry. The enemy is nothing but EXP... I mean, a rabble. But!”
“But?”
“Stop them with everything you have. Just hold them back.”
“What? What do you mean?”
What do I mean?
Don’t take the last hit.
“Defensive formation! Form up!”
Yep. All the EXP was mine.
“Captain!”
“No! Captaaaain!”
“The Captain’s trying to kill himself!”
That wasn’t what I was doing, you lunatics.
Leaving the reconnaissance squad members’ screams behind, I charged straight at the enemy.
Internal energy surged from my dantian and spread through my limbs and bones.
“You crazy bastard.”
The man at the front grinned, baring yellow teeth.
I grinned back.
“Pretty boy.”
“What?”
Slash.
He clutched his throat and collapsed. As I swept past him, the voice I had been waiting for rang out.
Ding.
System You gained EXP. - You gained 50 Merit!
“What the—!”
“How dare this fucking bastard...”
The enemy was a magnificent sight. Facial scars came standard, and their hygiene was so atrocious that the stench stabbed at my nose.
And yet...
“Ah, this is great.”
I felt like I was standing in a flower garden.
Twenty flowers, each brimming with the sweet honey of EXP.
I charged into them with a blissful expression and sucked out the honey.
Stab. Stab. Stab.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System You gained EXP. - You gained 50 Merit... - You gained EXP... - You gained 50 Merit...
I tore through their ranks without pause.
Their front line collapsed in the blink of an eye, and the others instinctively faltered.
That works for me.
The Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique and Spear Technique were martial arts built around advancing.
I stepped forward with the Manoeuvre Technique, drove into their center, and swung my spear.
“Gaaah!”
“Aaaargh!”
A razor-sharp spear with crushing weight behind it, wielded with an overwhelmingly aggressive technique. Better yet, the enemy was steadily retreating.
It was time for the Jin Family’s Spear Technique to show its true worth.
First form.
I began swinging the spear in step with my footwork. Every swing and thrust brought forth someone’s scream and a burst of blood.
“Ghk.”
“Grrrgh.”
Second form. Third form. Fourth form.
At some point, I surrendered myself to the flow.
The ripples became waves, and the enemies were swept away by them. Every nerve in my body stood on end.
More. More. More...
“You fucking bastard!”
Stab. Stab-stab.
Throat. Chest. Abdomen.
I stabbed and cut them down one after another. The System alerts confirmed the fatalities for me.
How much time had passed?
Only one man remained standing.
“O-our boss will find you no matter—”
I didn’t wait.
A wave was all about flow.
And the final wave erupted from the tip of my spear.
The last form of the Jin Family’s Spear Technique.
Sky-Piercing Strike.
Splurt!
The last man—the one with the narrow, birdlike eyes—stared at the shattered pieces of his sword before dropping to his knees.
The center of his chest had burst open as if struck by a cannonball.
Ding.

System You defeated Level 32 Black Mountain Blade! - You completed the Survivors of the Sakju Branch Quest! - A Chain Quest has been created! - You gain a large amount of EXP! - You gain a large amount of Merit! - You have leveled up! - You have leveled up! - You have leveled...
As the System alerts continued without pause, I rubbed my stomach.
“Buuurp.”
Ah, I’m stuffed.
