I knew it.
I knew this was going to happen.
But it was too late for regrets.
What could I do about my shitty luck?
I heaved a deep sigh and shouted.
“Attack formation!
Form up!”
Clack-clack-clack.
Caught off guard, the squad members nevertheless moved as they had been taught.
By the time they had formed up, the enemy had realized who we were and started shouting.
“They’re brats from the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
“There aren’t many of them!
Wipe them out!”
Brats.
Outnumbered.
Those two facts hit me right in the chest.
I hadn’t even finished teaching these guys.
Their martial arts were weak, they had no real combat experience, and they were complete rookies...
If this goes bad, should I run for it by myself?
With a growing sense of dread, I used Qi Sense.
Blue waves of qi, visible only to me, swept over the enemies charging toward us with wild shrieks.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
System Level 12 - Level 11 - Level 12
The reconnaissance squad members shouted, their faces deathly pale.
“What do we do?”
“They’re coming!
They’re coming!”
“Captaaaain!”
Thirty meters.
Twenty...
I watched the enemy close in at terrifying speed and opened my mouth.
“Don’t worry.
The enemy is nothing but EXP...
I mean, a rabble.
But!”
“But?”
“Stop them with everything you have.
Just hold them back.”
“What?
What do you mean?”
What do I mean?
Don’t take the last hit.
“Defensive formation!
Form up!”
Yep.
All the EXP was mine.
“Captain!”
“No!
Captaaaain!”
“The Captain’s trying to kill himself!”
That wasn’t what I was doing, you lunatics.
Leaving the reconnaissance squad members’ screams behind, I charged straight at the enemy.
Internal energy surged from my dantian and spread through my limbs and bones.
“You crazy bastard.”
The man at the front grinned, baring yellow teeth.
I grinned back.
“Pretty boy.”
“What?”
Slash.
He clutched his throat and collapsed.
As I swept past him, the voice I had been waiting for rang out.
Ding.
System You gained EXP. - You gained 50 Merit!
“What the—!”
“How dare this fucking bastard...”
The enemy was a magnificent sight.
Facial scars came standard, and their hygiene was so atrocious that the stench stabbed at my nose.
And yet...
“Ah, this is great.”
I felt like I was standing in a flower garden.
Twenty flowers, each brimming with the sweet honey of EXP.
I charged into them with a blissful expression and sucked out the honey.
Stab.
Stab.
Stab.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
System You gained EXP. - You gained 50 Merit... - You gained EXP... - You gained 50 Merit...
I tore through their ranks without pause.
Their front line collapsed in the blink of an eye, and the others instinctively faltered.
That works for me.
The Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique and Spear Technique were martial arts built around advancing.
I stepped forward with the Manoeuvre Technique, drove into their center, and swung my spear.
“Gaaah!”
“Aaaargh!”
A razor-sharp spear with crushing weight behind it, wielded with an overwhelmingly aggressive technique.
Better yet, the enemy was steadily retreating.
It was time for the Jin Family’s Spear Technique to show its true worth.
First form.
I began swinging the spear in step with my footwork.
Every swing and thrust brought forth someone’s scream and a burst of blood.
“Ghk.”
“Grrrgh.”
Second form.
Third form.
Fourth form.
At some point, I surrendered myself to the flow.
The ripples became waves, and the enemies were swept away by them.
Every nerve in my body stood on end.
More.
More.
More...
“You fucking bastard!”
Stab.
Stab-stab.
Throat.
Chest.
Abdomen.
I stabbed and cut them down one after another.
The System alerts confirmed the fatalities for me.
How much time had passed?
Only one man remained standing.
“O-our boss will find you no matter—”
I didn’t wait.
A wave was all about flow.
And the final wave erupted from the tip of my spear.
The last form of the Jin Family’s Spear Technique.
Sky-Piercing Strike.
Splurt!
The last man—the one with the narrow, birdlike eyes—stared at the shattered pieces of his sword before dropping to his knees.
The center of his chest had burst open as if struck by a cannonball.
Ding.

System You defeated Level 32 Black Mountain Blade! - You completed the Survivors of the Sakju Branch Quest! - A Chain Quest has been created! - You gain a large amount of EXP! - You gain a large amount of Merit! - You have leveled up! - You have leveled up! - You have leveled...
As the System alerts continued without pause, I rubbed my stomach.
“Buuurp.”
Ah, I’m stuffed.

chapters.title: Chapter 25
paragraphs: “Is this the afterlife?”
That was the first thing the middle-aged man said when he woke up.
Before I could answer, a small figure sprang forward and threw himself into the man’s arms.
The boy cried out, his eyes brimming with tears.
“Uncle Gong!”
“Socheon! You’re safe. But what in the world...?”
Socheon explained through his sobs that he had met us on the hill and that I had killed all their enemies. The middle-aged man’s eyes widened.
“Are you from the main family?”
“Yes, I am.”
“Ah, Heaven has helped us!”
I helped you, you old man.
“I was sure I’d fallen down the mountain... I thought that was the end of me.”
“You nearly did. You were lucky.”
I pointed below the ridge. Two corpses that appeared to belong to the enemy lay with their heads embedded in trees.
If the slope he had tumbled down hadn’t been covered in thick undergrowth, he would have ended up just like them.
I didn’t notice him at first, either.
I had only realized the middle-aged man was there because of the Quest Window.
Even after I defeated all the enemies, the Survivors of the Sakju Branch Quest had not been completed. That meant there were more survivors.
The question was whether there were any more besides him...
The last trace of unease vanished as soon as I helped the exhausted man to his feet.
Ding.
System You completed the Survivors of the Sakju Branch Quest! - A Chain Quest has been created! - You leveled up! - You leveled up! - Merit and Fame increase!
“Whew.”
The middle-aged man exhaled. Though he had only circulated his qi briefly, his complexion had improved noticeably.
He rose and respectfully clasped his hands in salute.
“Benefactor, you saved us all.”
“Not at all. I only did what anyone should have done.”
These days, lies came pouring out whenever I opened my mouth. Then again, it wasn’t entirely untrue. I had to clear the Quest somehow.
If anything, I should be the one bowing and thanking them.
Still, Santa Claus—or rather, the survivors—seemed deeply moved by my attitude.
“Such outstanding martial arts, and such chivalry as well. I, Gong Yacheong, sincerely admire you.”
“Socheon and Soyul owe you a tremendous debt, Great Hero.”
That was how I learned their names. The middle-aged man was Gong Yacheong, and the young siblings were Socheon and Soyul.
“If it isn’t too impertinent, may I ask your name, Benefactor?”
“My name is...”
Then a thought struck me.
Wait. If I tell them my name, won’t they come at me with swords?

Whatever conspiracy lay behind it, the person who had lit the fuse on this war was none other than me, Jin Taekyung. I doubted two people who had lost their home and family would feel kindly toward me.
Right. This calls for a well-intentioned lie.
“Hong Gil-dong. My name is Hong Gil-dong.”
“Hong Gil-dong... I’ve never heard the name before, but it has the air of a hero.”
Socheon chimed in from beside him.
“Here one moment, there the next. It sounds like the name of someone who could appear and disappear like a ghost.”
...How did that kid know?
Before he could bring up the part about calling one’s father Father and one’s elder brother Brother, I hurriedly changed the subject.
“More importantly, what happened?”
Dark shadows fell across their faces.
Gong Yacheong spoke first.
“It happened only a few days ago.”

By the time the messenger pigeon arrived with news of the war, the Sakju Branch had already been surrounded so tightly that not even a drop of water could escape. The wandering martial artists hired by the Mount Heng Sword Sect slaughtered the people inside and set fire to the buildings.

“There were no fewer than a hundred of them. The Branch Leader and his martial artists bought us enough time to escape through a secret passage. Most of those who got out were women and children who knew no martial arts.”
I didn’t need to ask what had happened to the others.
The System was absolute and factual. According to the Quest Window, these three were the only survivors of the Sakju Branch.
“I want to know about the enemy.”
“They’re wandering martial artists.”
“Wandering martial artists?”
“As you know, they’re bastards who’ll do anything for money. The Mount Heng Sword Sect hired the worst of them to attack us.”
“They seemed pretty weak for such vile bastards.”
“What do good and evil have to do with strength? The ones they hired were ordinary wandering martial artists, common as dirt. Their leader was the problem.”
Gong Yacheong gritted his teeth.
“Jopil, One Question, One Kill. That was the man. The Branch Leader knew we were doomed the moment he saw him and entrusted his dependents to me.”
Socheon’s small fists trembled.
“I’ll tear him limb from limb and kill him with my own hands.”
That was an unusual choice of words for a child, but considering the grudge carved into his bones, it was understandable.
I patted Socheon on the head.
“And you will. I’ll help you.”
“Really?”
“A man’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold. Do you think I’d say one thing and do another? I’ll definitely catch that bastard and level u—”
“Huh?”
“No, I mean I’ll kill him and avenge your grudge.”
“Ah... Thank you. Thank you so much, Great Hero Hong!”
“Thank you. Truly, thank you!”
The two of them repeatedly expressed their gratitude. I felt like a real scumbag, and a sharp stab tore through one corner of my chest.
No, this is fine. They’ll be happy when their enemy dies, and I’ll be happy when I level up. It’s mutually beneficial. Mutually beneficial.
Having forced myself to accept that logic, I asked, “How many are there?”
“While scouting their position, I overheard them talking. They said there were about thirty, including Jopil.”
“Thirty? Thirty men?”
“That’s right. So we must flee at once...”
Gong Yacheong’s voice faded into the distance. In its place, I heard a faint sound drawing closer.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
I could hear it—the sound of leveling up. The sound of logging out!
Struggling to keep the corners of my mouth from rising, I said, “Let’s wait here for the rest of them.”
“Wait? What do you mean?”
“We’ll wipe them all out! We can’t let such vile bastards live!”
“No, Great Hero Hong, listen to me...”
“A master like you can do it! Thank you, Benefactor!”
Socheon ran into my arms with tears in his eyes. I spread my arms and pulled him into a hug.
“That’s right. Let’s kill them all!”
“Let’s kill them!”
“Jopil, you son of a bitch!”
“Son of a bitch!”
That was when Gong Yacheong spoke.
“Jopil is a Peak master.”
“Jopil is a fucking bast—huh?”

“Jopil, One Question, One Kill. He’s one of the few Peak masters in all of Shanxi. What do you think is the reason he has survived until now, despite being tangled up in all kinds of gratitude and grudges?”
“Don’t tell me...”
“Everyone who challenged him died. That’s the kind of man Jopil is. Cruel—and every bit as strong.”
“Ah.”
Sensing that something was wrong, Socheon looked up at me.
“Socheon.”
“Yes, Great Hero.”
“Now that I think about it, this probably isn’t the right time.”
“Huh?”
“I was being foolish. Our first priority should be getting you and your sister safely back to our family. Right?”
“I was injured during the fight, and my men are exhausted. It would probably be a difficult battle.”
Socheon looked me up and down. My clothes were soaked in the enemies’ blood, but they were perfectly intact, without a single tear. There was no way I could have been injured.
“I suffered an internal injury.”
This time, he turned to the reconnaissance squad. They hadn’t even swung their swords during the fight and were practically overflowing with energy.
“Things aren’t always what they seem.”
“...Great Hero.”
I gently pulled Socheon away and shouted, “We’re returning to the main family. Everyone, prepare to leave!”
I hurried back toward the squad, but Socheon’s hand clutched my collar tightly and refused to let go. Tears glimmered in his round eyes.
“Great Hero.”
“Hey, why aren’t you moving? Move, move! Socheon, I’m a little busy right now, so let’s talk later. Okay?”
“Great Heeero.”
“Mister Gong Yacheong. No, Great Hero Gong, what are you doing? Every second counts.”
“...Socheon, come here.”
Gong Yacheong looked at me as if I were a complete idiot and pulled Socheon away. It was the protective gesture of a guardian keeping a criminal away from his child.
Socheon practically wailed.
“Great Hero Hong Gil-dooong!”
That was the signal.
Boom!
The cabin door shattered, and someone burst through it.
System Level 22 Hyuk Mujin
“Jin Taekyung, you fucking bastard!”
Hyuk Mujin stood there panting, his furious eyes fixed squarely on me. Gong Yacheong and Socheon stared at me blankly.
“Great Hero Hong?”
“Great Hero Hong Gil-dong?”
“Ah. Well, you see...”
...Fuck.
“Hmm.”
Jopil stared silently down at the corpse. Its face was twisted, its eyes bulging. Frozen beneath blood and snow, the man had once been known as Black Mountain Blade.
“Tsk, tsk. How did you end up like this, my friend?”
He had been fairly loyal and sharp. Jopil had never imagined he would meet such a pointless end.
“See? Haven’t I told you time and again to keep your eyes wide open?”
Jopil grabbed Black Mountain Blade’s bulging eyelids and pried them farther apart.
The frozen flesh tore with a hideous sound.
Rip. Riiip.
The others watched without daring to breathe.
His expression and tone were no different from usual, but they could feel in their bones that Jopil was furious.
The killing intent radiating from the Peak master left them struggling for breath, cold sweat trickling down their backs.
And no wonder.
More than twenty men had been wiped out while carrying out a simple mission to dispose of the remnants of the Sakju Branch.
Jopil was called One Question, One Kill because of his bizarre habit of asking any enemy who caught his interest exactly one question before killing them.
The wandering martial artists were relieved that Black Mountain Blade was dead. If he had survived, he would have suffered an even more horrifying fate.
“That’s better.”
Jopil wiped the blood on the front of his trousers and rose.
“So, what does everyone think? Speak freely.”
“We should follow our orders, of course.”

One man stepped forward. The neatly dressed, dignified middle-aged man and the dozen or so martial artists standing at attention behind him were the overseers and guides the Mount Heng Sword Sect had sent to keep the wandering martial artists under control.
Jopil smiled faintly.
“Ah, yes. I’d forgotten the Hall Master of the great Mount Heng Sword Sect was here. But what’s this about an order?”
“Erase the Sakju Branch and rejoin the main force. Have you already forgotten the Young Sect Leader’s order?”
“An order? I remember accepting a commission.”
“Isn’t that the same thing?”
The middle-aged man glared at Jopil, displeased.
“Coming this far was your own unilateral decision. And what came of it? You lost more than twenty subordinates to the remnants of a single branch!”
“Which is why we should pursue them. We can finish them off in half a day.”
“Jeongyang might be one thing, but if we pursue them as far as Honju, we risk a counterattack. I won’t permit any more unilateral decisions.”
“Permission. Permission...”
After mulling it over, Jopil spoke.
“No. That won’t do. I don’t like it.”
“What do you mea—”
Crunch.
The middle-aged man’s neck shattered, killing him before he could finish. Jopil had snapped it with blinding speed. He licked his lips.
“I like war. No matter who dies, they’re forgotten.”
“You bastard!”
The Mount Heng Sword Sect’s martial artists realized what had happened and drew their weapons, but Jopil had already plunged into their midst.
Crunch! Slash!
Warm blood poured across the snow. Every time Jopil rampaged like a wild beast, someone’s neck, arm, or leg was torn free and sent flying.
“Gaaah...”
The groan of an unnamed martial artist was the last sound.
Standing atop the heap of corpses, Jopil spoke into the crushing silence.
“We’re pursuing them.”
This time, no one said a word. As his subordinates hurried to prepare as though fleeing for their lives, Jopil continued to stare at the bodies.
What kind of man was it?
He was a Peak master. From the wounds on the corpses and the footprints left behind, he could reconstruct his opponent.
Only one man. A highly skilled spearman had been here. He was the one who had slaughtered the other twenty-odd men.
If he killed Black Mountain Blade in one strike, he must be something else.
The final strike that pierced through Black Mountain Blade’s chest had been particularly interesting.
This should be a fun fight.
Who was he? A master from the Jin Family of Taiyuan? Or someone unknown?
It didn’t matter. Jopil let out a pleased laugh.
“Let’s meet soon, friend.”
“What news has come in?”
“None. All we can do is move as quickly as possible...”
“Damn it! Damn it!”
Wipeng vented his frustration, but there was nothing he could do. As his subordinate had said, their only option was to find the Third Young Master as quickly as possible and protect him.
Jopil, One Question, One Kill...
Wipeng knew the man’s reputation well. If the Third Young Master fell into his hands, death would be the only possible outcome.
If that happens, I won’t be able to face my lord.
Jin Wikyung had endured with superhuman patience.

He currently stood at the head and center of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. He had weighed his beloved younger brother against the lives of hundreds of family members and, after long deliberation, sent his most trusted subordinate, Wipeng, to protect him.
But if I fail...
I won’t be able to face my lord.
His grip tightened around the reins. Wipeng spurred his horse onward, with more than twenty mounted riders racing in a long line behind him.

The neatly dressed, dignified middle-aged man and the dozen or so martial artists standing at attention behind him were the overseers and guides the Mount Heng Sword Sect had sent to keep the wandering martial artists under control.
Jopil smiled faintly.
“Ah, yes.
I’d forgotten the Hall Master of the great Mount Heng Sword Sect was here.
But what’s this about an order?”
“Erase the Sakju Branch and rejoin the main force.
Have you already forgotten the Young Sect Leader’s order?”
“An order?
I remember accepting a commission.”
“Isn’t that the same thing?”
The middle-aged man glared at Jopil, displeased.
“Coming this far was your own unilateral decision.
And what came of it?
You lost more than twenty subordinates to the remnants of a single branch!”
“Which is why we should pursue them.
We can finish them off in half a day.”
“Jeongyang might be one thing, but if we pursue them as far as Honju, we risk a counterattack.
I won’t permit any more unilateral decisions.”
“Permission.
Permission...”
After mulling it over, Jopil spoke.
“No.
That won’t do.
I don’t like it.”
“What do you mea—”
Crunch.
The middle-aged man’s neck shattered, killing him before he could finish.
Jopil had snapped it with blinding speed.
He licked his lips.
“I like war.
No matter who dies, they’re forgotten.”
“You bastard!”
The Mount Heng Sword Sect’s martial artists realized what had happened and drew their weapons, but Jopil had already plunged into their midst.
Crunch!
Slash!
Warm blood poured across the snow.
Every time Jopil rampaged like a wild beast, someone’s neck, arm, or leg was torn free and sent flying.
“Gaaah...”
The groan of an unnamed martial artist was the last sound.
Standing atop the heap of corpses, Jopil spoke into the crushing silence.
“We’re pursuing them.”
This time, no one said a word.
As his subordinates hurried to prepare as though fleeing for their lives, Jopil continued to stare at the bodies.
What kind of man was it?
He was a Peak master.
From the wounds on the corpses and the footprints left behind, he could reconstruct his opponent.
Only one man.
A highly skilled spearman had been here.
He was the one who had slaughtered the other twenty-odd men.
If he killed Black Mountain Blade in one strike, he must be something else.
The final strike that pierced through Black Mountain Blade’s chest had been particularly interesting.
This should be a fun fight.
Who was he?
A master from the Jin Family of Taiyuan?
Or someone unknown?
It didn’t matter.
Jopil let out a pleased laugh.
“Let’s meet soon, friend.”
“What news has come in?”
“None.
All we can do is move as quickly as possible...”
“Damn it!
Damn it!”
Wipeng vented his frustration, but there was nothing he could do.
As his subordinate had said, their only option was to find the Third Young Master as quickly as possible and protect him.
Jopil, One Question, One Kill...
Wipeng knew the man’s reputation well.
If the Third Young Master fell into his hands, death would be the only possible outcome.
If that happens, I won’t be able to face my lord.
Jin Wikyung had endured with superhuman patience.
He currently stood at the head and center of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
He had weighed his beloved younger brother against the lives of hundreds of family members and, after long deliberation, sent his most trusted subordinate, Wipeng, to protect him.
But if I fail...
I won’t be able to face my lord.
His grip tightened around the reins.
Wipeng spurred his horse onward, with more than twenty mounted riders racing in a long line behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 26
paragraphs: Gong Yacheong gave me a strange look.
“So you’re that Young Master Jin Taekyung.”
The moment had finally come. I let go of Hyuk Mujin’s collar—he’d passed out for the third time—and smiled awkwardly.
“Yes. I’m Jin Taekyung.”
The reconnaissance squad members preparing camp pricked up their ears. We were on our way back to the family estate.
We had ridden for more than five hours without a break since leaving the cabin where the fight had taken place. Gong Yacheong had remained silent the entire way. Only now did he finally speak.
If it weren’t for that bastard.
I glared at Hyuk Mujin as one of the quicker-witted squad members dragged him away. I should’ve hit him one more time before letting go.
While I was regretting that missed opportunity, Gong Yacheong continued.
“I’ve heard plenty about you, Young Master.”
“...I see.”
“Even a three-year-old knows who you are. You must be the main family’s biggest celebrity.”
At this point, it would probably be faster to find someone who hadn’t heard of me.

“Lazy by nature and arrogant beyond belief. Addicted to wine and women, without even bothering to learn martial arts... But it seems the rumors of the martial world truly can’t be trusted. The prowess you displayed today was remarkable.”
If there were such a thing as the Martial World Daily, collecting all the latest rumors from across Murim, I’d subscribe immediately. It seemed surprisingly reliable.
More importantly...
Did Gong Yacheong really not know?
Whatever bullshit the Mount Heng Sword Sect had pulled, I was at the center of this entire mess.
It was an undeniable fact that countless people had died along the way.
It wouldn’t have been strange for Gong Yacheong and Socheon to hold a grudge against me. That was why I had hidden my name.
If he really doesn’t know, that’s a relief.
We were being chased by a ruthless Peak master. I had no interest in stirring up extra trouble.
“How long until we reach the main family?”
Gong Yacheong’s question snapped me back to reality.
“We should arrive in two or three days.”
“Of all times, it had to snow now...”
Gong Yacheong sighed and glared resentfully at the sky, which was still dumping snow on us.
“Young Master, we should prepare for the worst.”
“The worst?”
The blizzard had us stuck, but it had our enemies stuck too. There was even a chance they had given up the chase.
But Gong Yacheong shook his head.
“Don’t underestimate wandering martial artists. Their internal energy may be less refined, and the martial arts they’ve learned may be inferior, but their greatest weapon lies elsewhere.”
I gave him the answer.
“Experience.”

“Exactly. Experience gained through a hundred battles. The ones chasing us aren’t merely martial artists. They’re wandering martial artists. The two may seem alike, but they’re entirely different creatures.”
Alike, yet different. I thought I understood what he meant.
In short, they were well-trained hunting dogs. And the man holding their leash was Jopil, One Question, One Kill.
“What makes Jopil truly frightening isn’t simply that he’s a Peak master. It’s his persistence. His viciousness. He has never once failed a commission or allowed a target to escape.”
I answered with a sigh.
“This time won’t be any different, then.”
“Probably.”
Gong Yacheong stared into the darkness ahead as though something might leap out and swallow us whole.
“That is the sort of man pursuing us.”
Whoosh.
The snow-laden wind vanished into the darkness.

We finished making camp. We had dug several small hollows and covered their entrances with branches, fallen leaves, and whatever else we could find. The shelters were crude, but this was no time to be choosy.
“Have a restful night.”
Gong Yacheong disappeared into one of them, carrying the siblings, who had already fallen fast asleep. I couldn’t stop thinking about the weary smile hanging from the corner of his mouth.
He really is an adult.
If he had wanted to live, he could have run away long ago. Gong Yacheong was a trained master, a seasoned man of the martial world.
But he hadn’t.
He had risked his life fighting for two children who didn’t share a drop of his blood.
That was why Gong Yacheong was a good adult.
Could I do the same?
I shook off the question as soon as it arose. This was a game. It wasn’t wise to think too deeply about an illusion that would soon disappear.
That was right. An illusion that would soon disappear.
Open Quest Window.
Ding.

System Quest Logout You must now make your way through this harsh Murim. Become stronger. Become famous. For the day that will come someday... Grade: Main Quest Limit: Jin Taekyung Task: Reach the First Rate realm — Incomplete Reach Lv. 30 — 24/30 Reach Fame 500 — 250/500 Reward: Logout
The EXP and Fame I had gained from dealing with the enemies, plus the Quest reward.
I could finally see the summit of this treacherous mountain.
I opened my Status Window and distributed all my remaining points. Vitality flowed back into my exhausted body.
I’m almost there.
I just had to get past this final hurdle. If I could avoid Jopil, One Question, One Kill—the bastard whose face I didn’t even know—I could finally bring this miserable journey to an end.
But there was another problem.
Let’s say I somehow fill up my Level and Fame. How the hell am I supposed to raise my realm?
Back when I first started clearing the tutorial Quests, distributing my stats had raised my realm from Third Rate to Second Rate. Since then, nothing.
What the hell am I missing?
I was an absurd existence in Murim. I could learn martial arts and raise my stats faster than anyone else. The System had helped me grow stronger in all kinds of ways.
That was why I could literally wipe the floor with ordinary First Rate martial artists despite being a dime-a-dozen Second Rate.
And yet I wasn’t First Rate!
I should’ve asked Jin Wikyung.
At first, I had assumed I just needed to keep raising my stats or internal energy. Lately, though, I had begun to suspect I was barking up the wrong tree.
Level? Stats? Internal energy?
What was it? What final piece did I need to complete the puzzle?
The answer came quickly.
If I don’t know, I have to find out.
Just as I always had. If I kept walking, I would eventually find the exit.
I sat cross-legged and steadied my breathing. The internal energy coiled within my dantian answered my call.
“We lost them.”
Jopil muttered as his black, viper-like eyes swept across the surroundings.
They had lost the fugitives. But traces remained, faint signs that would serve as new guideposts.
“About twenty people. They left this place roughly two shichen ago.”
Jopil nodded at his subordinate’s report. The man’s martial arts were only Third Rate, but his tracking skills had reached the Peak. Jopil had countless hunting dogs like him under his command.
Two shichen.
The gap had already narrowed to two shichen. How much longer would it take them to catch the fugitives?
Half a day at most.
They should have run with everything they had. Without looking back. They should have cast off every burden, abandoned anyone who fell behind, and run for their lives.
If they had done that, the distance would not have narrowed. But they had let their guard down. They must have thought the blizzard had them trapped.
That misjudgment had brought them to this point.
But I’m a little different.
The previous night had been long. Even among his subordinates, men well accustomed to pursuit, some had fallen behind.
In the mountains during a blizzard, falling behind was no different from death.
The only difference from dying on a battlefield was that it took a little longer.
That was why Jopil had given the order.
Kill them.
They said a tiger left its hide when it died, while a person left their name.
But Jopil thought differently. What kind of name could a Third Rate nobody who’d spent his whole life drifting through back alleys leave behind?
They should at least leave a hide.
Leaving twenty stripped corpses behind, the group had pressed onward. When the long night finally ended, they discovered the fugitives’ trail shortly before dawn.
We’ll meet soon, friend.
The corners of Jopil’s mouth curled upward. This mysterious master was the first person in a long time to pique his interest.
His heart, stiff for so long, began to pound.
I shuddered.
“Ugh. What the hell?”
A sudden chill ran through me. I raised my arm and found it covered in goose bumps.
If this had been a scene in a novel, the protagonist would have muttered that something felt wrong, then continued on his way.
But I was different. I had a solid hunch, and I acted on it.
“Hey. Get over here, quick.”
I couldn’t see him, but I could sense him. The footsteps of someone trudging along behind me faltered.
“W-why?”
“I’m counting to three. One, two... three.”
The moment I reached three, Hyuk Mujin hurried over and stuck to my side.
“It was you, wasn’t it?”
“What?”
“You were the one. Tell me the truth and I’ll let it slide.”
“What are you talking about? It wasn’t me!”
I silently stared at his face, swollen like a steamed bun.
“You were cursing me behind my back just now, weren’t you?”
“Gasp.”
“You were, weren’t you?”
“I-I was...”
So it really had been this bastard. When I raised my hand, Hyuk Mujin squeezed his eyes shut.
After getting beaten about three times, he had lost all his fighting spirit. On top of that, he had learned a valuable life lesson:
Dodging only meant getting hit more.
“Fine. Since you told the truth, I’ll let it slide this once.”
Hyuk Mujin’s head shot up.
“Really?”
I gave him a warm smile.
“Of course. But don’t even think about deceiving me from now on. I’ll be watching you with mind-reading.”
Hyuk Mujin stared at me with eyes full of demonic rage, then darted back to his place. If only we’d had more time, I could have smashed his head in with a mace.
Swallowing my regret, I kept walking.
“What’s mind-reading?”
The chirping voice tickled my ear. It belonged to Soyul, Socheon’s little sister. Had they said she was five?
She was small enough to fit right inside my backpack.
“Is it martial arts?”
“Something like that.”
“Is mind-reading strong?”
“Very strong.”
“Wow! Soyul wants to learn mind-reading too!”
“But you have to be one-eyed.”
“Gasp!”
I glanced back and saw Soyul staring at me in shock, her eyes enormous. She was ridiculously cute.
Hayeon used to be like that too.
These days she was a creepy little sister, but when she was little she had been a baby angel. She had even gotten offers to be a child model...
Having her around felt exactly like piggybacking Hayeon at that age.
“Want me to teach you?”
“...Soyul doesn’t like martial arts. I want to become a proper young lady.”
“That’s good too.”
“Mm. Mister, do you like martial arts?”
“Me?”
“My brother says you’re really strong. Dad said only people who work hard can become strong.”
“Your dad said that?”
“Yes. My dad is really strong too. That’s because...”
Soyul chattered excitedly for a long while before sticking out her lower lip.
“Soyul wants to see Dad. But I guess Dad doesn’t want to see us. Oppa says he went out to play with Mom, leaving me and Oppa behind.”
My heart dropped with a thud.
An old memory filled my vision. In a funeral hall draped in black and white, little Hayeon had searched for our father, and I had been forced to tell her an obvious lie.
Just as Socheon had done for Soyul.
It was the only thing I could say.
“...I see.”
What else could I say?
I looked at Socheon, who was following in the middle of the formation. He was breathing hard, drenched in sweat.
He must be exhausted.
His willpower was far beyond his years. The saying that pain made people mature was fucking bullshit, but it was true.
Socheon had never fallen behind even once, and the other reconnaissance squad members marveled at him for it.
But the real problem is somewhere else.
Gong Yacheong.

His face was deathly pale; he still hadn’t shaken off his injuries. If not for the remarkable effects of the fasting pills I had given him, and the qi he had circulated last night, he might have collapsed long ago.
At this rate, they’ll catch us.
Even after sunrise, the deep snow showed no sign of melting. I was leading the way and breaking a path through it, but everyone was exhausted, and our pace kept slowing.
Worse, we had an injured man and two children with us.
Should I run away on my own?
The thought came to me in an instant.
It was a game. So what?
Gong Yacheong, the young siblings, every member of the reconnaissance squad—they were all artificially created intelligences. Nothing more than NPCs.
But me?
I was alive. I was the only real person among them. The only one who truly existed.
But...
Fuck. It’s such a simple problem... So why am I like this?
An inexplicable aversion surged up. It was strong enough to startle me—strong enough to throw me off.
Why?
I didn’t know.
For hours afterward, I failed to find the answer.
And then night fell.

It was strong enough to startle me—strong enough to throw me off.
Why?
I didn’t know.
For hours afterward, I failed to find the answer.
And then night fell.

chapters.title: Chapter 27
paragraphs: “Fifteen-minute break.”
The reconnaissance squad collapsed with a collective hiss, like the air going out of them.
They looked exhausted, but I wasn’t particularly worried about those guys. As I’d observed, they had solid basic stamina, and during the battle they had done nothing but stand around and watch.
The other two were the problem...
“Are you all right?”
“Huff. I’m fine. I’m fine.”
Socheon answered between ragged breaths. He didn’t look ready to collapse just yet, but if he kept going like this, he would reach his limit before long.
Stubborn little brat.
Earlier, I had offered to carry both him and his sister. He had flatly refused.
“If it gets too hard, tell me. I can handle the two of you.”
“Huff. I’m fine as I am. This is enough.”
Doesn’t look like it.
“I’m saying this for everyone’s sake. Don’t answer so quickly.”
“Understood.”
His eyes hardened with resolve. I handed the sleeping Soyul to him and turned away.
“Great Hero Gong.”
The pale-faced man raised his head.
“...Young Master Jin.”
His voice sounded ready to give out at any moment. His condition was worse than I’d thought. Are you all right? rose to the tip of my tongue, then faded away.
“How much longer can you hold out?”
“I don’t know.”
His answer was honest—and serious.
“What about the fasting pills?”
I had given him several of the fasting pills I had left. But Gong Yacheong shook his head.
“They weren’t much help. Some quack must have made them. All they did was ruin my appetite. Hahaha.”
“...Was that supposed to make me laugh?”
“It wasn’t funny?”
“No. Not at all.”
“What a shame... Cough!”
A sudden cough.
Drops of blood fell onto the white snow.
Damn it.
Worried that someone might see, I hurriedly stepped in front of Gong Yacheong.
“What’s going on? You weren’t this bad before.”
His condition had deteriorated rapidly in half a day. Gong Yacheong no longer looked merely exhausted. He looked unmistakably ill.
“It was inevitable.”
The calm look in his eyes made it even more ominous. I brushed aside the hand trying to stop me and pulled up the front of his robe.
“Ah.”
His body was covered in all kinds of wounds. But what shocked me were the blue veins spreading outward from his lower abdomen.
“What is this...? Don’t tell me...”
Gong Yacheong weakly fastened his robe again. He seemed worried that someone else—especially Socheon and Soyul—might see.
“Those wolf-like bastards coated their weapons with poison.”
Now I understood why Gong Yacheong hadn’t recovered even after taking the fasting pills. They could only stave off hunger and restore stamina. They had no detoxifying effect whatsoever.
“You should’ve told me sooner!”
“Those bastards must have been short on money. They used cheap poison. It was so weak that I didn’t notice until last night. By then, it was too late.”
Gong Yacheong’s stamina had already been at rock bottom when he was poisoned. Then he had continued forcing himself through this weather...
“Is there anything we can do?”
“There is.”
“Tell me.”
“But time won’t allow it. I can’t waste such precious time on one person.”
He was right.
But still...
“We have to try.”
“Young Master.”
“Everyone’s exhausted. If we rest for one shichen—no, just half a shichen—and try the method, that should be enough.”
“Hahaha.”
“Please don’t laugh. I was planning to stop and rest around here anyway...”
I didn’t even know what I was saying anymore. As Gong Yacheong watched me ramble, a faint smile touched his lips.
“Go.”
“You know it too, don’t you? If we waste time here, we’ll be held back.”
I fell silent.
He was right. I had been considering this possibility since I saw his precarious complexion and the blood he coughed up. Perhaps I had been thinking about it since last night.
So this is how it ends?
I had to leave Gong Yacheong behind. If we took him with us, he might survive for now, but everyone’s pace would slow.
What if I carried him myself?
Even with the System’s help, I was still human. I had spent two days at the head of the group, breaking a path through the snow, and the fatigue had built up.
Two fasting pills left.
The thirty or so fasting pills I’d started with were almost gone. Could I escape their clutches while carrying Gong Yacheong with only two pills left?
And if we still ended up running into them, would I be able to fight them while exhausted? Would I be able to face Jopil, One Question, One Kill, a Peak master?
The answer had been clear for a long time.
We both knew it.
“Please take care of the children.”
The moment Gong Yacheong spoke, a System notification chimed.
Ding.

System Quest Gong Yacheong’s Last Request He wants only one thing now. See that the surviving children make it back safely. Grade: None Limit: Jin Taekyung Task: Socheon and Soyul’s safe return (Incomplete) Reward: None - Would you like to accept the Quest?
No reward.
It was the most shameless Quest I had ever received.
I’m busy trying to stay alive myself, old man.
But I nodded. If accepting it could ease the nagging discomfort in the corner of my heart, I would gladly do it.
“Let’s do that.”
Gong Yacheong smiled in satisfaction.
“You’re saying we’re leaving Great Hero Gong behind?”
Han Yeop muttered with a shocked expression. Hyuk Mujin said nothing, as though he was lost in thought, while the other reconnaissance squad members were busy watching one another’s faces.
“Yes.”
“That makes no sense!”
“Keep your voice down.”
Nothing good would come of Socheon finding out. He was exactly the sort of kid who would insist on staying behind with Gong Yacheong.
“B-but this...”
“It was Great Hero Gong’s decision. I agree with him.”
That was when Hyuk Mujin abruptly spoke up.
“Why?”
Has this bastard not been beaten enough?
I glared at him, but Hyuk Mujin neither flinched nor backed down. My clenched fist slowly relaxed.
“His condition is serious. If we keep taking him with us, the rest of us will be in danger too.”
“Is that all?”
“Yes.”
Han Yeop cut in, his face flushed.
“No.”
“It’s an order.”
“Then I’ll disobey.”
Everyone stared at Han Yeop in surprise.
I hadn’t expected the boy who had declared himself my ardent follower from the very first time we met to use the word disobey, either.
“That won’t change anything.”
“We can’t leave him behind like this.”
“And if we can’t leave him behind?”
A wave of exhaustion suddenly washed over me. I rubbed my gritty eyes.
“If we can’t leave him behind, will you carry him?”
“Yes. I’ll carry him.”
“And you’ll get tired soon.”
If Han Yeop got tired, someone else would step forward to help him. Then they would grow tired one by one, our pace would slow, and the enemy would catch up.
“We’re up against battle-hardened wandering martial artists led by a Peak master. Do you think we’ll survive?”
Han Yeop lowered his head without answering. The other reconnaissance squad members avoided my gaze as well.
Only one person kept looking me in the eye.
“Number One. Do you still have something to say?”
After a long silence, Hyuk Mujin bowed his head.
“I’ll follow your orders, Captain.”
We began moving again.
Just before we left, Gong Yacheong gently stroked Socheon and Soyul’s heads with a peaceful expression.
“I’ll see you soon.”
Socheon nodded bravely. Still half-asleep, Soyul whimpered and nestled into my arms.
Every time I heard her soft breathing, something twisted uncomfortably in my chest.
Has he left by now?
Gong Yacheong hadn’t wanted the children to know he was gone. He had told me he would quietly slip away while we were moving.
Socheon was in the middle of the formation, so the reconnaissance squad members would block his view. He wouldn’t see Gong Yacheong leave.
How long has it been since we set out?
A sikyeong? Half a shichen?
I didn’t know. In the dead of night, with darkness swallowing everything around us, I couldn’t even feel the passage of time.
With every step I took, one thought refused to leave my mind.
He must have left by now.
It was only natural. Gong Yacheong and I both knew it, and everyone in the reconnaissance squad except Han Yeop had accepted it.
Most importantly...
I had a family waiting for me. I had a real world out there that I still had to face.
Then why does this feel so damn awful?
My feet felt heavy.
It wasn’t just the snow piled up to my calves. It wasn’t the grass and branches blocking the path ahead.
A mere NPC named Gong Yacheong kept weighing on my mind.
I remembered his final smile. The cheap Quest with no reward.
I remembered Han Yeop’s defiance, and Hyuk Mujin’s calm gaze pricked the corner of my heart like a thorn.
It’s only natural. So why?
Because it was a game.
Because it was only a game.
If I didn’t leave him behind, everyone would die. I’d die too! You fucking bastards!
“Fuuuck...”
The curse lodged in my throat finally spilled out.
Soyul stirred from her light sleep, mumbled something, and wrapped her arms around my neck.
Her tiny hands were cold. So real that goose bumps rose across my skin. Too real for me to believe this was only a game.
Real enough to make me feel guilty for abandoning a single NPC.
“...What a fucked-up game.”
I turned around.
“Where are you going?”
I strode back the way we had come. I couldn’t see Socheon’s face or the faces of the reconnaissance squad members.
That was why I didn’t notice the fleeting smile on Hyuk Mujin’s face as he asked where I was going.
Or that Han Yeop, who should have been at the very rear, was nowhere to be seen.
“Huff. Huuuff.”
I raced across the snow like the wind.
And then I found him.
Below the hill, Han Yeop was gritting his teeth and forcing one foot in front of the other, even as he gasped for breath.
The unconscious Gong Yacheong was on his back.
I didn’t know what to say. With a sigh, I grabbed Han Yeop’s hand and pulled him up.
“Th-thank you.”
Shit...
I don’t know anymore, either.
This was a hidden retreat meant for one person alone.

Since becoming its owner thirty years ago, he had forbidden anyone else from entering. As the years passed, that prohibition had hardened into an unbreakable rule, and everyone else regarded it as such.
“How are things going?”
The air trembled faintly as the two shadows conversed through Sound Transmission.
“Smoothly. And on your end?”
“Do you even need to ask?”
“I wouldn’t expect otherwise.”
“The Blood Wolf Sword. For someone with that epithet, he’s surprisingly fond of his family.”
“Even a wolf cares for its own flesh and blood. So?”
“The vanguard alone numbers two hundred. A madman named Jopil is running wild as he pleases, but... it should be fine.”
“Jopil, One Question, One Kill? The Blood Wolf Sword chose well.”
“The wastrel young master is being chased for his life. It wasn’t part of the plan, but it isn’t a bad development.”
“Hahahaha.”
“Could it be...?”
“That’s right. I sent him. Once the Lesser Family Head sees the head of his beloved youngest brother, he’ll change his mind.”
“Whew. A heart as cold as poison, without blood or tears. Impressive.”
“Is that something you should be saying?”
“I only took one hopeless life.”
“And thanks to that, a bloody storm will sweep through Shanxi Province?”
“Isn’t that what you wanted?”
“I can’t deny it. Yes. I’ve waited far too long.”
“The fruit will taste all the sweeter.”
“I hope so.”
“Ah, right. The Lower District Sect has gotten involved.”
“The Lower District Sect? How?”
“The new Branch Leader has a keen nose. Once this matter is settled, I intend to drive them out.”
“Be careful. No matter how formidable Heaven may be, you must never let your guard down...”
At that moment, the wind stopped.
The air quivered.
“...I misspoke.”
A long silence passed before another Sound Transmission came.
“You would do well to mind your words and actions.”
The voice was as soft as a cat’s paw.
But the listener could feel the cold, razor-sharp blade beneath it.
“Let me apologize once more.”
“Let’s end things here for today. If a problem arises, I’ll come see you again soon.”
The conversation ended there.
The other person vanished without a sound or trace.
They’re like ghosts.
Sometimes, he wondered what their true identities were. How strong were they? Who were their members?
But he soon shook his head.
Such curiosity would only shorten my life.
He had endured years of hardship to reap the fruit. He couldn’t let mere curiosity ruin his plans.
It truly has been a long time.
The shadow reached toward the moon. Faint moonlight slipped between his fingers, illuminating his silver beard.
Soon... everything will return to its rightful place.
The Head Elder smiled with delight.

chapters.title: Chapter 28
paragraphs: Hoo.
I sat cross-legged and evened out my breathing. The breath I exhaled still carried qi I hadn’t managed to gather.
What a waste.
Circulating qi meant drawing in energy from outside, cycling it together with my internal energy, and accumulating it. But only a small amount remained in my body.
Most of it returned to nature.
In novels, you could shoot up just by doing a little of this.
The greatest martial arts under heaven? An elixir of the ages?

Not here. The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was Peak-grade, but it was hopeless at accumulating internal energy. And elixirs? Bullshit. I hadn’t even gotten a look at one. All I’d done was suffer like hell.
Is that my only hope?
Another mass of internal energy crouched in a corner of my dantian. If I could make all of it mine, it would be a huge help in the fights ahead.
The problem was that no matter how many times I tried, it wouldn’t budge.
Move. Move!
As if the thing that had sat there like a boulder this whole time was going to start moving. I tried drawing up my internal energy, but it gave me nothing. I sighed and got to my feet.
“Are we leaving?”
Hyuk Mujin had been watching our surroundings.
“Yeah.”
“Understood.”
Then he briskly got the reconnaissance squad ready and scooped Soyul into his arms. I stared at him in disbelief.
What the hell did this bastard eat?
Why had he suddenly gotten so efficient?
This was the guy who used to move only when I shoved a fist in his face. Somehow, he seemed like a different person.
Not that I’m complaining.
I shoved the stray thoughts aside and slung Gong Yacheong onto my back. As the poisoning worsened, his face had turned a dark blue.
Hyuk Mujin asked worriedly, “Will he be all right?”
“He has to be.”
I’d already done everything I could. All that remained was to hope Gong Yacheong held on. I muttered to the unconscious man.
“Not much farther. Just hold on a little longer.”
Sunlight squeezed through the dim dawn. I took a long stride toward it.
No—I started to.
- Awoooooo!
At first, I thought it was the wind. But those were the cries of living beasts. Hyuk Mujin muttered,
“The wolves must be hungry.”
“Wolves?”
“Of course. It’s hardly strange for there to be wild animals in the mountains.”
This was a game set in ancient China. It wouldn’t be strange for wolves or tigers to leap out from anywhere. I’d heard wild animals crying more than once over the past few days.
But...
Something feels off.
This wasn’t like the others. Just hearing those howls made my chest tighten and my fingertips tingle.
The gut I’d honed over seven years seemed to whisper. Something was beyond that forest, where the sunlight hadn’t reached yet.
“Prepare for battle.”
“Then we’re leaving now... Huh?”
“Form a defensive formation.”
Hyuk Mujin quickly recovered and relayed my order. Three reconnaissance squad members carrying shields clad in thin iron blocked the snow-covered path.
A narrow trail and the high ground atop a hill. We had the advantage.
- Awoooooo!

“Then that’s even better.”
“Won’t this delay us too long?”
I shook my head. We’d been fleeing for two full days. If this brief pause was what got us caught, then it was fate.
“Hold. We’ll wait a little longer.”

“Doesn’t sound like one or two.”
Hyuk Mujin glanced at my face.

No sooner had he finished than the pack emerged. Maybe they hadn’t been able to find prey in winter; most of them were so gaunt that their ribs showed. But they were still predators. We couldn’t let our guard down.

- Grrrrr...

“D-don’t tell me it’s that?”
That ability that could terrify enemies—and even knock them unconscious—with qi alone.

“We finally meet.”

Not even me.
When the hell did he...?

If he hadn’t spoken first—if the Quest Window hadn’t appeared—I would have turned around without ever knowing he was there.
The wolves.

I already knew his name.
“Jopil?”

Jin Wikyung, Wipeng, and the Head Elder. All three looked the part. Jopil, One Question, One Kill, did not.
He looks ordinary.
He wasn’t a giant like Jin Wikyung, didn’t have sharp eyes like Wipeng, and hadn’t grown a silver beard like the Head Elder.
Jopil was of average height with an unremarkable face—and that made him look even more dangerous.
“Nice to meet you.”
The instant Jopil smiled brightly and stepped forward, I sprang back without a second thought.
“Nimble. Good reactions, too. I like you.”
My heart hammered. Maybe it was the tension, but my voice came out hoarse.
“Don’t come any closer.”
“Sorry about that. I was so happy to see you that I got carried away.”
I wasn’t happy at all.
“Don’t be so tense. I only want to talk.”
“Talk?”
“Yes. I’ve been wanting to meet you.”
From Jopil’s perspective, he probably had. He’d lost twenty men just a few days ago.
Fuck. I’m fucked.
The thought of a master like that chasing me day and night for two days just to tear me apart made my stomach turn.
“Don’t give me that bullshit, Jopil!”
When I shouted, I felt the air freeze behind me. Jopil smiled as though he already knew what I was doing.
“What difference will telling them who I am make? Second Rate, Third Rate. They’re all idiots and trash.”
He’d read the reconnaissance squad’s level exactly. I almost wondered if he was using the System too.
“Why don’t we have a brief conversation? There’s a great deal I want to ask you.”
“A conversation? You’re not just buying time?”
“Buying time? What do you mean?”
“You know what I mean. You’re waiting for your men.”
As if I’d hit the mark, the bridge of Jopil’s nose twitched. Right. I didn’t know why, but he was alone. If I was willing to take a few losses, it might be enough to...
“Waiting? Me? For those pathetic weaklings?”
“...What?”
“Didn’t I already tell you? They’re all idiots and trash. Hopeless lives without effort or talent.”
“Black Mountain Blade was decent enough, but he had no eye for people, so he deserved to die. I ripped his eyes open before I left. Punishment for failing to recognize a master.”
Correction. Jopil, One Question, One Kill, didn’t merely look dangerous.
He was one fucking dangerous bastard.
This guy’s completely insane.
I’d never met anyone like Jopil, either in real life or in a game. That utterly nonchalant tone and manner. He treated people like tools. A psychopath.
“Anyway, what you’re worried about won’t happen. They’re painfully slow. It’ll take them half a shichen to catch up. By then, everything will be over.”
One thing was certain. In the ending Jopil had in mind, his own death wasn’t part of it.
“Well?”
“And if I refuse?”
Jopil smiled softly.
“I’ll be disappointed in you. Very disappointed.”
I could more or less picture what would happen if he was disappointed.
“Junior, I bear you no grudge. No—if anything, I’m rather fond of you. Answer a few questions truthfully, and I may even let you go.”
“Wait. Let me go?”
“Yes. I won’t harm you in any way. I’ll send you back in one piece.”
“...Really?”
“I’ll stake my neck on it. Is that enough?”
Sincerity showed on Jopil’s face. Unpredictable psychopath or not, maybe there was a chance we could all make it out alive.
“All right.”
Even if the worst came, all I could do was fight. I’d buy a little time and try to read his openings.
“Good. A friend who listens to reason, hahaha.”
Jopil clapped and laughed. The scabbard hanging at his left hip swayed.
Right-handed. Swordsman.
I continued filing away information in my head.
“First, I’d like to ask your age.”
“Twenty.”
Jopil’s eyes widened.
“My. That realm at twenty. Impressive.”
I’d spent seven years as a Hunter without ever escaping F-rank, yet here in the game, I was treated like a martial arts genius. It was a strange feeling.
“Judging by your clothes, you seem to be from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
I nodded readily.
“Supreme First Rate at twenty. You wouldn’t be that famous Heaven Shaking Sword, so... your name?”
“Jin Taekyung.”
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung. I’ve heard that name somewhere. Ah!”
After mulling it over, Jopil exclaimed.
“The wastrel Third Young Master! That’s you?”
“Not a wastrel. These days, they call me the Hidden Dragon.”
“Puhahaha! I knew it. The straitlaced Jin Family of Taiyuan, resorting to poison? As if. I don’t know who set all this up, but things are getting interesting.”
Jopil regarded me with satisfaction.
“I’d already heard plenty of rumors about you. Was all of that a disguise?”
“...Something like that.”
“Good. A hidden blade, then. I like it. When did you begin learning martial arts?”
“Seven years ago.”
It wasn’t entirely a lie. By Murim standards, a Hunter’s combat methods were a kind of martial art too.
“Seven years. And your master?”
“Don’t have one.”
“No master?”
He studied me for a while, then said,
“Doesn’t seem like a lie.”
“You promised to spare me if I answered honestly. That was your promise, wasn’t it?”
“Yes, it was. What an absurd yet fascinating story. A direct descendant of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, with no master, reaching that realm at twenty... My, my.”
My mouth was bone-dry. I gripped the spear and scanned Jopil’s body. The openings on him right now were unbelievable. But was what I was seeing really all there was?
He could be baiting me into attacking first.
The thought went no further. Jopil suddenly burst out laughing.
“Hahaha! Good. I like it. I’ll keep my promise.”
He’d keep his promise?
The thing I’d thought impossible was actually happening. I stared at him blankly.
“No need to look at me like that. Truthfully, I wanted very badly to kill you at first... But now that we’ve met, I find myself wanting to watch you a little longer.”
Jopil continued, his voice brimming with goodwill.
“It would be a shame to kill such outstanding talent. Especially under the current circumstances.”
“What circumstances?”
“Ah, you may not know yet. You’ll find out once you return. Go on, then. I hope you’ll have grown a little more by the next time we meet.”
I could go? He meant it?
I backed away without lowering my guard. Jopil merely watched me with a smile.
He looked like a fisherman releasing a minnow.
They say even if you enter a tiger’s den, you’ll survive as long as you keep your wits about you.
Who would have thought Jopil’s unpredictability would become my way out?
Once I’d put a safe distance between us, the breath I’d been holding rushed out. But there was no time to catch it. I had to get out of there even one second sooner.
“We’re moving. Hurry!”
Then—
“Hold on, Junior.”
Jopil looked at me in puzzlement.
“What are you doing?”
“What do you mean? Going back, like you promised...”
“I only gave you permission to leave. Alone.”
“...What?”
“I may not look it, but I’m in someone’s employ. I have to complete the mission I was given.”
The mission. Don’t tell me...
“The three survivors of the Sakju Branch. And those pieces of trash you call your subordinates. Leave them behind. I should be paid for two days’ work, don’t you think?”
His eyes, clear as a child’s, flashed. The next instant, they became the eyes of a predator.
“I’ll warn you now. If you refuse, I’ll be very disappointed.”

I stared blankly at Jopil, the reconnaissance squad, the young siblings, and the dying Gong Yacheong. There was little time, but my mind churned through the decision dozens of times before one answer finally burst out.
“Then be disappointed, you fucking bastard.”
Jopil laughed savagely.

paragraphs: Some people never hesitate once they’ve made a decision. Jopil was one of them.
“Let’s see what you’ve got.”
With that casual remark, Jopil kicked off the ground. More than ten zhang vanished in two steps. A flash burst from his waist.
Whoosh!
What the...?
My body moved before I could think. The instant my outstretched spear shaft met that flash—
Boom!
The impact hurled me backward with a thunderous crash. I flew toward the reconnaissance squad like a cannonball. Shields be damned—the three or four men at the front went down in a heap.
“Argh!”
“Captain! Are you all right?”
...Would I be all right?
Holy shit.
I gripped the spear shaft, which was still trembling from the impact.
The flash had been Jopil’s sword. It was the fastest, strongest attack I had faced in all twenty-seven years of my life.
It hit that hard even though I blocked it?
If I’d reacted even a moment later, I would have been hiking up Mount Beimang by now. I steadied my pounding heart and rose to my feet.
Jopil was smiling.
“I’m disappointed. Is that all you’ve got?”
The only reason I had been able to block it was because it was merely “that much.” If I hadn’t leveled up after mowing down those twenty men, I might already have been dead.
Fuck. Wrong opponent.
My realm was Second Rate. Even so, I had easily beaten two First Rate masters so far—with the martial arts and stats I’d gained through the System, and with the combat experience I’d accumulated.
But I could tell from that one attack.
This guy is different.
I felt outmatched in every way. Jopil was on a completely different level from Lee Seogeun or Black Mountain Blade.
So different that the word death came to mind.
“You’re afraid.”
Afraid? Me?
I looked at my hand. The spear had stopped vibrating, but the hand gripping it was shaking like an aspen leaf. My heartbeat was so loud it felt as though everyone could hear it.
“How do you expect to survive the storms of the martial world with such a timid heart?”
Jopil clicked his tongue.
“This won’t do. Let me give you a little encouragement.”
“What?”
“Anger always overcomes fear.”
Before I could understand what he meant, Jopil flicked his sleeve. Several streaks of light shot out at once.
Danger!
The instant a red alert blared in my head, I swung my spear.
Clang!
Several throwing knives ricocheted away with a sharp ring.
But I couldn’t stop them all.
“Guh.”
One of the reconnaissance squad clutched his throat. Blood fountained between his fingers, and I saw a throwing knife buried there.
“Grrk. Cap... Captain. Grrk.”
He dropped to his knees, gurgling on blood. His still-boyish face was twisted with the terror of dying.
“P-please, save me...”
Whoosh! Thunk!
No one survived throwing knives to the throat and between the eyes.
Neither did he.
Splat.
He fell face-first onto the ground, which had only just begun to thaw, and never rose again.
It had all happened in an instant.
“I chose him because he looked the youngest... Was he a cherished subordinate?”
I shook my head.
“No.”
“That’s a shame.”
“I don’t even know his name.”
“And you call him your subordinate?”
“He’s an NPC. I don’t need to know his name or his age.”
“What?”
I rolled the corpse onto his back. After brushing the dirt and snow from his face, I closed his staring eyes.
Then, as if making a confession, I told the still-bewildered Jopil the truth.
“We only met three days ago.”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah.”
“Then...”
Jopil smiled as he continued.
“Why are you angry?”
He was right. Something was boiling up from the pit of my stomach. My head and chest burned so hot that I had to say something.
What was that kid’s name again?

He was Number Seven in the reconnaissance squad. I’d forced him to carry a shield even though he hadn’t wanted to, and I’d trained him whenever I got the chance. He was young enough that a few words of praise always made him grin from ear to ear.
What was his name?
I couldn’t remember.
I didn’t even know the names of everyone who lived in my goshiwon. Why would I remember some NPC I’d only known for a few days? I had no reason to. No need.
But...
I was annoyed.
I was furious.
I’d thought things would be different in a game, but even here, I had failed to protect one of my teammates.
The whole reason I had trained him so hard, all the effort of the past few days—it had vanished like foam. I opened my mouth and breathed out hot air.
“You son of a bitch. You’re dead.”
I chewed and swallowed my last fasting pill.
A System message announced that my energy had recovered.
Boom!
I kicked off the ground and launched myself forward.
Jopil knocked aside the spearhead surging up from his blind spot.
Clang! Skrrratch!
Fast and powerful. His fundamentals were solid, and he had a keen sense for combat.
He was beyond the likes of that brat from the Mount Heng Sword Sect or a rootless wandering martial artist like Black Mountain Blade.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan... Even rotten, a Chinese herring is still a Chinese herring, is that it?
Jopil leisurely slipped past the spearhead as he considered the young man before him.

The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s decline was nothing new. The prestige that had once dominated Shanxi Province had long since faded. All that remained was the dim glory of the past and the rare talent that appeared once in a blue moon.
Someone like Jin Taekyung.
They’ve raised an interesting one.
Such skill at twenty. He was not yet a match for the Heaven Shaking Sword, who was already hailed as the greatest master in Shanxi Province, but he was certainly intriguing.

Age aside, his internal energy and martial arts were both middling... but he knew how to fight. He knew exactly when to retreat and when to advance, and whenever an opportunity appeared, he charged in like a fighting demon.
Just as he was doing now.
“Ha!”
Whoosh—Boom!
The spearhead flashed toward Jopil’s face and pierced empty air. The explosive crack sent his hair flying.
Well, look at this.

Every motion from gripping the spear to thrusting it was compact and flowed seamlessly into the next. More striking still was the way Jin Taekyung smoothly twisted his entire body before releasing an explosive burst of force.
Silk-reeling force.
It was still clumsy, but there was no mistaking it.
Silk-reeling force at twenty?
An innate feel for combat. Experience reminiscent of an old veteran of the martial world. And talent.
His potential was frightening.
Just as Jopil reached that conclusion, Jin Taekyung muttered with a stiff expression,
“Fuck, what the hell is this?”
Jopil stumbled over his own feet.
The instant he thought ah, shit, Jin Taekyung’s spear slid in like a snake. He hopped back and opened the distance, but the internal energy on that spear was no joke.
Riiip!
It was the first attack Jopil had allowed through. His robe split open in a long gash, baring his chest.
“Ah, so close. I could’ve finished it.”
So close? Finished it? Against me—Jopil, One Question, One Kill?
As Jin Taekyung smacked his lips in disappointment, Jopil felt rage surge through him.
“Youuu bastard!”
His shout, laden with internal energy, shook the forest. His eyes rolled back as he charged at Jin Taekyung.
The instant I sliced open Jopil’s robe, a System notification rang.
Ding.
System Lv.??? Jopil enters Berserk! Strength and Agility increase for the duration!
Damn it. Even more?
“Graaaaah!”
Boom! Boom!
Blow after blow crashed down with a thunderous roar. The ground erupted, and trees were torn out by the roots.
With his eyes rolled completely white, Jopil rampaged like a madman.
The problem is, he’s no ordinary madman.
He was a madman who also happened to be a Peak master. If not for the Gambler Title, which increased my combat stats by ten percent in a one-on-one fight, I wouldn’t have lasted this long.
Boom!
That wasn’t martial arts.
It was a bombardment.
But Jopil’s attacks had lost all precision. His movements were normally compact and fast, but the excessive strength from Berserk made them wider and left him full of openings.
I only need him to show me one...
The problem was, I couldn’t find it.
He had completely lost his mind and was laying waste to everything around him. Dodging was all I could manage. Blocking was out of the question.
Step into range and I would be shredded. That much was obvious.
“Captain!”
“We’re coming!”
I hurriedly waved off the reconnaissance squad members charging toward me.
“Hey, don’t come over here! Don’t come! Fall back!”
Had they lost their minds? Coming here?
We had already lost one man for nothing. I didn’t want the entire reconnaissance squad wiped out.
Besides...
If those guys come over here, the Gambler Title’s effect disappears!
Gambler only worked in a one-on-one fight.
I was barely hanging on as it was. If I lost the Title’s effect too, I had no idea how much longer I could last.
“Get back, you bastards!”
I shouted and hurled myself sideways. Right on cue, Jopil’s sword smashed the ground apart.
Crunch!
“Captain!”
Hyuk Mujin’s shout came a beat too late. Despite my warning, he was already charging in. Behind him, I saw Han Yeop’s grim, determined face.
“Hey, don’t—!”
“Jopil, you vicious bastard!”
“Get away from the Captain!”
But they were already too late. Hyuk Mujin and Han Yeop, who had sprinted over with everything they had, thrust their weapons at Jopil while his attention was still on me.
“Die!”
Sword and spear. Spear and sword.
Their timing was excellent, and their attacks worked together as if they had practiced them beforehand.
There was only one problem.
They had the wrong opponent.
“How dare you, you rats!”
Jopil reacted instantly. He planted his sword in the ground, spun around, and struck both weapons with his bare hands.
Facing a sword and spear empty-handed was suicide.
But this was Murim.
More precisely, Jopil was a Peak master.
Crack—Crunch!
His palm merely brushed the side of Hyuk Mujin’s blade, yet the sword shattered before it could even reach him. Han Yeop stared in horror at his own spear, its head sliced clean off.
That was the result of Jopil’s rigid knife-hand.
“What the...”
“That’s impossi—”
Before they could finish, Jopil slammed both hands into their chests.
They smashed into trees, spraying fountains of blood.
“I’ll kill you.”
The whites of his eyes had vanished from his chillingly smiling face.
Berserk had worn off. He had regained his senses.
“Fuck...”
One disaster after another. Mountains beyond mountains. Enemies on every side.
Jopil, you son of a bitch.
The situation kept spiraling toward the worst possible outcome. If anyone was going to stop him, it had to be me.
“Jopil—!”
The internal energy I drew up with all my strength raced through my body. I kicked off the ground and shot toward him.
Jopil grinned broadly.
“Right. I’ll kill you first.”
But I had one thing to count on.
He’s empty-handed right now.
That was the mistake he’d made while Berserk. And I was certain I could end this before he pulled the sword from behind him and swung it.
In the next instant, I dragged up every last bit of internal energy in my dantian. I focused all of it into a single point—the tip of my spear—and thrust.
“Die!”
The final form of the Jin Family’s Spear Technique.
Sky-Piercing Strike.
If it could pierce the heavens, why couldn’t it pierce Jopil’s heart?
I was certain.
This is... the end.
The world slowed, and I saw Jopil’s face.
He was smiling.
The instant I saw that smile, I realized it.
Something was wrong.
Skrrrng!
Jopil’s sword was faster than my spear.
The blood-soaked crimson blade shoved the spear shaft aside and drove inward. The instant my spearhead, laden with internal energy, pierced empty air—
Slash!
A chilling sound rang out, and my chest suddenly felt cool.
Then came the searing pain and a burst of blood.
Fortunately, I had jerked back at the last instant and avoided a fatal wound.
Damn it.
What the hell had just happened?
As I staggered backward, Jopil rushed me.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Crimson sword-light poured down. Every flash was so fast and strong I could barely see it.
I gritted my teeth and swung my spear, but Jopil surpassed me in both momentum and martial arts.
Slash! Thunk! Splurt!
Lightning tore across my body. The blade stabbed my shoulder, slashed my knee, and pierced my side before pulling free in a spray of blood.
“Guh.”
“You still haven’t dropped your weapon. I’ll give you that.”
Jopil added,
“If you survive this too.”
The next instant, his hand slammed into my chest.
