chapters.title: Chapter 30
paragraphs: Whoosh.
The instant Jopil’s red-hot palm struck my chest, lava-hot qi swept through me. My breath caught, and my internal energy surged backward.
What is this?
The question crossed my mind as I went flying. I bounced and rolled for more than ten zhang before finally coming to a stop.
“Cough.”
Blood trickled down my chin. Every so often, unidentified chunks came up with it. They were... fuck. Pieces of my organs.
He got me good.
Through my blurred vision, I saw Jopil walking toward me. His unhurried stride carried the ease of a victor.
I have to get up.
I groped beside me until my hand closed around a cool spear shaft. Using the spear as a cane, I barely managed to stand—and found Jopil staring at me with narrowed eyes.
“You can still stand after taking a Flame Divine Palm at seventy percent power... What a troublesome junior.”
Wham!
Another palm strike slammed into me.
The Flame Divine Palm was every bit as powerful as its name. My shirt burned away, and my flesh melted and sloughed off. The heat that invaded my body tore through my meridians one after another.
“Guh.”
Horrific pain crashed over me. Instead of writhing in agony, I thrust my spear at Jopil’s vital point.
Thunk.
“You’re like a fighting dog.”
Jopil snatched the spear shaft and clicked his tongue.
“Someone at your level can’t do anything to me.”
“Go... fuck yourself!”
The next instant, I let go of the spear and threw myself into his chest.
This was my last chance. I focused every bit of internal energy into a single point. If I could strike one of his vital points, I could turn the tables.
But...
“Gasp.”
The result was disastrous.
I had forced up my internal energy without regard for my internal injuries. I collapsed on the spot, trembling as if I’d been struck by lightning.
Drool ran from the corner of my mouth.
“Pfft. Puhahaha! Have you ever seen such a stupid bastard!”
Jopil howled with laughter and snapped off the spearhead.
“Well? What now? Huh? Youngest Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
Now I didn’t even have a weapon. Despair darkened my vision.
Am I going to die like this?
In the past seven years, death had never felt this close. I had fought more than a thousand times and survived. Was I really going to die here, of all places?
This pointlessly?
No. I can’t die like this...
I reached out, but that was as far as I got.
“Captain!”
A shout crackling with static was the last thing I heard before all light vanished.
When I opened my eyes again, I was in neither heaven nor hell. I was drenched in sweat and panting, my whole body as heavy as waterlogged cotton.
A dream? Or my life flashing before my eyes?
Whatever it was, one thing was certain. This was the past—a memory from seven years ago. The familiar face of the training instructor was proof enough.
“You... What did you...”
The instructor couldn’t finish. He was staring at a steel training dummy modeled after a monster.
Now it looked more like scrap metal, bent and split all over.
“Was that a skill just now?”
My younger self answered in an exhausted voice.
“Thrust with All My Might.”
“Thrust with All My Might?”
“Yes. I just thrust as hard as I could.”
“You don’t know how you’re doing it, but you started using it naturally after you Awakened?”
“Uh, yes. That’s right.”
“That’s a skill, you idiot.”
Looking dumbfounded, the instructor turned to the file in his hand.
“Jin Taekyung. Twenty years old. Lives in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province. F-rank Awakened. Is this you?”
“Yes. So, my full-power thrust—no, my skill. It’s good, right?”
“You’re asking if it’s good?”
The instructor let out a hollow laugh.
“I’ve been at this training center for fifteen years, and I’ve never seen anything like it. That kind of destructive power shouldn’t appear below D-rank.”
“Fuck, I knew it. Instructor, I’m leaving.”
“What?”
“I’m going to get reassessed. Honestly, that should be enough for E-rank, at least.”
“No. I think they assessed you correctly.”
“What?”
“The skill itself is incredible. It’s far beyond anything an F-rank should be capable of. But...”
The instructor scratched the back of his head.
“You can’t use it.”
“Why? Why not?”
“Your body can’t keep up. That skill is beyond what F-rank mana and physical ability can handle. That’s why you collapse after using it once.”
“But I’m fine.”
“Are you?”
Before I could even nod, the instructor’s hand shot out like lightning and tapped me on the chest.
Literally just a tap. But I’d used up all my strength, so I toppled flat onto my back.
My whole body throbbed. I could barely move a finger.
“You’re already putting out more power than your body can handle. Eventually, it won’t end with a little soreness.”
“...Is there another way?”
“Solid fundamentals. Excellent technique. And your own combat sense. If you want to live a long life, don’t use that skill. Ah, except under special circumstances.”
“Special circumstances?”
The instructor grinned and added,
“When your life is in danger. That skill might save you once.”
The next instant, I opened my eyes on the cold snowfield.
“Captain!”
The last shout I’d heard now rang clear. So did the sharp pain from my mangled body.
I’m still alive.
My life had flashed before my eyes in a mere instant. Jopil had turned to look behind him, close enough for me to touch if I reached out.
“They’re certainly loyal. Their skills are pathetic, though.”
The reconnaissance squad was charging toward us in a cluster.
“I’m thinking of tearing them apart. What do you say?”
“...been fighting...”
“What?”
“Like an idiot... fighting...”
I mumbled again. Jopil bent down, irritation on his face.
“Can’t you even speak properly?”
“I said I’ve been fighting like an idiot this whole time.”
Ptoo!
The moment I’d been waiting for.
I spat the blood I’d gathered into his face. At the same time, my hand—already moving half a beat ahead—slammed down toward his foot.
Inventory Open.
Jopil didn’t know.
I was a Hunter, a man of Murim, and a player who could use the System!
Equip Dagger.
A solid weight filled my empty hand. His face covered in blood, Jopil tried to jerk back, but the dagger had already punched through the top of his foot.
Shunk!
“Guh.”
Even a Peak master was still human.
His body froze at the sudden pain. I released the dagger and reached for his ankle.
Equip Dagger.
My Inventory was piled with weapons taken from the enemies I’d killed since the Tutorial. Swords, spears, axes, daggers... more than twenty in all.
Jopil’s men had been walking armories.
Slice.
“Gaaah!”
His Achilles tendon.
The instant I severed the tendon at his ankle, a scream burst from him. As his stance collapsed, I rolled aside, slashing and stabbing until his remaining left leg was soaked in blood as well.
Slice. Thrust. Thrust. Stab-stab-stab!
Jopil’s mouth opened wide in rage and pain.
“Gaaaaah! You son of a bitch!”
Both his legs were useless, but Jopil was still a Peak master. He spun like lightning, slipped past my dagger, caught my wrist, and twisted.
Crack.
“Gah!”
His attack didn’t end there.
A red-hot palm.
The Flame Divine Palm.
Boom.
My chest caved in. My vision went white as powerful fire qi tore through my body.
Boom.
The strength drained from me.
I heard the bones in my neck grind out of place under Jopil’s grip. His chilling voice slid into my ear.
“Now you understand, don’t you? Who you dared lay a hand on.”
“...Cough.”
“If King Yama asks, tell him I sent you.”
As I hung limp as a corpse, Jopil declared with rapture written across his face,
“Die.”
His final Flame Divine Palm shot toward my chest. Lava-hot power capable of swallowing my life whole burned within that crimson palm.
And at last...
Tap.
The world stopped.
There was no lava. No heat of any kind.
Only his battered, callused palm resting against my chest.
A ripple ran through Jopil’s eyes.
The grip around my throat went slack. As Jopil staggered backward, I saw the dagger below his navel, buried deep in his dantian.
“What... What the hell is this?”
The next instant, blood ran down his chin.
That was only the beginning.
Blood began pouring from his eyes, nose, and ears as well—a waterfall streaming from all seven orifices.
The reconnaissance squad stopped in their tracks at the horrifying sight. Someone muttered as if groaning.
“Qi deviation...”
Internal energy was a double-edged sword.
I had waited for the moment Jopil drew his internal energy to its peak, then driven a dagger summoned from my Inventory into his dantian.
The result was a violent reversal of internal energy.
Qi deviation.
“You were definitely empty-handed.”
I answered wearily.
“Live long enough, and all sorts of things happen.”
“I can’t die like this. This makes no sense.”
Jopil muttered like a man who had lost his mind, stumbling forward one step at a time.
Pools of blood formed wherever he passed.
“I am Jopil. Jopil, One Question, One Kill. The nineteenth-generation successor of the Fire Gate Clan. I am not someone who should die at the hands of a nobody like you!”
A chilling, ghostly aura radiated from him as he screamed, drenched in blood. Even the reconnaissance squad members who had charged in ready to die trembled in fear.
“Then why? Why, at the likes of you, would I—!”
That was when the ember I’d thought extinguished burst into flame.
The change began in Jopil’s body. His bleeding stopped, and blue veins bulged all over him. He looked as if he could no longer feel the pain of his severed tendons—or even the qi deviation.
Terrible heat poured from every breath.
What is this?
A literal resurrection?
No. This was Jopil’s last desperate struggle.
Everyone around me screamed in terror, but I could see it clearly. His hair was turning white by the second. His skin was shriveling.
Right now, he was...
Burning away his life.
He means to kill me, at least, before he goes.
This was power gained by sacrificing the most precious thing he had, and every bit of it was aimed at me. I knew instinctively that I couldn’t dodge.
Can I do this? Me?
I picked up the fallen spear.
The Sharp Spear I’d used ever since the Tutorial.
Its spearhead had been broken off. Now it was nothing more than a pointed iron rod.
I’ll end up looking like this soon enough.
I had only one option left.
Even if it worked, there was no guarantee I’d survive. But I had no time to hesitate.
“Jin Taekyung!”
“Yeah. Let’s finish this.”
Me and Jopil.
Jopil and me.
We shot toward each other. The heat pouring off him melted the piled snow and dried my lips. I drew a long breath.
Sss. Hoo.
The noise around me receded. My heartbeat and breathing thundered in my ears.
Thump. Thump-thump. Thump-thump-thump.
My heartbeat reached its peak. My breathing fell into place with mechanical precision.
I knew.
Now.
At that instant, I awakened the internal energy in my dantian. Inside my body, where my qi and blood pathways lay twisted and ruined, only one source of internal energy remained.
The third, hardened like rock.
My only option—and the last piece that would fill my Skill.
Run wild as you please.
The awakened energy went berserk. It forced its way through my ruined pathways and surged throughout my body. Mind-numbing pain struck me.
But the new strength flooding through me soon made me forget it.
Go!
Every muscle in my body pulled taut. From my calves and thighs, through my waist and along my thrusting arm, every last bit of my strength and internal energy surged forward.
Condensed air burst from the broken spear tip.
Matching it, Jopil thrust out his Flame Divine Palm.
“Dieeeee!”
Whoooosh.
A mound of snow erupted with the wind. Through the flakes drifting gently back down, Jopil came into view.
His right arm, the one that had unleashed the Flame Divine Palm, was gone. So were his shoulder and side.
Half his upper body had evaporated.
“What kind of martial art...?”
I dropped the spear and answered.
“Thrust with All My Might.”
The next instant, heaven and earth flipped.
Beyond my blurring vision, Jopil’s already lifeless head shot high into the sky.
Socheon was crying out loud, holding a sword as tall as he was.

chapters.title: Chapter 31
paragraphs: “Well, look at you. Must be nice.”
I slowly opened my eyes to a familiar face.
“Did you come here for a picnic? Who sleeps in the middle of a Gate?”
I must have dozed off. I shamelessly denied it.
“I wasn’t sleeping. Who says I was?”
“Wipe the drool off your mouth before you start lying.”
“Tch.”
“Oh, you little—”
He shook a fist at me, but a smile tugged at the corners of his mouth. I rubbed my stiff neck.
“Ugh, I’m tired.”
“Did you meet a woman yesterday? Why are you nodding off like a sick chicken even in the middle of a raid?”
“When would I have time to meet a woman? You know my situation.”
“True enough.”
We’d been through thick and thin together for five years, ever since our first battle. He knew me as well as I knew him.
“Then what’s wrong?”
“What do you think? Money.”
“Money? Don’t tell me you’re moonlighting.”
His voice dropped. I looked past his shoulder at the team members resting nearby and nodded.
“Well, well. This bastard gets a little experience under his belt and starts lining his pockets on the side. And you call yourself the vice team leader.”
“Raids have been scarce lately, and I’m strapped. Really strapped. You’ve done it yourself, hyung, so don’t give me that.”

Hunters with professional licenses were legally barred from taking second jobs. A D-rank Hunter probably wouldn’t have to live like this, but F-ranks like us had no choice. The Guild knew how things were, so they looked the other way even when they found out.
“True, but... be careful. If someone files a complaint with the Management Agency, you’ll have a real mess on your hands.”
“It’s a trustworthy place. They pay cash the same day, so there’s no problem. You think I’d risk it otherwise?”
“Really?”
Judging by his expression, he was tempted.
“Do you need money too, hyung?”
“I’ve got three kids. I need an oil well to spring up in my yard.”

Misery filled his eyes as the words poured out. I’d already heard this routine dozens of times. After railing against the hardships of raising children, the rising price of formula, and the shamelessness of merchants, he patted me on the shoulder.
“Don’t get married.”
“I won’t.”
More precisely, I couldn’t.
I had no woman and no money. My goal in life was to buy a house in a safe zone within five years, so deep down, I envied him.
A spouse I loved. Children. A happy family.
I had no idea when I’d ever have something like that.
“Marriage is a swamp.”
For all his talk, he was famous for being a devoted husband and a good father. I knew he sometimes took out his family photos and smiled fondly at them.
“It sucks your whole life in. By the time you come to your senses, you’re buried up to your chest and can barely breathe.”
Maybe I’d had the wrong idea about him.
“So don’t spend all your time working. Take breaks. Dating, hobbies—stuff like that’s good for you.”
“I don’t know. I still need the money.”
I scratched my head as I answered. He gave me a concerned look.
“I saw you sleeping earlier. You were drenched in cold sweat. Keep that up and you’ll drop dead from overwork.”
“Was I?”
Now that he mentioned it, my back was damp with cold sweat. I must have had a bad dream...
Can’t remember.
Probably just some stupid dream anyway.
A Gate.
These days, Gates provided a living for Hunters like me, but their true purpose was to serve as invasion routes for the armies of the Demon Realm.
When Demon King Asmodeus fell, his mighty army was routed with him. But even decades later, the Gates remained.
“Defensive formation!”
At his command, three Hunters carrying enormous tower shields blocked the path ahead. In a narrow cave, that alone was enough to stop most attacks.
Clang! Clang-clang!
“Giiiiik!”
Some twenty goblins hurled poison needles, axes, and spears, but every last one bounced off those big, beautiful tower shields.
“Archers!”
The tanks blocked every attack from the front while the archers rained arrows from the rear. As we pressed forward and took down nearly half of them, the goblins let out panicked shrieks.
“Gyaaaah!”
“Kieek!”
He gave the next order at exactly the right moment.
“Attack formation!”
The tanks dropped their tower shields and burst forward at the same time. I was faster.
“Hah!”

I swept the iron spear through a wide arc. Green blood burst into the air, and the front rank collapsed. I plunged into the gap, stabbing and slashing at everything within reach, and their formation crumbled.
“Charge!”
The damage dealers and tanks piled in. In moments, the goblin pack had become a heap of corpses.
“Pretty easy today, huh?”
“Honestly, the vice team leader did half the work. He was flying around out there. When did he get that good...? Shh. The Team Leader’s pissed.”
The team members chatting among themselves fell silent the moment he appeared.
“Hey, Jin Taekyung!”
That made me jump.
I’d been staring into space, lost in thought, and jerked in surprise.
“What?”
“Who told you to go off on your own? Are you a tank? Did you forget the attack order? And you still call yourself the vice team leader?”
“That’s not—”
“If you’re going to pull this kind of shit, transfer teams. You’re putting everyone else in danger.”
I looked at his grim face and sighed.
“I’m sorry. I don’t know why I did that. They just... suddenly didn’t seem like a big deal. I must have lost it for a second.”
It was a strange feeling. The instant I saw the goblin pack, I thought I could wipe them all out by myself.
No, it hadn’t been a thought.
It had been certainty.
He swallowed whatever he had been about to say. We’d had each other’s backs for five years, and this was the first time I’d ever done anything so reckless.
“Don’t do it again. If something’s bothering you, tell me.”
He patted my shoulder and walked away. As I watched him go, something in my chest throbbed.
Should I see a doctor?
But it wasn’t long before I stopped thinking about the pain altogether.
“Magic Gem!”
“Got one here!”
“Another!”
“It dropped! It dropped! It dropped!”
“Mom! Hayeon!”
Ah, that last shout was mine.
His face was flushed with excitement too as he muttered, “What the hell is all this...?”
Twenty Magic Gems of various sizes lay neatly arranged on the ground.

Magic Gems. They looked like red pebbles, but they were known as the flower of the Gate. These concentrations of magical power found inside monsters were a form of higher-dimensional energy—and the most valuable of all monster byproducts.
“At this rate, each one’s got to be worth over a million won.”
That came from the Team Leader, an E-rank Hunter who had survived ten years in this business. Everyone’s eyes went glassy at the intoxicating sight.
“Is it normally like this?”
At the new recruit’s question, everyone shook their heads emphatically.
“Absolutely not.”
An F-rank Gate yielded one or two on average. Even with incredible luck, you wouldn’t find five.
I was busy doing the math.
Twenty million won from the Magic Gems alone, another five million won for the byproducts and Equipment. Add all the various allowances and...
Fuck. How much is all this?
It was the biggest jackpot I’d hit since becoming a Hunter.
And the raid wasn’t even over yet.
“How far have we come?”
“We’re almost there. Turn right and the boss zone is just ahead.”
The words boss zone made everyone’s eyes light up.
It went without saying, but a boss zone contained a boss. The boss monster was the strongest monster in the Gate—and the one with the most expensive byproducts, Equipment, and Magic Gems.
What if we take down the boss monster too?
It would be a literal jackpot. The opportunity of a lifetime for an F-rank Hunter.
Everyone was beaming at the thought when he spoke.
“Wait. Let me think.”
What the hell was he saying?
“What do you mean?”
“Think about it. Every monster we’ve encountered has been an ordinary goblin, but we’ve found this many Magic Gems? Something’s wrong.”
He sighed. His face was still flushed with excitement, but now uncertainty clouded it.
“I know how you feel. I do... but we’ve already made a fortune. Let’s be satisfied with this and turn back.”
Satisfied?
Now? After coming this far, he wanted to turn back?
I looked at the other team members. Some of them had fought alongside me for two or three years. Others were new.
Every one of them wore the same expression I did.
“I’m against—”
My breath caught.
Damn it. The chest pain again.
I tried to continue, but no sound came out. Now my ears had started ringing too.
What is this?
The pain and the ringing grew worse. I dropped to my knees, gasping for breath.
Someone. Please, help me.
I grabbed someone’s pant leg and clung to it.
It was him. The man who had looked after me like a brother—and like a father—for the past five years.
Hyung. Please save me.
He looked down at me without emotion.
“Me? After you ran away and left everyone behind?”
What?
“I wanted to live too.”
I forgot the pain and stared up at him. His clothes and skin melted away, exposing bone.
Everyone but me had become skeletons, sprawled across the ground.
Ah. That’s right.
They had all died.
That day two years ago. In the boss zone I had insisted we enter, every one of them had died.
I was the only one who survived.
I floundered, drowning in the memories.
The ominous darkness hanging over the boss zone. The foul stench. The damp floor. That thing’s enormous wings.
Bodies ripped to pieces in midair.
Terrified screams.
People running for their lives.
You fucking bastard!
But even the Skill I poured everything into wasn’t enough to kill it. As I waited for death, he hauled me to my feet.
“Taekyung!”
“Hyung, I’m sorry. It was all my fault.”
If it hadn’t been for me—if I hadn’t gotten greedy—everyone could have survived.
They could have gone home to their families.
As I sobbed like a child, he forced himself to smile.
“How is that your fault? Look at this kid. Now you’re even trying to play Team Leader.”
The massive body drifted through the cave. Stalactites rained down, and the last member of the team let out a death cry. In the darkness, its red eyes turned toward us.

“Hyung. Cheonsu hyung!”

The ringing in my ears became a monster’s roar.
Kyaaaaau!
“Hyung—!”

“No. It was a nightmare.”
“Then I’ll leave that part out when I tell him.”
“Suit yourself.”

“Really?”
“Yes. When my lord heard, he flew into a rage. If I hadn’t stopped him, he would have beaten the Medicine King Hall Master to death.”
“Ah.”
I remembered the old man from the meeting a few days ago—the one who had threatened to drive a giant needle into the White Tiger Hall Leader’s anus.
So he’d practically been praying for me to die.
“Did anything else happen?”

“The good news.”
“First, the reconnaissance squad and the survivors of the Sakju Branch returned safely. Two of them suffered fairly serious injuries, but neither is in danger of dying.”
Survivors.
The word made my heart drop.
Number Seven.

He couldn’t have been more than twenty.
Far too young to die.

“What does that...”

sentences.text: “Well, look at you.
Must be nice.”
I slowly opened my eyes to a familiar face.
“Did you come here for a picnic?

I must have dozed off.
I shamelessly denied it.

“Tch.”

“When would I have time to meet a woman?

“True enough.”

He knew me as well as I knew him.
“Then what’s wrong?”
“What do you think?

“Money?

His voice dropped.
I looked past his shoulder at the team members resting nearby and nodded.
“Well, well.

And you call yourself the vice team leader.”
“Raids have been scarce lately, and I’m strapped.
Really strapped.
You’ve done it yourself, hyung, so don’t give me that.”
Hunters with professional licenses were legally barred from taking second jobs.
A D-rank Hunter probably wouldn’t have to live like this, but F-ranks like us had no choice.
The Guild knew how things were, so they looked the other way even when they found out.
“True, but... be careful.
If someone files a complaint with the Management Agency, you’ll have a real mess on your hands.”
“It’s a trustworthy place.
They pay cash the same day, so there’s no problem.
You think I’d risk it otherwise?”
“Really?”
Judging by his expression, he was tempted.
“Do you need money too, hyung?”
“I’ve got three kids.
I need an oil well to spring up in my yard.”
Misery filled his eyes as the words poured out.
I’d already heard this routine dozens of times.
After railing against the hardships of raising children, the rising price of formula, and the shamelessness of merchants, he patted me on the shoulder.
“Don’t get married.”
“I won’t.”
More precisely, I couldn’t.
I had no woman and no money.
My goal in life was to buy a house in a safe zone within five years, so deep down, I envied him.
A spouse I loved.
Children.
A happy family.
I had no idea when I’d ever have something like that.

For all his talk, he was famous for being a devoted husband and a good father.
I knew he sometimes took out his family photos and smiled fondly at them.
“It sucks your whole life in.
By the time you come to your senses, you’re buried up to your chest and can barely breathe.”
Maybe I’d had the wrong idea about him.
“So don’t spend all your time working.
Take breaks.
Dating, hobbies—stuff like that’s good for you.”
“I don’t know.
I still need the money.”
I scratched my head as I answered.
He gave me a concerned look.
“I saw you sleeping earlier.
You were drenched in cold sweat.
Keep that up and you’ll drop dead from overwork.”
“Was I?”
Now that he mentioned it, my back was damp with cold sweat.
I must have had a bad dream...
Can’t remember.
Probably just some stupid dream anyway.
A Gate.
These days, Gates provided a living for Hunters like me, but their true purpose was to serve as invasion routes for the armies of the Demon Realm.
When Demon King Asmodeus fell, his mighty army was routed with him.
But even decades later, the Gates remained.
“Defensive formation!”
At his command, three Hunters carrying enormous tower shields blocked the path ahead.
In a narrow cave, that alone was enough to stop most attacks.
Clang!

“Giiiiik!”
Some twenty goblins hurled poison needles, axes, and spears, but every last one bounced off those big, beautiful tower shields.

I looked at the other team members.

chapters.title: Chapter 32
paragraphs: “There was a major battle two days ago. One hundred elite fighters from our family clashed with two hundred vanguard troops from the Mount Heng Sword Sect in Honju.”
“There was a battle?”
And a major one, no less—hundreds of people thrown in. My heart lurched for a moment, but then I remembered what Wipeng had said earlier.
Good news and even better news. He’d already given away the outcome.
“We won.”
“It was a great victory. Fewer than thirty of them escaped alive. That’s about the same as our family’s total casualties.”
Judging by the scar running from Wipeng’s forehead to his chin, it must have been a fierce battle.
Well, of course. They outnumbered us two to one.
Still, it was a relief we’d won. From the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s perspective, we’d poured in nearly half our strength. If we’d lost, the damage would have been enormous.
“It’s unfortunate that we let the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s Lesser Family Head escape, but taking down the Mount Heng Twin Devils was a major gain.”
“The Mount Heng Fucking Devils?”

“The Mount Heng Twin Devils. They were Peak masters under the Mount Heng Sword Sect, and their loyalty was something else... They kept throwing themselves at us without regard for their lives, so we had no choice but to kill them.”
Wipeng tapped the fresh scar on his face.
“If we’d captured them alive, we could have extracted valuable information.”
“Did you—I mean, did Great Hero Wipeng kill them?”
“My lord and I took one each. They were pretty good.”
I was left speechless as Wipeng slurped his tea.
For fuck’s sake... Are Peak masters a joke to him?

That had been the fiercest fight of my twenty-seven years. I’d suffered every kind of internal injury and been carved up like a steak. Then I’d been unconscious for five days, so I’d practically taken a half-bath in the River Jordan.
And after taking down Peak masters of that caliber, all he had to say was that they were pretty good?
This guy’s a complete monster.
I learned something for certain this time: even Peak masters came in different levels. It was a huge relief that people of that caliber were on my side.
“That aside...”
Clink.
Wipeng set down his teacup and regarded me with an unreadable look.
“You were remarkable.”
“Pardon?”
“I’m talking about Jopil, One Question, One Kill. Even calling it remarkable doesn’t do justice to what you accomplished by defeating him.”
You people seem a lot more remarkable to me.
It felt like being praised by an A-rank Hunter for being good at killing goblins.
“Ah. Right. Thanks, I guess.”
I wanted to end the discussion about Jopil there. I was in lousy shape, my mood wasn’t much better, and I wanted to check all the System Rewards waiting for me.
Let me rest already. I’m still a patient, damn it.
I tried to convey that with a wink. Wipeng frowned.
“Does your eye hurt? Shall I call a physician?”
“...No. I’m fine.”
“Your eye just spasmed.”
“That wasn’t a spasm.”
“It was. I saw it clearly.”
“No, what I just did was...”
Then Wipeng rolled his eyes back until only the whites showed and started to tremble.
The table shook, and tea sloshed over the rim of his cup. I cried out in alarm.
“My God, Great Hero Wipeng!”
This guy has epilepsy. No—how does a Peak master even get epilepsy?
Just as I hurriedly tried to stand, the convulsions stopped. Wipeng returned to normal and spoke with perfect calm.
“That’s what you did.”
“Are you all ri—wait, what?”
“That’s what you did just now, Third Young Master. Your eye spasmed.”
“So you were imitating me?”
“Yes.”
What kind of lunatic is this...?
I tried to explain the difference between a wink and an epileptic fit, but the words stuck. Wipeng was glaring at me like a pissed-off dictator.
“...Why don’t we just finish talking about Jopil?”
“Let’s.”
Wipeng nodded in satisfaction.
Crazy bastard.
In the end, I had to tell him everything about my fight with Jopil from beginning to end.
How Jopil had moved. What martial arts he’d used. Wipeng’s incisive questions had me tensing up more than once.
“You severed the sinews and meridians in Jopil’s legs with a dagger?”
“Yes. I’d hidden it beforehand.”
“There’s no way Jopil would have failed to notice it... Continue.”
When the long story finally ended, Wipeng released the breath he’d been holding. The complicated look in his eyes said more than words could.
“Third Young Master, you have accomplished a truly great deed.”
“Ah, thank you...”
“I hate to admit it, but I mean that.”
“...Ah. Right.”
“When I think of all the trouble you’ve caused until now, my blood boils, but I was genuinely impressed. I mean that.”

“Who could have imagined that the Third Young Master who stole family funds day after day and poured them into pleasure houses, then paraded through the streets dead drunk and smeared shit all over the family’s reputation, would become such a great man? I, Wipeng, am genuinely in awe.”
Just curse me out, you bastard...
I barely held back the torrent of abuse threatening to burst out.
“I got lucky. Jopil let his guard down too.”
Wipeng shook his head.

“No. It was all skill. It makes no difference who let their guard down or who hid a dagger in advance. If that alone had been enough to kill Jopil, he would never have been Jopil, One Question, One Kill. Murim is a place where only the strong survive.”
“Only the strong survive.”
I quietly rolled the words over my tongue. They tasted somehow bitter and sweet at once.
Murim—this game—had been that kind of place from the beginning. I had survived there, and I had grown stronger.
“Jopil used every martial art at his disposal to its fullest. In the end, he even drew upon his innate qi. A Peak master threw away his own life in an attempt to kill you. But what was the result?”
“I won.”
“Yes. Exactly.”
“Then I was stronger than Jopil.”
Wipeng, who had looked vaguely displeased all this time, suddenly turned dead serious.
“What are you talking about? Jopil was stronger. Do Peak masters look like a joke to you?”
“You were only strong enough to kill Jopil with a surprise attack.”
Enough already. Seriously.
While I was debating whether to pull a weapon from my Inventory, Wipeng let out a short chuckle. It was the first time I had ever seen him laugh.
“Well done.”
I looked at Wipeng suspiciously.
“What are you going to add this time?”
His smile deepened.
“I mean it. It’s true I disliked you quite a lot, but... this time, I have no choice but to acknowledge you.”
When he put it that way, I had nothing to say. For some reason, I felt embarrassed and cleared my throat.
“Ahem. Well, I nearly died, but all I really did was take down Jopil and a few wandering martial artists. Ahem.”
“How many Peak masters do you think there are in a single city? Even across all of Shanxi, where our family is based, there are fewer than twenty.”
Twenty. Far fewer than I’d expected.
“The Mount Heng Sword Sect must have taken serious losses. They lost three Peak masters like that.”
“But the greatest blow lies elsewhere.”
“What is it?”
“That would be...”
The instant Wipeng opened his mouth, a trembling voice came from the doorway.
“Their pretext. They’ve lost the pretext they used to start this war. The Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan is more than strong enough without resorting to poison. Yes, indeed.”
The enormous Jin Wikyung stood in the doorway, teary-eyed and holding both arms wide open.
“My youngest!”
Please, just leave me alone.
In the end, I had to replay the chase of the past several days and my battle with Jopil all over again.
“The wandering martial artists who pursued the survivors...”
“Those bastards! I’ll tear them apart!”
Boom!
“Jopil’s Flame Divine Palm left me with internal injuries...”
“I’ll kill him! How dare that vicious wandering martial artist bastard! Even if I ripped out his guts and chewed them to a pulp, it wouldn’t be enough!”
Boom! Boom! Boom!
I stared blankly at the ruins of my bedroom. This was what Jin Wikyung’s excessive immersion in the story had wrought.
Wipeng had already backed far away and was mouthing something.
—It would be best not to bring that story up again.
For the first time, the two of us were in complete agreement.
Jin Wikyung huffed and puffed for a long while before finally calming dow—
“If that bastard had still been alive, he wouldn’t have died peacefully.”
Crunch.
I watched with sad eyes as the corner of the bed crumbled into powder. Wipeng shook his head.
“My lord. Please calm down. The Young Master seems anxious.”
That one actually worked. Seeing me sitting there sadly, wrapped in bandages from head to toe, Jin Wikyung’s eyes reddened.
“Just look at my youngest. How much must this poor child have suffered to be sitting there so completely out of it?”
Grab!

A hand the size of a cauldron lid clamped onto my shoulder and pulled me in. I was a fairly big guy myself, but this man was practically a small ogre. Trapped against his broad chest, I trembled in fear.
“There, little brother. It’s all right now. It’s all right.”
After a heartfelt hug that only he found moving, Jin Wikyung sniffed.
“I thought you’d be a child forever... but you’ve grown up now. Wipeng, did you know?”
Wipeng answered without even pausing to breathe.
“Yes. You don’t need to tell me.”
Of course, Jin Wikyung pretended not to hear him.

“Rumors have spread throughout our family and even through the streets. The tale of the hero who led a death squad in a raid on the enemy camp, defeated Jopil, One Question, One Kill, and one hundred wandering martial artists, and rescued the Sakju Branch’s household.”
“Wow. That’s amaz—wait, what?”
I blinked.
Hold on. That was my story?
“Um, I think there’s been some kind of misunderstanding.”
“That’s right, my lord. There seems to have been some misunder—”
Jin Wikyung smiled with satisfaction.
“Our little brother is modest, too. Wipeng, you shut your mouth.”
“No, it isn’t modesty. I think the rumor has been distorted a little.”
“That’s right. I know you care for the Young Master, my lord, but this is going too far. If the rumor gets too far-fetched, people won’t beli—”
“Rumor? Outlandish?”
BOOM!
Wipeng’s voice vanished beneath a thunderous crash. My mouth fell open as I stared at the gaping hole in my bedroom wall.
What the hell are you doing, you lunatic?
Jin Wikyung threw another punch. With a sound like compressed air bursting, what was left of the wall came down.
Wood and bricks poured from the two-story pavilion, sending the people outside into an uproar.
“It’s the Third Young Master! The Third Young Master’s residence is collapsing!”
“Get people over here! Hurry!”
While everyone was still reeling in shock, Jin Wikyung hoisted me into the air.
Put me down. Put me down, you crazy bastard!
I struggled with all my strength, but there was no fighting him off. One step. One step. Every step toward the gaping wall sent terror through me.
He’s going to drop me!
More than fifty people had gathered below. They called it a two-story building, but the pavilion was so large that we had to be a good ten meters up. The wind gusting through the hole made me dizzy.
If I fall, that’s a fracture at the very least.
Even as a chill ran down my spine, more people kept crowding in. Over fifty of them craned their necks to stare up at us.
“Who’s that? Wasn’t there an accident?”
“Isn’t that the Lesser Family Head? Who’s he holding?”
“The Third Young Master! It’s the Third Young Master!”
Someone’s shout sent a stir through the crowd.
“The Third Young Master—no, the Third Young Master, sir?”
“The Third Young Master who defeated Jopil, One Question, One Kill, has awakened!”
What is this situation?
While my eyes and ears were still whipping around, a solemn voice rang out clearly.
“Can you see?”
“Ah, yes. I can see them. Could you put me down—”
“Can you hear?”
“I can hear them too, but first, could you—”
“What do you feel?”
“Embarrassment. And shame.”
“They believe in you. They’re calling your name!”
“No, you fucking bastard.”
My final curse vanished beneath the crowd’s shouts.
“Third Young Master! Third Young Master!”
Dozens more people had appeared in that brief span of time. Countless gazes flew toward me and pinned me in place.
No, what is this?
Then Jin Wikyung, his expression grave, slid his hands beneath my armpits and lifted me high.
Right on cue, a thunderous cheer erupted.
“Woooooo!”
“Third Young Master! Jin Taekyung!”
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi! Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
And then...
Fuck. What is this, a baby lion?
The theme music from an old cartoon began playing in my head.

“There was a battle?”
And a major one, no less—hundreds of people thrown in.
My heart lurched for a moment, but then I remembered what Wipeng had said earlier.
Good news and even better news.
He’d already given away the outcome.
“We won.”
“It was a great victory.
Fewer than thirty of them escaped alive.
That’s about the same as our family’s total casualties.”
Judging by the scar running from Wipeng’s forehead to his chin, it must have been a fierce battle.
Well, of course.
They outnumbered us two to one.
Still, it was a relief we’d won.
From the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s perspective, we’d poured in nearly half our strength.
If we’d lost, the damage would have been enormous.
“It’s unfortunate that we let the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s Lesser Family Head escape, but taking down the Mount Heng Twin Devils was a major gain.”
“The Mount Heng Fucking Devils?”
“The Mount Heng Twin Devils.
They were Peak masters under the Mount Heng Sword Sect, and their loyalty was something else...
They kept throwing themselves at us without regard for their lives, so we had no choice but to kill them.”
Wipeng tapped the fresh scar on his face.
“If we’d captured them alive, we could have extracted valuable information.”
“Did you—I mean, did Great Hero Wipeng kill them?”
“My lord and I took one each.
They were pretty good.”
I was left speechless as Wipeng slurped his tea.
For fuck’s sake...
Are Peak masters a joke to him?
That had been the fiercest fight of my twenty-seven years.
I’d suffered every kind of internal injury and been carved up like a steak.
Then I’d been unconscious for five days, so I’d practically taken a half-bath in the River Jordan.
And after taking down Peak masters of that caliber, all he had to say was that they were pretty good?
This guy’s a complete monster.
I learned something for certain this time: even Peak masters came in different levels.
It was a huge relief that people of that caliber were on my side.
“That aside...”
Clink.
Wipeng set down his teacup and regarded me with an unreadable look.
“You were remarkable.”
“Pardon?”
“I’m talking about Jopil, One Question, One Kill.
Even calling it remarkable doesn’t do justice to what you accomplished by defeating him.”
You people seem a lot more remarkable to me.
It felt like being praised by an A-rank Hunter for being good at killing goblins.
“Ah.
Right.
Thanks, I guess.”
I wanted to end the discussion about Jopil there.
I was in lousy shape, my mood wasn’t much better, and I wanted to check all the System Rewards waiting for me.
Let me rest already.
I’m still a patient, damn it.
I tried to convey that with a wink.
Wipeng frowned.
“Does your eye hurt?
Shall I call a physician?”
I’m fine.”
“Your eye just spasmed.”
“That wasn’t a spasm.”
“It was.
I saw it clearly.”
“No, what I just did was...”
Then Wipeng rolled his eyes back until only the whites showed and started to tremble.
The table shook, and tea sloshed over the rim of his cup.
I cried out in alarm.
“My God, Great Hero Wipeng!”
This guy has epilepsy.
No—how does a Peak master even get epilepsy?
Just as I hurriedly tried to stand, the convulsions stopped.
Wipeng returned to normal and spoke with perfect calm.
“That’s what you did.”
“Are you all ri—wait, what?”
“That’s what you did just now, Third Young Master.
Your eye spasmed.”
“So you were imitating me?”
“Yes.”
What kind of lunatic is this...?
I tried to explain the difference between a wink and an epileptic fit, but the words stuck.
Wipeng was glaring at me like a pissed-off dictator.
“...Why don’t we just finish talking about Jopil?”
“Let’s.”
Wipeng nodded in satisfaction.
Crazy bastard.
In the end, I had to tell him everything about my fight with Jopil from beginning to end.
How Jopil had moved.
What martial arts he’d used.
Wipeng’s incisive questions had me tensing up more than once.
“You severed the sinews and meridians in Jopil’s legs with a dagger?”
“Yes.
I’d hidden it beforehand.”
“There’s no way Jopil would have failed to notice it...
Continue.”
When the long story finally ended, Wipeng released the breath he’d been holding.
The complicated look in his eyes said more than words could.
“Third Young Master, you have accomplished a truly great deed.”
“Ah, thank you...”
“I hate to admit it, but I mean that.”
Right.”
“When I think of all the trouble you’ve caused until now, my blood boils, but I was genuinely impressed.
I mean that.”

“Who could have imagined that the Third Young Master who stole family funds day after day and poured them into pleasure houses, then paraded through the streets dead drunk and smeared shit all over the family’s reputation, would become such a great man?
I, Wipeng, am genuinely in awe.”
Just curse me out, you bastard...
I barely held back the torrent of abuse threatening to burst out.
“I got lucky.
Jopil let his guard down too.”
Wipeng shook his head.
“No.
It was all skill.
It makes no difference who let their guard down or who hid a dagger in advance.
If that alone had been enough to kill Jopil, he would never have been Jopil, One Question, One Kill.
Murim is a place where only the strong survive.”
“Only the strong survive.”
I quietly rolled the words over my tongue.
They tasted somehow bitter and sweet at once.
Murim—this game—had been that kind of place from the beginning.
I had survived there, and I had grown stronger.

In the end, he even drew upon his innate qi.
A Peak master threw away his own life in an attempt to kill you.
But what was the result?”
“I won.”
“Yes.
Exactly.”
“Then I was stronger than Jopil.”
Wipeng, who had looked vaguely displeased all this time, suddenly turned dead serious.
“What are you talking about?
Jopil was stronger.
Do Peak masters look like a joke to you?”
“You were only strong enough to kill Jopil with a surprise attack.”

chapters.title: Chapter 33
paragraphs: “Please kill me.”

A young man with disheveled hair, covered in blood and dust, dropped to his knees. His name was Lee Seogwang—the elder brother of the late Lee Seogeun and the Young Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
“Report. Tell me yourself.”
The cold voice froze everyone inside the tent. Every last one of them was a senior of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, a master who had spent long years roaming the martial world.
Yet even they had to bow their heads before one man.
“Father...”
“That isn’t the answer I want.”
The Blood Wolf Sword, Lee Cheonbaek, did not even turn around. Lee Seogwang forced the words out in a trembling voice.
“There are only twenty-three survivors, including me. We don’t know whether the rest are alive or dead.”
A heavy silence settled over the gathering.
Some two hundred troops had been killed or captured, and they had lost three Peak masters. That alone would have made it difficult to escape punishment, but there was an even greater problem.
“What orders were you given?”
“...To wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s branch and advance as far as Jeongyang.”
“And after that?”
“To blockade the road and wait for the main force to join us.”
“Why did you push as far as Honju?”
“I received... intelligence.”
“Intelligence?”
“Yes. I was told that Jopil, One Question, One Kill, had pursued Jin Taekyung all the way to Honju and captured him. But...”
“He must have said the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s pursuit party was on his heels and asked you to help him.”
Lee Seogwang lowered his head, and Lee Cheonbaek let out a hollow laugh.
“Who delivered that information?”
“A wandering martial artist under Jopil.”
“Do you still believe it?”
Smack!
Lee Seogwang’s head snapped to the side. Lee Cheonbaek glared down at him, his eyes blazing.
“Be grateful you were born my son.”
In the end, Lee Seogwang was ordered to return to the Mount Heng Sword Sect. Once he withdrew, the matter was settled for the time being.
Now it was time to assess the situation with a cool head.
“What is our current position?”
“We lost two hundred men, but more than half were wandering martial artists we scraped together in a hurry. The damage isn’t as severe as it sounds. The problem is...”
“We lost three Peak masters.”
The thought left a bitter taste in Lee Cheonbaek’s mouth. The Mount Heng Twin Devils had stood beside him for twenty years, and Jopil, whom he had paid a fortune to hire, was dead as well.
A Peak master could change the course of a battle. Somehow, they had to fill the void.
“Gather more. Buy wandering martial artists from the black market, hire mounted bandits—use whatever means necessary.”
“Our expenses are already too high. By now, word of what happened in Honju will have spread, and they’ll try to raise their prices.”
“They aren’t trustworthy men, either. Especially the mounted bandits. Aren’t they human butchers? If we hire people like that, our sect’s reputation will suffer afterward...”
Lee Cheonbaek did not even blink.
“All the better. Hire every last one.”
“Sect Leader!”
“There are no fewer than five hundred men gathered here. We have more than twice their numbers, and we aren’t outmatched in Peak masters either.”
“My son thought the same thing. Then he got utterly crushed in Honju.”
“That was...”
“I don’t care whether they’re human butchers or anything else. Throw everything we have into this. If we lose this war, it won’t be our reputation we lose—it’ll be our lives!”
At Lee Cheonbaek’s thunderous command, the seniors realized there was no point trying to persuade him. But the discussion was not yet over.
“The martial artists’ morale is in shambles.”
“The defeat at Honju is bad enough, but the news that Jin Taekyung killed Jopil, One Question, One Kill, has shaken them.”
Jin Taekyung.
Hearing his enemy’s name made Lee Cheonbaek’s stomach churn.
Are there really people stupid enough to believe such an absurd rumor?

As if it weren’t enough that the pathetic fool Jin Taekyung had poisoned his son, now he had supposedly killed a Peak master as well. The scheme was obvious. Lee Cheonbaek ground his teeth at the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s despicable tactics.
“Root out everyone spreading that nonsense. Don’t let a single one escape!”
Taking a few heads as examples might lower morale even further, but it would keep the army from collapsing. Now was the time to clamp down and press forward.
“Three days. In three days, we march on Taiyuan!”
That was the nature of gratitude and grudges in Murim. The cycle would not end until one side fell.
I’ll take everything from you. Just as you did.
“What an incredible recovery.”
The physician clicked his tongue in amazement. It was my second day since waking up, and overnight, the scabs had fallen away to reveal smooth new skin beneath them.
“In ten years as a physician, I’ve never seen anything like this.”
Even to me, the speed of my recovery was astonishing. The flesh melted by the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, the fractured bones, the deep sword wounds—there was no trace of any of them left.
Oh, and the internal injuries too.
Must be the effect of leveling up.
There was only one way to produce a similar result in the real world: the healing magic used by the tiny handful of Hunters known as healers.
Is complete healing too much to ask?
I was a little disappointed, but it was probably for the best. If a single level-up had healed every injury on my body, avoiding suspicion would have been difficult.
Even now, the physician kept glancing at me as though I were a monster.
“Heavens. How strange. This is far too much to attribute to the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng...”
“Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng?”
I remembered seeing something like that in martial arts novels. Ginseng that had grown for a hundred years, or whatever.
Why is that suddenly coming up?
Seeing my confusion, the physician explained. He was one of the few NPCs who knew I had lost my memory.
“Around this time last year, the Medicine King Hall’s storeroom was robbed.”
Ah. The moment he said it, I knew where this was going.
The stolen medicinals must have included the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, and the culprit was obviously...
“The Medicine King Hall Master was absolutely furious.”
The physician gave me an awkward smile.
“After all, it isn’t something you can obtain merely by having money. You stole and consumed an elixir capable of granting twenty years of internal energy in a single dose.”
“Twenty years of internal energy?”
Something clicked. That third reserve of internal energy that had refused to obey me.
So that was it.
At the same time, a pang of regret hit me. When I used the Skill at the last moment, most of the twenty years of internal energy from the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng had vanished.
It had been a complete disaster caused by the energy running wild instead of obeying my control.
I blew the whole thing like a one-use item.
The physician misread my grimace and hurriedly added, “Of course, Young Master, you must have had some grand purpose in making such a decision.”
Grand purpose, my ass. I probably ate it as a tonic.
The snow ginseng’s internal energy had kept me alive, but it still felt like a terrible waste.
Such a waste I could die.
“You’ve almost completely recovered, so you shouldn’t have any trouble moving around. Then I’ll be on my way.”
The moment the physician hurried out, I opened the System window.
Open Status Window.
Ding.

System Status Window Lv. 30 Jin Taekyung Class: Second Rate Martial Artist Fame: 410 Titles: 4 (Title effects active) — Scion of a Prestigious Family (All stats +5, Fame +50) — Family Shame (All stats −5, Fame −50) — Novice Trainee (Training speed +10%) — Gambler (Combat-related stats increased by 10% in a one-on-one fight) Strength: 115 Stamina: 120 Agility: 116 Intelligence: 15 Charm: 15 Internal Energy: 15 years Remaining Points: 0
Pride welled up the moment I saw it.
I’ve come a long way.

It felt like only yesterday I’d been shaking in front of a few two-bit bandits. Now I was a master in my own right. My Level had shot up after I took down Jopil, and I’d gained a massive amount of Fame.
That wasn’t all. By absorbing some of the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng’s remaining energy, I had gained another four years of internal energy. And on top of that...

System Skill Window One Annihilation Grade: Peak Realm: Second Stage Restriction: Jin Taekyung Effect: Consumes Stamina and internal energy to deliver a powerful strike. Depending on the amount used, the user enters a helpless state for a certain period of time.
I had gained a new martial art—or rather, a new Skill.
But it differed greatly from my Skills in the real world.
I can control how much it consumes and how much power it releases.

Thrust with All My Might. The Skill now named One Annihilation couldn’t be used recklessly. It could unleash destructive power several stages above my usual level for an instant, but that single attack consumed all my strength.
No. Maybe the Skill could always be controlled like this.
In the real world, I was an F-rank Hunter. My physical abilities were pathetic, and so was the amount of mana in my body. But here in this game—in Murim—I was different.

Here, I was a martial artist with fifteen years of internal energy and physical abilities superior to NPCs twenty or thirty Levels above me. With a better vessel to contain the power, I could finally use the Skill the way it had always been meant to be used.
I’ve gotten stronger again.
It felt like only yesterday Hyuk Mujin had been wiping the floor with me while I struggled to learn martial arts. Now I had taken down a Peak master.
Outside the window, people chanted my name several times a day.
Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. Hero of the family. That sort of thing.
A hero.
I never thought I’d hear anyone call me that. I was a two-bit F-rank Hunter whose motto was safety first. The word had never had anything to do with me.
I lay still and fidgeted with my hands. Palms that had once been a young master’s—white and soft—were now packed tight with calluses.
I took down Jopil with these hands.

All told, the people I’d taken down numbered more than a few dozen. Bandits, wandering martial artists, even people rated as First Rate—and I had survived. I’d even taken down a Peak master I thought I could never beat: Jopil, One Question, One Kill.
Something Wipeng had said suddenly came back to me.
The one who survives is strong.
If he was right, then I was undeniably strong. I had survived every enemy I had faced so far, and now people were calling me a hero.
Yeah. If I was being honest...
It doesn’t feel bad.
The real-world me was pitiful.
I ate and slept in a goshiwon room barely ten square meters in size, the breadwinner responsible for supporting my family. I couldn’t become a hero, and I didn’t want to.
I was just Jin Taekyung, a bottom-rung Hunter who fought every day while praying he would survive.
That was me.
But in this game, I’m different.

I had accomplished many things that F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung never could. At the very least... I could protect the people who trusted and followed me from their enemies. People acknowledged me. They called me a hero.
Even if everything here was nothing but virtual, even if the people I saw were NPCs, that fact didn’t change.
Thinking that, I suddenly laughed.
This is why games are scary.
Was this what game addiction felt like?
Before I knew it, I had started enjoying life as Jin Taekyung, a martial artist of Murim. This place was a game. It could turn every impossibility into a possibility.
But now it was time to leave.
Back to that place filled with impossibilities—the real world. My family was there. The real me was there.
Check Quest Window.
Ding.

System Quest Logout Now you must make your way through this harsh Murim. Become stronger and more famous. For the day that will eventually come... Grade: Main Quest Restriction: Jin Taekyung Objective: Achieve the First Rate realm (Incomplete) Achieve Lv. 30 (Complete) Achieve Fame 500 (410/500) Reward: Logout
Logout.
The moment I saw those four glittering characters, my breath caught.
Only two conditions left before I could log out. Time could take care of Fame. The more rumors about me spread, the more it would keep climbing.
The problem lay elsewhere.
“First Rate.”
What did I even need to become First Rate?
If it wasn’t Level, stats, or Fame, then...
Internal energy? Or do I need to raise the realm of my martial arts further?
Just then, a polite voice came from outside the door.
“Young Master. The Lesser Family Head is looking for you.”
“Ah.”
Right. When you don’t know something, the best thing to do is ask.
And in that respect, Peak master Jin Wikyung was the best private tutor I could ask for.

sentences.text: “Please kill me.”
A young man with disheveled hair, covered in blood and dust, dropped to his knees.
His name was Lee Seogwang—the elder brother of the late Lee Seogeun and the Young Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
“Report.
Tell me yourself.”
The cold voice froze everyone inside the tent.
Every last one of them was a senior of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, a master who had spent long years roaming the martial world.
Yet even they had to bow their heads before one man.
“Father...”
“That isn’t the answer I want.”
The Blood Wolf Sword, Lee Cheonbaek, did not even turn around.
Lee Seogwang forced the words out in a trembling voice.
“There are only twenty-three survivors, including me.
We don’t know whether the rest are alive or dead.”
A heavy silence settled over the gathering.
Some two hundred troops had been killed or captured, and they had lost three Peak masters.
That alone would have made it difficult to escape punishment, but there was an even greater problem.
“What orders were you given?”
“...To wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s branch and advance as far as Jeongyang.”
“And after that?”
“To blockade the road and wait for the main force to join us.”
“Why did you push as far as Honju?”
“I received... intelligence.”
“Intelligence?”
“Yes.
I was told that Jopil, One Question, One Kill, had pursued Jin Taekyung all the way to Honju and captured him.
But...”
“He must have said the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s pursuit party was on his heels and asked you to help him.”
Lee Seogwang lowered his head, and Lee Cheonbaek let out a hollow laugh.
“Who delivered that information?”
“A wandering martial artist under Jopil.”
“Do you still believe it?”
Smack!
Lee Seogwang’s head snapped to the side.
Lee Cheonbaek glared down at him, his eyes blazing.
“Be grateful you were born my son.”
In the end, Lee Seogwang was ordered to return to the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
Once he withdrew, the matter was settled for the time being.
Now it was time to assess the situation with a cool head.
“What is our current position?”
“We lost two hundred men, but more than half were wandering martial artists we scraped together in a hurry.
The damage isn’t as severe as it sounds.
The problem is...”
“We lost three Peak masters.”
The thought left a bitter taste in Lee Cheonbaek’s mouth.
The Mount Heng Twin Devils had stood beside him for twenty years, and Jopil, whom he had paid a fortune to hire, was dead as well.
A Peak master could change the course of a battle.
Somehow, they had to fill the void.
“Gather more.
Buy wandering martial artists from the black market, hire mounted bandits—use whatever means necessary.”
“Our expenses are already too high.
By now, word of what happened in Honju will have spread, and they’ll try to raise their prices.”
“They aren’t trustworthy men, either.
Especially the mounted bandits.
Aren’t they human butchers?
If we hire people like that, our sect’s reputation will suffer afterward...”
Lee Cheonbaek did not even blink.
“All the better.
Hire every last one.”
“Sect Leader!”
“There are no fewer than five hundred men gathered here.
We have more than twice their numbers, and we aren’t outmatched in Peak masters either.”
“My son thought the same thing.
Then he got utterly crushed in Honju.”
“That was...”
“I don’t care whether they’re human butchers or anything else.
Throw everything we have into this.
If we lose this war, it won’t be our reputation we lose—it’ll be our lives!”
At Lee Cheonbaek’s thunderous command, the seniors realized there was no point trying to persuade him.
But the discussion was not yet over.
“The martial artists’ morale is in shambles.”
“The defeat at Honju is bad enough, but the news that Jin Taekyung killed Jopil, One Question, One Kill, has shaken them.”
Jin Taekyung.
Hearing his enemy’s name made Lee Cheonbaek’s stomach churn.
Are there really people stupid enough to believe such an absurd rumor?
As if it weren’t enough that the pathetic fool Jin Taekyung had poisoned his son, now he had supposedly killed a Peak master as well.
The scheme was obvious.
Lee Cheonbaek ground his teeth at the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s despicable tactics.
“Root out everyone spreading that nonsense.
Don’t let a single one escape!”
Taking a few heads as examples might lower morale even further, but it would keep the army from collapsing.
Now was the time to clamp down and press forward.
“Three days.
In three days, we march on Taiyuan!”
That was the nature of gratitude and grudges in Murim.
The cycle would not end until one side fell.
I’ll take everything from you.
Just as you did.
“What an incredible recovery.”
The physician clicked his tongue in amazement.
It was my second day since waking up, and overnight, the scabs had fallen away to reveal smooth new skin beneath them.
“In ten years as a physician, I’ve never seen anything like this.”
Even to me, the speed of my recovery was astonishing.
The flesh melted by the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, the fractured bones, the deep sword wounds—there was no trace of any of them left.
Oh, and the internal injuries too.
Must be the effect of leveling up.
There was only one way to produce a similar result in the real world: the healing magic used by the tiny handful of Hunters known as healers.
Is complete healing too much to ask?
I was a little disappointed, but it was probably for the best.
If a single level-up had healed every injury on my body, avoiding suspicion would have been difficult.
Even now, the physician kept glancing at me as though I were a monster.
“Heavens.
How strange.
This is far too much to attribute to the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng...”
“Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng?”
I remembered seeing something like that in martial arts novels.
Ginseng that had grown for a hundred years, or whatever.
Why is that suddenly coming up?
Seeing my confusion, the physician explained.
He was one of the few NPCs who knew I had lost my memory.
“Around this time last year, the Medicine King Hall’s storeroom was robbed.”
Ah.
The moment he said it, I knew where this was going.
The stolen medicinals must have included the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, and the culprit was obviously...
“The Medicine King Hall Master was absolutely furious.”
The physician gave me an awkward smile.
“After all, it isn’t something you can obtain merely by having money.
You stole and consumed an elixir capable of granting twenty years of internal energy in a single dose.”
“Twenty years of internal energy?”
Something clicked.
That third reserve of internal energy that had refused to obey me.
So that was it.
At the same time, a pang of regret hit me.
When I used the Skill at the last moment, most of the twenty years of internal energy from the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng had vanished.
It had been a complete disaster caused by the energy running wild instead of obeying my control.
I blew the whole thing like a one-use item.
The physician misread my grimace and hurriedly added, “Of course, Young Master, you must have had some grand purpose in making such a decision.”
Grand purpose, my ass.
I probably ate it as a tonic.
The snow ginseng’s internal energy had kept me alive, but it still felt like a terrible waste.
Such a waste I could die.
“You’ve almost completely recovered, so you shouldn’t have any trouble moving around.
Then I’ll be on my way.”
The moment the physician hurried out, I opened the System window.
Open Status Window.
Ding.
System Status Window Lv.

30 Jin Taekyung Class: Second Rate Martial Artist Fame: 410 Titles: 4 (Title effects active) — Scion of a Prestigious Family (All stats +5, Fame +50) — Family Shame (All stats −5, Fame −50) — Novice Trainee (Training speed +10%) — Gambler (Combat-related stats increased by 10% in a one-on-one fight) Strength: 115 Stamina: 120 Agility: 116 Intelligence: 15 Charm: 15 Internal Energy: 15 years Remaining Points: 0
Pride welled up the moment I saw it.
I’ve come a long way.
It felt like only yesterday I’d been shaking in front of a few two-bit bandits.
Now I was a master in my own right.
My Level had shot up after I took down Jopil, and I’d gained a massive amount of Fame.
That wasn’t all.
By absorbing some of the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng’s remaining energy, I had gained another four years of internal energy.
And on top of that...
System Skill Window One Annihilation Grade: Peak Realm: Second Stage Restriction: Jin Taekyung Effect: Consumes Stamina and internal energy to deliver a powerful strike.
Depending on the amount used, the user enters a helpless state for a certain period of time.
I had gained a new martial art—or rather, a new Skill.

I can control how much it consumes and how much power it releases.
Thrust with All My Might.

No.

chapters.title: Chapter 34
paragraphs: Once, while Jinho hyung and I were watching TV, we had a conversation like this.
“That’s him, right? Han Seongjin.”
“You know Han Seongjin?”
“Wouldn’t it be weirder if I didn’t? His face is everywhere whenever I turn on the TV. I’ve seen him so often, he feels like family.”
“Watch your mouth. That’s defamation.”
“Son of a bitch.”
On the screen, a handsome man with a lanky build was smiling brightly. Dozens of cameras and a huge crowd reacted to his every move. Flashes and screams kept going off without a pause.

“He’s got everything. An A-rank Hunter is basically a walking mid-sized company, isn’t he? And he gets a model’s proportions and a celebrity’s face on top of that? That’s just cheating. How old did you say he was?”
“I think he’s the same age as me.”
“...Hang in there.”
No matter the profession, some people made good money and others didn’t. And no profession had a wider gap between the two than Hunters.
“Don’t worry, man. If you wait a little longer, your day will come.”
“How long do I have to wait?”
“Try waiting another hundred years. It’ll be possible in your next life.”
I wished I could show Jinho hyung, who had cackled as he mocked me back then, what I looked like now.
I wonder what kind of face he’d make if he saw this.
With every step I took, dozens of people swarmed after me. NPCs from the Jin Family of Taiyuan, men and women of all ages, were looking at me with shining eyes.
Is this how famous people feel all the time?
All that attention, all those admiring looks—it was a burden, but it also felt kind of good.
For the first time, I understood that clichéd line from game ads: A new hero awaits!
Yeah. It’s almost over. I might as well enjoy it.
I smiled and waved, and a roar went up. With the ever-growing crowd trailing behind me, I arrived at the main hall used for meetings.
“They’re waiting for you.”
The martial artist at the door looked familiar. He was the same man who had stared at me with contempt when Lee Seogeun came to visit.
Has it been about fifteen days?
Just as I was no longer the person I had been then, neither was he. He gave me an extremely respectful fist-and-palm salute and opened the door wide.
The main hall looked exactly as I remembered it. A large table stood in the center, and the chairs scattered on either side showed that a meeting had just ended.
“You’re here?”
Seated at the head of the table, Jin Wikyung gave me a weary smile. He was alone in the spacious hall.
“Where’s Wipeng?”
“He’ll be back shortly.”
Once I sat down, Jin Wikyung got straight to the point.
“The Lower District Sect has contacted us. The Mount Heng Sword Sect is gathering every last fighter it can.”
They must be shitting bricks over there.

I didn’t know war, but I knew fighting. And war was made up of battles. The enemy had already lost many martial artists and suffered a crushing blow to its morale. They would throw everything they had into the next battle.
“It’ll be a difficult fight.”
“They’ve poured their sect’s entire wealth into it. If the reinforcements join the main force led by the Blood Wolf Sword, they’ll number around a thousand.”
“A thousand...”
That was an insane number. I had never fought in a battle on that scale, and I had no desire to.
Jin Wikyung continued grimly.
“We’ll march north with all our forces and strike the enemy’s main force before it can join the reinforcements.”
“When?”
“In two days.”
Goddammit. That’s fucking fast.
The race against time wasn’t only between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect. I was in one too.
Can I log out by then?
If I reached First Rate within two days, I could log out. But if I didn’t, I would have to fight my ass off all over again.
Then I’d be completely screwed.
Jin Wikyung spoke again.
“I’d like you to take charge of the rear guard.”
Can’t. Won’t.
I barely swallowed the words that tried to leap out on reflex.
Jin Wikyung looked more serious than I had ever seen him.
“This is a fight our family is staking everything on. Your presence alone will greatly raise morale.”
I was still debating whether to accept when he continued.
“Fortunately, the Five Gates of Shanxi have agreed to help us. I want you to move with some of their people in the rear guard.”
“The Five Gates of Shanxi?”
“An alliance of five small and mid-sized sects. They’ve always been on good terms with our family.”
“...I see.”
“Then will you take charge of the rear guard?”
Ding.

System Quest Rear Guard Defense Jin Wikyung has proposed that you take charge of the rear guard. If you accept this mission, the martial artists will praise your will and courage. Type: Short-Term Quest Grade: Second Rate Restriction: Jin Taekyung Objective: Accept the proposal (Incomplete) Reward: Fame +10 Failure: Fame −10
I answered without another thought.
“I will.”
A message appeared announcing the Quest’s completion and the increase in my Fame.
My Fame drops if I refuse?
The Quest Window had made me an offer I couldn’t refuse. It was ridiculous, yet a strange sense of relief spread through me all the same.
Relief? Have I actually lost my mind?
As I berated myself for being a game addict, Jin Wikyung smiled broadly.
“I’m glad you’re here.”
He was smiling, but an invisible shadow hung over his face.
As if spending all day buried under stacks of paperwork wasn’t enough, now there was a war. Leading a vast clan like the Jin Family of Taiyuan had to be a heavy burden even for him.
He said two days.

Two powers that divided an entire region between them were about to collide. The Jin Family of Taiyuan was short on martial artists, so even if we threw everything we had into the fight, we would still be at a disadvantage.
Can we win?

I forced the thought aside. What did I care whether they lived or died? The march was in two days, and it would take several more days for the battle to begin. No matter who won, I would be gone by the time a victor was decided.
Now it was time to hear what I needed to know.
“Um, there’s something I wanted to ask.”
“Go ahead.”
“I’m still stuck at the Second Rate realm...”
After hearing me out, Jin Wikyung tilted his head.
“You’re Second Rate?”
His tone said he couldn’t understand what I was talking about. I had utterly crushed Lee Seogeun and even brought down Jopil. Jin Wikyung had assumed I was First Rate long ago, and so had Jopil.
“Yes. My realm just won’t rise, so I was hoping you could give me some advice.”
“Advice...”
Jin Wikyung thought for a moment before speaking.
“You’re already First Rate.”
“But I’m Second Rate.”
“I’m telling you, you’re First Rate. More than that, you’re a Supreme First Rate martial artist standing at the wall of the Peak realm.”
“No, I really am Second Rate...”
“Who told you that?”
Ugh, this is driving me crazy.
I wished I could show him the System Window. It plainly said Second Rate, but I was the only one who could see it, and the frustration was killing me.
I sighed.
“No one told me I was Second Rate.”
“Then?”
“It’s just... I’m Second Rate. I don’t really know how to explain it.”
“Do you believe you’re Second Rate?”
“Yes.”
“Then it’s simple.”
“Wh-what is?”
Is he finally going to reveal the secret to advancing realms?
I stared at Jin Wikyung, my eyes full of anticipation, but he said nothing. Instead, he dipped a finger into his cold tea and brought it to the table.
Scritch.
A single character appeared.
信
信? The character for “belief”?
Jin Wikyung took one look at my face and let out a short laugh.
“You look like you’ve just been slapped.”
“...You must be seeing things.”
More like I look like I want to slap you.
“What is this?”
“Exactly what it says. Believe in yourself.”
“What does that have to do with advancing realms?”
“Because martial arts begin with belief.”
Martial arts begin with belief? It sounded like airy nonsense. Yet the moment I heard those words, my heart began to pound.
They begin with belief...
For some reason, that one sentence kept circling through my mind, spinning around and around until I felt dizzy.
What had I believed in all this time?
The first word that came to mind—and the only one—was the System.
The thing that had helped me most in this game, the thing that had always told me nothing but absolute facts.
I had believed I was Second Rate because the System said I was Second Rate.
Because I believed in the System.
I had already overwhelmed Lee Seogeun, a First Rate master. I had taken down more than twenty wandering martial artists by myself and even defeated Jopil, a Peak master.
Everyone hailed me as a First Rate master and a hero, yet I had remained Second Rate.
Because I had believed in the System instead of myself.
But now I understood.
I’m already First Rate.
Already. Maybe I had been for a long time.
I was First Rate.
“You look like you’ve just been slapped.”
This time, Jin Wikyung was right. I slumped against the back of my chair, stunned.
What a dumbass.
If I couldn’t even believe in myself, I was Second Rate. No. I had been Second Rate.
Ding.

System — You have reached the First Rate realm! — The realm of all martial arts increases by one stage! — Your Muscles and Bones and your Sinews and Meridians improve greatly! — The size of your dantian expands! — Level Up! — Level Up!
From Third Rate to Second Rate. Then from Second Rate to First Rate.
I felt power surge from deep within me, and Jin Wikyung burst out laughing.
“What happened?”
Wipeng showed up late and asked, looking bewildered.
It felt like a blocked nose had suddenly cleared. Reaching First Rate had brought a tremendous leap in every way—my senses, my martial arts, everything.
I left the main hall and started walking. The wind felt cool and refreshing.
“It’s the Third Young Master.”
“Has he fully recovered?”
Sure enough, people’s gazes gathered on me. I changed course toward an even more crowded area.
Anyone watching would think I was desperate for attention.
But everything happens for a reason.
Ding.
System — Someone gazes at you with awe. — Fame increases by 1. — Someone is impressed after hearing rumors about you. — Fame increases by 1.
As I walked, people gathered around me like clouds. Among them were plenty of NPCs wearing clothes I had never seen before.
Who are they?
I made eye contact with one of them. The young man looked to be in his early twenties. He flinched in surprise, then hurried over and gave me a fist-and-palm salute.
“Gwak of the Samdo Sect presents his respects.”
“Ah, yes.”
By now, the fist-and-palm salute came out on reflex and looked fairly convincing. But where was the Samdo Sect?
Oh. Could it be...?
“Are you with the Five Gates of Shanxi?”
Gwak Whatsisname nodded enthusiastically.
“That is correct. Our Samdo Sect has agreed to lend its strength to the Jin Family of Taiyuan. I, Gwak, could not be more delighted to offer what little help I can.”
In a situation like this, he was a reinforcement worth his weight in gold. I took Gwak Whatsisname by the hand, hoping he would fight hard enough for both of us.
“Thank you for coming.”
“Please, think nothing of it. It is an honor simply to take part in the Young Master’s tale of martial valor.”
System — Someone is impressed after hearing rumors about you. — Fame increases by 1.
A total stranger had come all this way to fight for us, and he was even making my Fame shoot up. I offered the endlessly generous Gwak Whatsisname my warmest thanks.
“God bless you.”
“Pardon?”
“It means I hope the Jade Emperor’s blessing will be with you.”
“Ahh. Thank you. God bleshyoo.”
“Ah. Yes.”
I put on a fake smile and kept walking. Maybe because everyone who needed to know about me already did, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s people no longer raised my Fame.
Still, I’ve built up quite a bit.
I opened the Status Window and saw that I was about fifty points short of the target. If I grinded hard for two more days, maybe I could log out.
“Um, Young Hero Jin.”
I turned around. It was the fellow from the Samdo Sect. He looked ready to follow me to the ends of the earth.
“If you aren’t busy, perhaps we could have some tea together...”
“I’m sorry. I have somewhere to be.”
It sounded like a lie, but it was the truth. My destination had been decided from the start.
I pointed to a building as disappointment crossed his face. A faded signboard hung above it, and the heavy smell of medicinal decoctions wafted from within.
Medicine King Hall.
Beneath the signboard hung a small wooden plaque.
Authorized Personnel Only.
The people surrounding me let out pitying sighs.
