Is this how famous people feel all the time?
All that attention, all those admiring looks—it was a burden, but it also felt kind of good.
For the first time, I understood that clichéd line from game ads: A new hero awaits!
Yeah.
It’s almost over.
I might as well enjoy it.
I smiled and waved, and a roar went up.
With the ever-growing crowd trailing behind me, I arrived at the main hall used for meetings.
“They’re waiting for you.”
The martial artist at the door looked familiar.
He was the same man who had stared at me with contempt when Lee Seogeun came to visit.
Has it been about fifteen days?
Just as I was no longer the person I had been then, neither was he.
He gave me an extremely respectful fist-and-palm salute and opened the door wide.
The main hall looked exactly as I remembered it.
A large table stood in the center, and the chairs scattered on either side showed that a meeting had just ended.
“You’re here?”
Seated at the head of the table, Jin Wikyung gave me a weary smile.
He was alone in the spacious hall.
“Where’s Wipeng?”
“He’ll be back shortly.”
Once I sat down, Jin Wikyung got straight to the point.
“The Lower District Sect has contacted us.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect is gathering every last fighter it can.”
They must be shitting bricks over there.
I didn’t know war, but I knew fighting.
And war was made up of battles.
The enemy had already lost many martial artists and suffered a crushing blow to its morale.
They would throw everything they had into the next battle.
“It’ll be a difficult fight.”
“They’ve poured their sect’s entire wealth into it.
If the reinforcements join the main force led by the Blood Wolf Sword, they’ll number around a thousand.”
“A thousand...”
That was an insane number.
I had never fought in a battle on that scale, and I had no desire to.
Jin Wikyung continued grimly.
“We’ll march north with all our forces and strike the enemy’s main force before it can join the reinforcements.”
“When?”
“In two days.”
Goddammit.
That’s fucking fast.
The race against time wasn’t only between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
I was in one too.
Can I log out by then?
If I reached First Rate within two days, I could log out.
But if I didn’t, I would have to fight my ass off all over again.
Then I’d be completely screwed.
Jin Wikyung spoke again.
“I’d like you to take charge of the rear guard.”
Can’t.
Won’t.
I barely swallowed the words that tried to leap out on reflex.
Jin Wikyung looked more serious than I had ever seen him.
“This is a fight our family is staking everything on.
Your presence alone will greatly raise morale.”
I was still debating whether to accept when he continued.
“Fortunately, the Five Gates of Shanxi have agreed to help us.
I want you to move with some of their people in the rear guard.”
“The Five Gates of Shanxi?”
“An alliance of five small and mid-sized sects.
They’ve always been on good terms with our family.”
“...I see.”
“Then will you take charge of the rear guard?”
Ding.
System Quest Rear Guard Defense Jin Wikyung has proposed that you take charge of the rear guard.
If you accept this mission, the martial artists will praise your will and courage.
Type: Short-Term Quest Grade: Second Rate Restriction: Jin Taekyung Objective: Accept the proposal (Incomplete) Reward: Fame +10 Failure: Fame −10
I answered without another thought.
“I will.”
A message appeared announcing the Quest’s completion and the increase in my Fame.
My Fame drops if I refuse?
The Quest Window had made me an offer I couldn’t refuse.
It was ridiculous, yet a strange sense of relief spread through me all the same.
Relief?
Have I actually lost my mind?
As I berated myself for being a game addict, Jin Wikyung smiled broadly.
“I’m glad you’re here.”
He was smiling, but an invisible shadow hung over his face.
As if spending all day buried under stacks of paperwork wasn’t enough, now there was a war.
Leading a vast clan like the Jin Family of Taiyuan had to be a heavy burden even for him.
He said two days.
Two powers that divided an entire region between them were about to collide.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan was short on martial artists, so even if we threw everything we had into the fight, we would still be at a disadvantage.
Can we win?
I forced the thought aside.
What did I care whether they lived or died?
The march was in two days, and it would take several more days for the battle to begin.
No matter who won, I would be gone by the time a victor was decided.
Now it was time to hear what I needed to know.
“Um, there’s something I wanted to ask.”
“Go ahead.”
“I’m still stuck at the Second Rate realm...”
After hearing me out, Jin Wikyung tilted his head.
“You’re Second Rate?”
His tone said he couldn’t understand what I was talking about.
I had utterly crushed Lee Seogeun and even brought down Jopil.
Jin Wikyung had assumed I was First Rate long ago, and so had Jopil.
“Yes.
My realm just won’t rise, so I was hoping you could give me some advice.”
“Advice...”
Jin Wikyung thought for a moment before speaking.
“You’re already First Rate.”
“But I’m Second Rate.”
“I’m telling you, you’re First Rate.
More than that, you’re a Supreme First Rate martial artist standing at the wall of the Peak realm.”
“No, I really am Second Rate...”
“Who told you that?”
Ugh, this is driving me crazy.
I wished I could show him the System Window.
It plainly said Second Rate, but I was the only one who could see it, and the frustration was killing me.
I sighed.
“No one told me I was Second Rate.”
“Then?”
“It’s just...
I’m Second Rate.
I don’t really know how to explain it.”
“Do you believe you’re Second Rate?”
“Yes.”
“Then it’s simple.”
“Wh-what is?”
Is he finally going to reveal the secret to advancing realms?
I stared at Jin Wikyung, my eyes full of anticipation, but he said nothing.
Instead, he dipped a finger into his cold tea and brought it to the table.
Scritch.
A single character appeared.
信
信?
The character for “belief”?
Jin Wikyung took one look at my face and let out a short laugh.
“You look like you’ve just been slapped.”
“...You must be seeing things.”
More like I look like I want to slap you.
“What is this?”
“Exactly what it says.
Believe in yourself.”
“What does that have to do with advancing realms?”
“Because martial arts begin with belief.”
Martial arts begin with belief?
It sounded like airy nonsense.
Yet the moment I heard those words, my heart began to pound.
They begin with belief...
For some reason, that one sentence kept circling through my mind, spinning around and around until I felt dizzy.
What had I believed in all this time?
The first word that came to mind—and the only one—was the System.
The thing that had helped me most in this game, the thing that had always told me nothing but absolute facts.
I had believed I was Second Rate because the System said I was Second Rate.
Because I believed in the System.
I had already overwhelmed Lee Seogeun, a First Rate master.
I had taken down more than twenty wandering martial artists by myself and even defeated Jopil, a Peak master.
Everyone hailed me as a First Rate master and a hero, yet I had remained Second Rate.
Because I had believed in the System instead of myself.
But now I understood.
I’m already First Rate.
Already.
Maybe I had been for a long time.
I was First Rate.
“You look like you’ve just been slapped.”
This time, Jin Wikyung was right.
I slumped against the back of my chair, stunned.
What a dumbass.
If I couldn’t even believe in myself, I was Second Rate.
No.
I had been Second Rate.
Ding.
System — You have reached the First Rate realm!
— The realm of all martial arts increases by one stage!
— Your Muscles and Bones and your Sinews and Meridians improve greatly!
— The size of your dantian expands!
— Level Up!
— Level Up!
From Third Rate to Second Rate.
Then from Second Rate to First Rate.
I felt power surge from deep within me, and Jin Wikyung burst out laughing.
“What happened?”
Wipeng showed up late and asked, looking bewildered.
It felt like a blocked nose had suddenly cleared.
Reaching First Rate had brought a tremendous leap in every way—my senses, my martial arts, everything.
I left the main hall and started walking.
The wind felt cool and refreshing.
“It’s the Third Young Master.”
“Has he fully recovered?”
Sure enough, people’s gazes gathered on me.
I changed course toward an even more crowded area.
Anyone watching would think I was desperate for attention.
But everything happens for a reason.
Ding.
System — Someone gazes at you with awe.
— Fame increases by 1.
— Someone is impressed after hearing rumors about you.
— Fame increases by 1.
As I walked, people gathered around me like clouds.
Among them were plenty of NPCs wearing clothes I had never seen before.
Who are they?
I made eye contact with one of them.
The young man looked to be in his early twenties.
He flinched in surprise, then hurried over and gave me a fist-and-palm salute.
“Gwak of the Samdo Sect presents his respects.”
“Ah, yes.”
By now, the fist-and-palm salute came out on reflex and looked fairly convincing.
But where was the Samdo Sect?
Oh.
Could it be...?
“Are you with the Five Gates of Shanxi?”
Gwak Whatsisname nodded enthusiastically.
“That is correct.
Our Samdo Sect has agreed to lend its strength to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I, Gwak, could not be more delighted to offer what little help I can.”
In a situation like this, he was a reinforcement worth his weight in gold.
I took Gwak Whatsisname by the hand, hoping he would fight hard enough for both of us.
“Thank you for coming.”
“Please, think nothing of it.
It is an honor simply to take part in the Young Master’s tale of martial valor.”
System — Someone is impressed after hearing rumors about you.
— Fame increases by 1.
A total stranger had come all this way to fight for us, and he was even making my Fame shoot up.
I offered the endlessly generous Gwak Whatsisname my warmest thanks.
“God bless you.”
“Pardon?”
“It means I hope the Jade Emperor’s blessing will be with you.”
“Ahh.
Thank you.
God bleshyoo.”
“Ah.
Yes.”
I put on a fake smile and kept walking.
Maybe because everyone who needed to know about me already did, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s people no longer raised my Fame.
Still, I’ve built up quite a bit.
I opened the Status Window and saw that I was about fifty points short of the target.
If I grinded hard for two more days, maybe I could log out.
“Um, Young Hero Jin.”
I turned around.
It was the fellow from the Samdo Sect.
He looked ready to follow me to the ends of the earth.
“If you aren’t busy, perhaps we could have some tea together...”
“I’m sorry.
I have somewhere to be.”
It sounded like a lie, but it was the truth.
My destination had been decided from the start.
I pointed to a building as disappointment crossed his face.
A faded signboard hung above it, and the heavy smell of medicinal decoctions wafted from within.
Medicine King Hall.
Beneath the signboard hung a small wooden plaque.
Authorized Personnel Only.
The people surrounding me let out pitying sighs.

chapters.title: Chapter 35
paragraphs: A hospital room in Medicine King Hall.
Hyuk Mujin, wound tight in bandages from head to toe, let out a groan.
“I’m dying.”
Han Yeop, lying beside him in much the same state, replied,
“It’s a miracle we didn’t die.”
“Right?”
“That’s right.”
A brief silence followed. Both of them were remembering that day.

Jopil’s palm strike. An attack they couldn’t have blocked even if they had known it was coming. Whenever Hyuk Mujin closed his eyes, he saw that bastard’s red-hot palm. It might haunt his nightmares for the rest of his life.
“That monster. How is something like that even possible?”
“He’s a Peak master.”
Unlike the dejected Hyuk Mujin, Han Yeop sounded calm.
“Hey, punk. Doesn’t any of that bother you?”
“What?”
“That...”
Hyuk Mujin found himself at a loss for words. Right. Maybe Han Yeop really was fine.
“No, that’s not what I meant...”
“I know.”
“Huh?”
“I know what you’re thinking, Deputy Squad Leader. I know what you want to say.”
“When I first came to, all kinds of things went through my mind. The relief of being alive. The helplessness I felt that day. The despair over my own martial arts.”
Hyuk Mujin fell silent. Han Yeop had it exactly right. Jopil’s Flame Divine Palm had broken his bones and torn his heart meridian, but his real wound lay elsewhere.
One question had been circling through his mind ever since that day.
Can I ever reach that realm?
Even “overwhelming” didn’t begin to describe it. All his hard work, all the pride he had taken in his martial arts, had been ripped up by the roots.
“You’ve shaken all that off?”
Han Yeop shook his head.
“Then?”
“I accepted that I’m weak. It wasn’t even that hard. I’ve always known it. But...”
“I’ll get stronger. As strong as Jopil. No—much stronger.”
Han Yeop continued, his voice firm.
“Once I started thinking that way, I felt happy. If I become a Peak master, I can be that strong too. That sort of thing.”
“A Peak master...”
The Peak realm was open to only a rare few. Coming from Han Yeop, who was barely second- or third-rate, the declaration was almost laughable.
But Hyuk Mujin didn’t sneer.
You’ve changed too.
So much had changed. Their circumstances. The people around him.
Even that timid second-rate martial artist had been swept up in the current before anyone noticed. Hyuk Mujin felt his heart swell, and the next words burst out before he could stop them.
“I’ll get even stronger.”
Han Yeop’s eyes widened, then he broke into a grin.
“You will. First, though, we have to catch up to one person.”
They both thought of the same man.
Jin Taekyung.
He was already running far ahead of them. What was he doing now?
Behind the two men, lost in thought, the door that had been left slightly ajar quietly slid shut.
I closed the door, turned away, and shuddered from head to toe.
“Ugh, shit.”
These idiots were shooting a teenage coming-of-age drama in a hospital room. I’d stood there listening to see what they were talking about, and what a sight it had been. Seriously.
If I’d gone in, I might’ve ended up swearing brotherhood with them.
Still, I have to admit it was kind of admirable.
We’d been through life and death together, after all. Besides, those two had risked their lives to help me. I’d be lying if I said I didn’t feel even a shred of affection for them.
Could this be the last time I see them?
In two days, I would set out in command of the main force’s rear guard, while those two and the rest of the injured reconnaissance squad stayed behind with the family. And probably...
By then, I’ll have logged out.
I was close to meeting the final condition of the Logout Quest: 500 Fame. Today’s visit to Medicine King Hall was a farewell of sorts.
You could call it the nostalgia filter of a sergeant in his last stretch before discharge.
Well, there’s no need to tell them. Seeing their faces is enough.
I’d already looked in on the other reconnaissance squad members. Now that I’d seen Han Yeop and Hyuk Mujin too, there was only one more place to visit...
Huh?
“Oh!”
A rag doll in one hand. Snacks in the other.
A little girl with her hair tied in a cute ribbon stared at me with round eyes and shouted,
“It’s the mind-reading mister!”
Couldn’t you call me Big Brother? I gave Soyul a sad little wave.
“Young Master Jin.”
“Benefactor!”
The moment I entered the room, they both reacted. I stopped the still-pale Gong Yacheong from rising, then hauled Socheon back to his feet after he dropped into a full bow.
“Stay lying down. And you, get up, punk. Am I old enough to have you bowing to me?”
“You have shown me a kindness a hundred bows could never repay.”
Tears were already welling in both their eyes. Soyul, who didn’t understand what was happening, hugged her rag doll tight and scampered over to cling to her brother.
“Big brother, did you put on the Benefactor’s kindness? Show me too. Is it pretty?”
Uh. That’s clothes, isn’t it?
Leaving the chattering Soyul behind, I turned to Gong Yacheong.
“How are you feeling?”
“Couldn’t be better. Though I’ll need to recuperate for a while.”
A faint smile spread across Gong Yacheong’s lips.
“It is all thanks to you, Young Master.”
“I didn’t do it for praise. I even left you behind once.”
“That was my choice. And you came back.”
I remembered that night Jopil had been chasing us. Gong Yacheong had been badly poisoned and had wanted to stay behind. Just as he had, I’d had to make a choice.
After a long struggle with myself, I had decided to go back for him.
And I regretted it like crazy.
It had been insane. Gambling my life for a mere NPC in a game. But now I thought I understood why I had made that choice.
What had I seen in those young siblings who had lost their parents? Who had Gong Yacheong and the reconnaissance squad reminded me of...?
“Young Master Jin?”
Gong Yacheong’s voice pulled me back.
“It’s nothing. I just—just had something on my mind.”
“Ah, I heard the news as well. Is that what this is about?”
“What news?”
“They say there will soon be a major battle.”
Wasn’t that military intelligence?
If Gong Yacheong, who never left his hospital room, knew about it, then everyone in the Jin Family of Taiyuan with eyes and ears must know.
If there was even one spy among us, we might as well have installed a loudspeaker aimed at North Korea.
Is this war really going to be all right like this?
I shook off the thought. What did it matter to me? Soon enough, none of this would have anything to do with me anyway.
The System alerts ringing even now were proof.
Ding.
System — Rumors about you continue to spread. — Fame increases by 1.
As the saying went, words without feet could travel a thousand li. Ever since I’d taken Jopil down, my name seemed to have started spreading in earnest.
I opened the Quest Window for a quick look. I had only about fifty Fame left to go.
Logout was practically a foregone conclusion.
“It will be a battle with our family’s fate at stake.”
Of course, neither of them had any way of knowing my situation. I listened quietly to Gong Yacheong and Socheon for a while, then rose from my seat.
“I should get going.”
“Benefactor.”
Socheon looked disappointed, but Gong Yacheong stopped him.
“Let him go.”
“That is enough.”
Socheon lowered his head glumly. Soyul, who had been playing alone with her doll, looked up at me with huge eyes.
“You’re leaving already, mister?”
“I said Big Brother.”
“Okay. Mister.”
I gave her chubby cheek a light pinch and was about to turn away when Gong Yacheong called out to me.
“Young Master Jin. Even if you must leave, should you not take what you left behind?”
“What I left behind?”
I thought about it for a moment, but there was no way I’d forgotten anything. Thanks to the cheat feature known as Inventory, I always traveled light.
“I didn’t leave anyth—what is this?”
Gong Yacheong was holding a long bundle.
“You were in no state to collect it at the time. Now that its owner has come, it is only right that I return it.”
What is it?
Still bewildered, I took the bundle. It was fairly heavy. Just as I was about to check what was inside, Gong Yacheong spoke.
“Unwrap it in your quarters. Do not let anyone else see.”
Did he put a golden calf in here?
I unwrapped the bundle the moment I reached my quarters. Then I understood what Gong Yacheong’s last words had meant.
These really are the sort of things people would covet if they saw them.
An old booklet. A small box. And a familiar sword.
To someone in Murim, these were beyond comparison to any golden calf. And I had the ability to judge that value more accurately than anyone.
Check Item.
Ding.

System Item Window Flame Divine Palm Type: Martial Arts Manual Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Holder of Scorching Yang Qi Description: One of the Fire Gate Clan’s secret techniques. A martial art based on powerful fire qi. Effect: Acquired Flame Divine Palm Item Window Blazing Flame Divine Pill Type: Spiritual Elixir Grade: Peak Restriction: None Description: A spiritual elixir made according to the Fire Gate Clan’s secret formula. Effect: Grants thirty years of internal energy when consumed. However, if the user cannot control the powerful fire qi contained within the elixir, they may meet a horrific end. Item Window Unnamed Sword Type: Sword Grade: None Restriction: None Description: Made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, this sword is exceptionally sharp and durable. After drinking a great deal of blood over many years, it transformed on its own. Special conditions are required to draw out the sword’s power. Effect: Unknown
“This is insane.”
It really was insane. A Supreme Peak martial arts manual. A spiritual elixir that granted thirty years of internal energy. And a sword I didn’t fully understand, but that looked ridiculously good.
They said a tiger left its pelt behind when it died, but Jopil had left three treasures behind.
Shit. It always gives me the good stuff after everything’s over.
Damn shitty game. If it was going to give me something, it should’ve done it sooner. Waiting until everything was finished to play catch-up just made my blood pressure spike.
Still, these items are seriously good.
Reading the descriptions, I couldn’t help feeling tempted. What if I took the elixir and learned Flame Divine Palm? If fire started shooting from my hands like Jopil’s...
That would be fucking cool.

But the thought lasted only a moment. They said a soldier nearing the end of his service had to watch out even for falling leaves. I had no intention of swallowing the elixir wrong and staging my own self-immolation ceremony.
Remember. Safety first. Safety first.
Talking about safety after everything I’d done was pretty funny, but I wasn’t stupid enough to gulp it down without thinking.
It’s almost over.
One wrong step and I was finished. I stuffed all the items into my Inventory. Somewhere in the dead of night, someone must have been talking about me over drinks, because a System alert rang out.
Ding.
System — Fame has increased by 1.
At that hour, the Head Elder was strolling through the garden.
This was the agreed-upon date and place. The man waiting in the darkness was never late.
“The moon is very bright tonight.”
“So it is.”
As he had said, the full moon shone exceptionally brightly.
“When I was young, I loved the moon... but the older I got, the more I found myself thinking.”
“Thinking what?”
“That I wished the moon didn’t exist. Something like that.”
“A world without charm.”
“What’s wrong with a little less charm? I make my living at night, so I’d be delighted if the moon disappeared.”
Night life, huh.
The man prattled on in the flippant, cheerful tone of a kept man, but the Head Elder knew the truth. He possessed formidable martial arts and was a superb assassin.
The wind seemed to carry the smell of blood.
“Ah, right. How is the work progressing?”
“Smoothly. Even the troop deployments are complete.”
“Do not overdo it. If the clever Lesser Family Head catches the scent, everything will fall apart.”
“Do not worry. I did not even need to make a move.”
“Heaven is helping us.”
“And your side?”
“You are asking the obvious.”
The mild reproach in his voice silenced the Head Elder.
As if it could be otherwise.

They were like sea fog. Their identities lay hidden within the mist, and no matter how one reached out and stirred it, there was nothing solid to grasp. All that remained was a damp palm and an unpleasant feeling.
But they have power.
The power to make him Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the sole hegemon of Shanxi Province.
It was an ambition he had harbored for half his life. The Head Elder was prepared to do anything.
“All preparations are complete.”
“Mine as well.”
On the day the two great sects that divided Shanxi between them clashed...
Everything would end, and everything would begin anew.

Soyul, who didn’t understand what was happening, hugged her rag doll tight and scampered over to cling to her brother.
“Big brother, did you put on the Benefactor’s kindness?
Show me too.
Is it pretty?”
Uh.
That’s clothes, isn’t it?
Leaving the chattering Soyul behind, I turned to Gong Yacheong.
“How are you feeling?”
“Couldn’t be better.
Though I’ll need to recuperate for a while.”
A faint smile spread across Gong Yacheong’s lips.
“It is all thanks to you, Young Master.”
“I didn’t do it for praise.
I even left you behind once.”
“That was my choice.
And you came back.”
I remembered that night Jopil had been chasing us.
Gong Yacheong had been badly poisoned and had wanted to stay behind.
Just as he had, I’d had to make a choice.
After a long struggle with myself, I had decided to go back for him.
And I regretted it like crazy.
It had been insane.
Gambling my life for a mere NPC in a game.
But now I thought I understood why I had made that choice.
What had I seen in those young siblings who had lost their parents?
Who had Gong Yacheong and the reconnaissance squad reminded me of...?
“Young Master Jin?”
Gong Yacheong’s voice pulled me back.
“It’s nothing.
I just—just had something on my mind.”
“Ah, I heard the news as well.
Is that what this is about?”
“What news?”
“They say there will soon be a major battle.”
Wasn’t that military intelligence?
If Gong Yacheong, who never left his hospital room, knew about it, then everyone in the Jin Family of Taiyuan with eyes and ears must know.
If there was even one spy among us, we might as well have installed a loudspeaker aimed at North Korea.
Is this war really going to be all right like this?
I shook off the thought.
What did it matter to me?
Soon enough, none of this would have anything to do with me anyway.
The System alerts ringing even now were proof.
Ding.
System — Rumors about you continue to spread.
— Fame increases by 1.
As the saying went, words without feet could travel a thousand li.
Ever since I’d taken Jopil down, my name seemed to have started spreading in earnest.
I opened the Quest Window for a quick look.
I had only about fifty Fame left to go.
Logout was practically a foregone conclusion.
“It will be a battle with our family’s fate at stake.”
Of course, neither of them had any way of knowing my situation.
I listened quietly to Gong Yacheong and Socheon for a while, then rose from my seat.
“I should get going.”
“Benefactor.”
Socheon looked disappointed, but Gong Yacheong stopped him.
“Let him go.”
“That is enough.”
Socheon lowered his head glumly.
Soyul, who had been playing alone with her doll, looked up at me with huge eyes.
“You’re leaving already, mister?”
“I said Big Brother.”
“Okay.
Mister.”
I gave her chubby cheek a light pinch and was about to turn away when Gong Yacheong called out to me.
“Young Master Jin.
Even if you must leave, should you not take what you left behind?”
“What I left behind?”
I thought about it for a moment, but there was no way I’d forgotten anything.
Thanks to the cheat feature known as Inventory, I always traveled light.
“I didn’t leave anyth—what is this?”
Gong Yacheong was holding a long bundle.
“You were in no state to collect it at the time.
Now that its owner has come, it is only right that I return it.”
What is it?
Still bewildered, I took the bundle.
It was fairly heavy.
Just as I was about to check what was inside, Gong Yacheong spoke.
“Unwrap it in your quarters.
Do not let anyone else see.”
Did he put a golden calf in here?
I unwrapped the bundle the moment I reached my quarters.
Then I understood what Gong Yacheong’s last words had meant.
These really are the sort of things people would covet if they saw them.
An old booklet.
A small box.
And a familiar sword.
To someone in Murim, these were beyond comparison to any golden calf.
And I had the ability to judge that value more accurately than anyone.
Check Item.
Ding.
System Item Window Flame Divine Palm Type: Martial Arts Manual Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Holder of Scorching Yang Qi Description: One of the Fire Gate Clan’s secret techniques.
A martial art based on powerful fire qi.

Effect: Acquired Flame Divine Palm Item Window Blazing Flame Divine Pill Type: Spiritual Elixir Grade: Peak Restriction: None Description: A spiritual elixir made according to the Fire Gate Clan’s secret formula.
Effect: Grants thirty years of internal energy when consumed.
However, if the user cannot control the powerful fire qi contained within the elixir, they may meet a horrific end.
Item Window Unnamed Sword Type: Sword Grade: None Restriction: None Description: Made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, this sword is exceptionally sharp and durable.
After drinking a great deal of blood over many years, it transformed on its own.
Special conditions are required to draw out the sword’s power.
Effect: Unknown
“This is insane.”
It really was insane.
A Supreme Peak martial arts manual.
A spiritual elixir that granted thirty years of internal energy.
And a sword I didn’t fully understand, but that looked ridiculously good.
They said a tiger left its pelt behind when it died, but Jopil had left three treasures behind.
Shit.
It always gives me the good stuff after everything’s over.
Damn shitty game.
If it was going to give me something, it should’ve done it sooner.
Waiting until everything was finished to play catch-up just made my blood pressure spike.
Still, these items are seriously good.
Reading the descriptions, I couldn’t help feeling tempted.
What if I took the elixir and learned Flame Divine Palm?
If fire started shooting from my hands like Jopil’s...
That would be fucking cool.
But the thought lasted only a moment.
They said a soldier nearing the end of his service had to watch out even for falling leaves.
I had no intention of swallowing the elixir wrong and staging my own self-immolation ceremony.
Remember.
Safety first.
Safety first.
Talking about safety after everything I’d done was pretty funny, but I wasn’t stupid enough to gulp it down without thinking.
It’s almost over.
One wrong step and I was finished.
I stuffed all the items into my Inventory.
Somewhere in the dead of night, someone must have been talking about me over drinks, because a System alert rang out.
Ding.
System — Fame has increased by 1.
At that hour, the Head Elder was strolling through the garden.
This was the agreed-upon date and place.
The man waiting in the darkness was never late.
“The moon is very bright tonight.”
“So it is.”
As he had said, the full moon shone exceptionally brightly.
“When I was young, I loved the moon... but the older I got, the more I found myself thinking.”
“Thinking what?”
“That I wished the moon didn’t exist.
Something like that.”
“A world without charm.”
“What’s wrong with a little less charm?
I make my living at night, so I’d be delighted if the moon disappeared.”
Night life, huh.
The man prattled on in the flippant, cheerful tone of a kept man, but the Head Elder knew the truth.
He possessed formidable martial arts and was a superb assassin.
The wind seemed to carry the smell of blood.
“Ah, right.
How is the work progressing?”
“Smoothly.
Even the troop deployments are complete.”
“Do not overdo it.
If the clever Lesser Family Head catches the scent, everything will fall apart.”
“Do not worry.
I did not even need to make a move.”
“Heaven is helping us.”
“And your side?”
“You are asking the obvious.”
The mild reproach in his voice silenced the Head Elder.
As if it could be otherwise.
They were like sea fog.
Their identities lay hidden within the mist, and no matter how one reached out and stirred it, there was nothing solid to grasp.
All that remained was a damp palm and an unpleasant feeling.
But they have power.
The power to make him Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the sole hegemon of Shanxi Province.
It was an ambition he had harbored for half his life.
The Head Elder was prepared to do anything.
“All preparations are complete.”
“Mine as well.”
On the day the two great sects that divided Shanxi between them clashed...
Everything would end, and everything would begin anew.

chapters.title: Chapter 36
paragraphs: System Quest Logout You must now make your way through this harsh Murim. Become even stronger, and become famous. For the day that will one day come... Grade: Main Quest Restriction: Jin Taekyung Objective: Reach the First Rate realm (Complete) Reach Lv. 30 (Complete) Reach Fame 500 (475/500) Reward: Logout
I closed the Quest Window. It was the middle of winter, but I felt a cold sweat coming on.
If this keeps up, I’m completely screwed.

My Fame had been creeping upward little by little, only to stop dead half a day ago. I’d bolted out of my quarters and gone around shaking hands like a presidential candidate until my hands nearly fell off, but the notification I was waiting for never came.
No, I did get a notification.
Beep!
System — There is no one in the Jin Family of Taiyuan who does not know of your Fame.
It was the System’s way of telling me I’d already milked this place for all the Fame it was worth, so I should knock it off. Even the System seemed to find me pitiful.
And so an entire day slipped helplessly away. Today was the long-awaited departure ceremony.
“Fuck...”
As I muttered the curse under my breath, Jin Wikyung was climbing onto the platform.

Hundreds of pairs of eyes followed him. The martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and those from the small and mid-sized sects that had recently joined us stood in formation across the Grand Training Ground, more than five hundred strong.
Boom. Boom. Boom.

A tremendous rumble began to spread. Some stamped their feet; others struck their weapons. When five hundred martial artists with internal energy moved as one, the earth shook and a deafening roar filled heaven and earth.
What the...?
I had never seen anything like it. No longer individuals, they had become a single army, waiting for one man’s command.
At last, Jin Wikyung spoke.
“I will not deny it. The enemy surpasses us both in troop numbers and in the number of Peak masters.”
Silence descended in an instant. But Jin Wikyung wasn’t foolish enough to crush morale with his opening words. The force of his presence was proof of that.
“However.”
His usual good-natured smile was nowhere to be seen. The Jin Wikyung standing before us was both a Peak martial artist and the head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“They are nothing but jackals with numbers on their side. That man’s rabble—wandering martial artists blinded by gold, and a pack of mounted bandits who have plundered the common people!”
The air crackled beneath his fiery shout. For that moment, even I felt my blood begin to boil.
“They have neither cause nor justice.”
Cause. Justice.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had lost the two most important things in any war.
That was why the small and mid-sized sects of Shanxi Province, which had only watched from the sidelines while the two great powers fought, had sent reinforcements.
“This war will be over within three days.”
Fifteen hundred martial artists would clash at the same hour on the same day.
It would be a hellish battle of killing and being killed.
“No one here can be certain whether they will live or die. However...”
Jin Wikyung’s flashing gaze swept across them all.
“We will prevail.”
The next moment, a roar erupted loud enough to leave my ears ringing. With the crowd’s fervor at its peak, Jin Wikyung towered over them like a giant.
“Survival of the fittest! Put your lives on the line, fight, and survive!”
The cheering continued for a long time afterward.

Our five hundred troops were divided into the vanguard, center, and rear guard. Most of our core fighting strength had been assigned to the vanguard and center, so the rear guard under my command consisted of only a few dozen martial artists.
Among them were several familiar faces.
“Captain!”
They were members of the reconnaissance squad. Both pleased and puzzled, I asked, “Why are you guys here? Weren’t you at Medicine King Hall?”
“This battle will decide the fate of our family. We can’t sit it out just because we’re a little injured.”
When I’d secretly visited them last time, some of them had still had cracked bones in their arms and legs. Murim people really were tough as hell.
“We asked to be placed under your command, and the higher-ups readily approved it. We’ve been able to walk around with our chests puffed out ever since that day. Haha.”
“Well, look at you.”
A quiet laugh escaped me.
I’d spent several days with them during the reconnaissance mission, but I still didn’t know some of their names. Even so, I felt close to them. We had been through life and death together.
They say three raids are enough to make sworn brothers.
I smiled at the eight members of the reconnaissance squad. Then something occurred to me.
No, wait.
Eight? Had I counted wrong?

I started counting again from the end, one person at a time. There had originally been nine, not including me. Hyuk Mujin and Han Yeop had both been severely injured, so naturally neither of them should have been here. That meant there should have been seven, but...
“...What are you doing here?”
Even as I stared at him, I couldn’t be sure it was really the same guy. His face was puffed up like a steamed bun, and the skin showing beyond his clothes was red and blotchy.
“Can’t you tell by looking?”
Right. There was only one bastard on the reconnaissance squad rude enough to answer like that.
“Hyuk Mujin?”
“Yes. Why? What?”
“Are you really Hyuk Mujin?”
“You can’t even recognize my face anymore?”
Looking like that, even your parents wouldn’t recognize you...
More importantly, why the hell was he here?
“Did you volunteer too?”
“I did.”
Then he added, “They wouldn’t take me, though.”
“Huh?”
“I told the physician, and he got angry and asked if I was out of my mind and trying to get myself killed. So I snuck out.”
I spoke seriously.
“Are you out of your mind and trying to get yourself killed?”
“I want to live.”
Hyuk Mujin answered with a sour expression.
“Then why did you come?”
“I know my own condition. I can fight well enough.”
“Your face looks ready to burst.”
“The swelling is going down. My internal injuries are completely healed, so there’s no problem.”
“What about your external injuries?”
“They’ll heal on the way.”
“A few bones are cracked, but I can handle—urk!”
Hyuk Mujin suddenly doubled over. Startled, I shouted, “Hey! What’s wrong?”
“Sometimes my chest hurts when I breathe... Ah, it’s fine now.”
Was this guy completely insane?
As I stood there speechless, Hyuk Mujin continued.
“Ah, Han Yeop couldn’t come. His internal injuries still haven’t healed, so he would’ve only been a burden. Captain? Captain, you are listening to me, right?”
There was only one thought in my head.
Logout. I need to log out, now.
Night came early in winter. The sun set, and after we had walked for who knew how long, we finally entered a broad basin and received the order to make camp.
“Ugh, every bone in my body hurts.”
Hyuk Mujin groaned. He clearly hadn’t fully recovered, and the march seemed to be taking its toll.
“It’s not too late. Want to turn back?”
“Are you saying that again?”
“I’m saying it because you look like you’re struggling.”
“You’re imagining things. Does Hyuk Mujin the man look like someone who’d be exhausted after walking for a mere half day?”
I nodded without the slightest hesitation.
“Yep.”
“Absolutely not!”
“Hmm. You’re really not tired? You’re fine?”
“Yes.”
“Then go help the others set up camp.”
At that moment, Hyuk Mujin the man’s eyes widened, and he sank to the ground.
“Ugh, the internal injuries Jopil gave me...”
You said your internal injuries were completely healed, you bastard.
I was wondering whether I should give him a good smack when a voice interrupted us.
“Is he injured?”
A huge shadow stretched beneath the moonlight. Hyuk Mujin cautiously raised his head to see who it was, and his eyes flew open.
“Gasp! Lesser Family Head!”
If Jin Wikyung was a division commander, Hyuk Mujin was a private.
The next moment, Hyuk Mujin sprang up like lightning and stood at attention. Jin Wikyung burst out laughing.
“You still don’t look fully recovered. Go ahead and lie down. Ah, but your internal injuries certainly seem to have healed. I’ll vouch for that.”
“Ah, I... That isn’t...”
Jin Wikyung lightly patted the flustered Hyuk Mujin on the shoulder, then turned to me.
“Shall we walk for a bit?”
I followed Jin Wikyung to a secluded corner. He spoke first.
“How are you feeling?”
“Good.”
I’d gotten full use out of the level-up. My body had recovered at a terrifying speed, and distributing my points had made it even stronger.
The problem lay elsewhere.
My Fame isn’t going up.
No, it was going up. By a rat dropping’s worth. Little by little. Very, very little.
At this rate, there was no guarantee I’d be able to log out before the fighting started.
At least, not if things stayed like this.
Jin Wikyung’s arrival was perfect timing. I brought up the idea I’d been mulling over.
“I want a mission.”
His eyes widened at my blunt request.
“Hm? A mission?”
“Now that I’ve recovered, I want to distinguish myself for our family.”
I was proud of myself. To think I could deliver a line like that—a lie like that—with a straight face.
“I-is that truly what you think?”
“Yes.”
The corners of Jin Wikyung’s eyes trembled. He seemed overcome with emotion.
This is actually making me feel a little guilty.
The only reason I was putting on this ridiculous act was to gain Fame. If I went out on a reconnaissance mission and accomplished something, the Fame would come rolling in.
Even better if I ran into a reconnaissance unit from the Mount Heng Sword Sect. They would provide excellent EXP and enough Fame to fill the rest of the bar.
Once the real battle starts, I’m screwed.
I had to log out before then, and fast. I spoke with firm resolve.
“Just leave it to me.”
“What made you think of doing something so admirable? Thank you, my youngest.”
Jin Wikyung wiped the damp corners of his eyes with his sleeve and continued.
“But no.”
“Then give me a reconnaissance mission—what?”
“I appreciate the thought. Continue guarding the rear.”
What the hell is he talking about?
I barely suppressed the urge to grab him by the collar and shake him.
“I-I really want to distinguish myself.”
“You’ve already done more than enough.”
“No, that’s not what I mean.”
“The merits you’ve earned so far have already been a tremendous help to our family. So don’t trouble yourself over it.”
“I’d like you to give me at least one reconnaissance mission. There might be enemies lying in ambush ahead...”
Jin Wikyung chuckled.
“This battle will decide our family’s fate. Do you think I wouldn’t have accounted for something like that?”
“Couldn’t there be a one-in-ten-thousand chance that something was overlooked?”
“That is quite literally a one-in-ten-thousand chance.”
Damn it.
Nothing was going my way. What if I really failed to reach the required Fame? Then I would have to fight in a massive battle involving fifteen hundred people.
I’m fucked.
Something large and warm settled on my dejected shoulder. Jin Wikyung’s hand.
“Youngest.”
His voice was heavy and lonely. At the sudden shift in mood, I fell silent and listened.
“Your mission is more important than anyone else’s.”
“What is my mission?”
After a long pause, he forced out a single word.
“Survive.”
“What?”
“Survive, no matter what. If our family loses, run without looking back.”
“If the roots survive, the tree will grow again. Second Brother and you could become better roots than I ever could.”
I was speechless. For a long time, all I could do was stare at his face.
Survive. Become roots.
His voice and gaze carried a gravity that struck me more deeply than ever before.
“That is your mission.”
The palm resting on my shoulder slid slowly down. I stared after Jin Wikyung’s departing back, unable to look away.

This is actually making me feel a little guilty.
The only reason I was putting on this ridiculous act was to gain Fame.
If I went out on a reconnaissance mission and accomplished something, the Fame would come rolling in.
Even better if I ran into a reconnaissance unit from the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
They would provide excellent EXP and enough Fame to fill the rest of the bar.
Once the real battle starts, I’m screwed.
I had to log out before then, and fast.
I spoke with firm resolve.
“Just leave it to me.”
“What made you think of doing something so admirable?
Thank you, my youngest.”
Jin Wikyung wiped the damp corners of his eyes with his sleeve and continued.
“But no.”
“Then give me a reconnaissance mission—what?”
“I appreciate the thought.
Continue guarding the rear.”
What the hell is he talking about?
I barely suppressed the urge to grab him by the collar and shake him.
“I-I really want to distinguish myself.”
“You’ve already done more than enough.”
“No, that’s not what I mean.”
“The merits you’ve earned so far have already been a tremendous help to our family.
So don’t trouble yourself over it.”
“I’d like you to give me at least one reconnaissance mission.
There might be enemies lying in ambush ahead...”
Jin Wikyung chuckled.
“This battle will decide our family’s fate.
Do you think I wouldn’t have accounted for something like that?”
“Couldn’t there be a one-in-ten-thousand chance that something was overlooked?”
“That is quite literally a one-in-ten-thousand chance.”
Damn it.
Nothing was going my way.
What if I really failed to reach the required Fame?
Then I would have to fight in a massive battle involving fifteen hundred people.
I’m fucked.
Something large and warm settled on my dejected shoulder.
Jin Wikyung’s hand.
“Youngest.”
His voice was heavy and lonely.
At the sudden shift in mood, I fell silent and listened.
“Your mission is more important than anyone else’s.”
“What is my mission?”
After a long pause, he forced out a single word.
“Survive.”
“What?”
“Survive, no matter what.
If our family loses, run without looking back.”
“If the roots survive, the tree will grow again.
Second Brother and you could become better roots than I ever could.”
I was speechless.
For a long time, all I could do was stare at his face.
Survive.
Become roots.
His voice and gaze carried a gravity that struck me more deeply than ever before.
“That is your mission.”
The palm resting on my shoulder slid slowly down.
I stared after Jin Wikyung’s departing back, unable to look away.

chapters.title: Chapter 37
paragraphs: The march went smoothly. The heavy snow that had fallen during our last reconnaissance mission had melted long ago, and command set a pace that conserved as much of the troops’ strength as possible.
“At this rate, we’ll reach Jeongyang by tomorrow at the latest.”
I blinked at the oddly familiar man’s words.
“Who are you?”

Judging by his clothes, he wasn’t from the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Aside from the reconnaissance squad, most of the rear guard consisted of martial artists from the newly allied small and mid-sized sects, so that made sense.
“I’m Gwak Jun of the Samdo Sect. We met once before... We even shook hands.”
Gwak Jun of the Samdo Sect? It felt like I should remember him.
It wasn’t as if I’d shaken only one or two hands trying to raise my Fame.
He was probably one of them.
“Sorry. My memory isn’t very good.”
“I wasn’t expecting you to remember, honestly. Haha.”
Gwak Jun gave me a friendly smile and continued.
“To be honest, I was disappointed at first when I found out we’d been assigned to the rear guard.”
“Why?”
“Because there’d be fewer chances to distinguish ourselves. Isn’t this the perfect opportunity for an unknown grunt like me to make a name for himself?”
“Ah. Right.”
There were two possibilities in cases like this. Either he’d fought in so many battles that he’d developed nerves of steel, or he simply had no fear.
I raised my Qi Sense.
Ding.
System Lv.40 Gwak Jun
Oh. He’s pretty good.
At Level 40, he was at least First Rate. He couldn’t exactly go around bragging that he was a master, but he was good enough to resent being stuck in the rear.

“Half of the enemy troops were recruited in a hurry. They’ve dragged in every kind of deadweight, and they must have force-marched to join the main force. They won’t stand a chance against the elites of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Samdo Sect.”
His argument sounded plausible enough.
If you leave out the part about the Samdo Sect being elite.
I nodded halfheartedly.
“I see.”

“And our Peak masters are superior to theirs. There’s the Lesser Family Head and Great Hero Wipeng, of course, but the fame of the Blade of Flowers has spread throughout the Central Plains, hasn’t it?”
The Blade of Flowers. It was the first time I’d heard the title, but I could guess who he meant.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan had three Peak masters. Excluding Jin Wikyung and Wipeng, only one person remained.
The Head Elder.
Was that old man really that strong?
Everything Gwak Jun said next was praise. Title after title, name after name of masters the Head Elder had cut down in his youth decades ago came spilling out.
“He was a hero born of the Great Faction War.”
A war hero from the past. Listening to Gwak Jun, he sounded like the noblest of chivalrous heroes—a man who loved justice and couldn’t stand to see injustice go unpunished...
Then why do I feel uneasy every time I see him?
Maybe it was because of my first impression, but I didn’t like the Head Elder.
That peculiar air of his. The strange gaze that seemed to bore straight through people. The fact that he had formed a political faction in opposition to Jin Wikyung.
Since then, however, the Head Elder had thrown his full support behind Jin Wikyung, allowing the Jin Family of Taiyuan to present a united front both inside and out.
Well, when an outside enemy invades, even family feuds have to stop.
The Head Elder was currently leading the vanguard alongside Jin Wikyung. If he truly was as skilled as the rumors claimed, tomorrow’s battle would be that much easier.
“Just thinking of Great Hero Blade of Flowers sweeping the battlefield tomorrow already has my heart racing.”
Gwak Jun shuddered like a man finally taking a piss after holding it for three days.
Does this bastard not know what tension is?
And where was he getting all this confidence that we were going to win?
“You sound certain we’ll win.”
“If we lose, we’ll be in big trouble.”
“Excuse me?”
Not big trouble. We’d be finished.
Judging by everything the Mount Heng Sword Sect had done so far, they would raze not only the Jin Family of Taiyuan but every small and mid-sized sect allied with us.
“What do you mean by—”
“I’m joking.”
This bastard’s a lunatic too.
As I stared at him in disbelief, Gwak Jun flashed me a grin.
“We’ll win. We will.”
The words rang with absolute conviction.
After Gwak Jun walked away, Hyuk Mujin came over and asked,
“Who was that?”
“Level 40.”
“What?”
“Just some guy overflowing with confidence.”
I didn’t like him for several reasons.
Well, it wasn’t as though I’d ever have to talk to him again.
Time passed quickly. On the second night of the march, we reached Honju, and Jin Wikyung gathered the command staff for a meeting. He held a small slip of paper in one hand.
“A letter from the Lower District Sect. The enemy reinforcements crossed Mount Otae two days ago.”
“Then...”
“They’re likely to join the main force around now, or sometime tomorrow.”
What?
I didn’t understand. If we had attacked the main force before the reinforcements joined them, the battle would have been much easier.
He must have something in mind.
Sure enough, Jin Wikyung continued.

“The enemy reinforcements are exhausted, and their food supplies are nearly gone. If we seize the advantageous ground at Jeongyang first tomorrow, the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect will face a choice. Retreat or clash with us.”
The next moment, Jin Wikyung looked at me.
“What choice do you think he’ll make?”
The sudden question caught me off guard, but the answer was obvious. If he were the kind of man to retreat at this point, he would have done so long ago.
“I think he’ll clash with us.”
They had nearly twice our numbers, and they weren’t behind us in Peak masters either. From the enemy’s perspective, the best option was to end the battle quickly and decisively.
“Exactly.”
Jin Wikyung smiled in satisfaction and traced a finger across the topographic map spread over the table.
“There are four routes the enemy can take into Jeongyang. But with their food situation as it is, they’ll choose the fastest one.”
His finger stopped on a place labeled Eight Spring Gorge. The Head Elder, who had been sitting quietly until then, spoke for the first time.
“Eight Spring Gorge. Jar-shaped, with a narrow, steep entrance. The mounted bandits will have to abandon their prized horses.”
“They’ll have to abandon their lives as well.”
“The enemy will fight with their lives on the line. This alone will not be enough.”
“I’ve hidden some hundred horn bows on the cliffs above the gorge.”
“Hoh.”
A stir ran through the tent. I stared at Jin Wikyung with my mouth open.
When the hell did he hide those there?
“Right after our victory at Honju. Thanks to a resourceful helper.”
Jin Wikyung looked straight at me as he spoke.
The Lower District Sect. Wolhwa.
She had been helping us constantly from places we couldn’t see. Of course, Jin Wikyung was impressive too, for putting together a plan this big.
That’s fucking cool.
A body like a human meat grinder and a brilliant mind to go with it. Suddenly I wanted to call him hyung.
“Oh!”
“Lesser Family Head...!”
The tent grew hot beneath the burning gazes of all those rough-looking men.
Jin Wikyung swept his solemn gaze over everyone assembled.
“Let’s settle this.”
No one objected. The Head Elder was the first to rise and give Jin Wikyung a fist-in-palm salute.
“By your command.”
That brought the meeting to an end. As I left the tent, a familiar voice pierced my ear.
“Do not forget what I told you yesterday.”
I stiffened for a moment, then gave a small nod.
At dawn, three hundred martial artists from the Jin Family of Taiyuan and one hundred fifty reinforcements from the small and mid-sized sects—four hundred fifty in all—departed for the gorge.
Even though this was goodbye, I never got to say it properly.
I climbed a hill and stared for a long time at the winding line of torches.
The next morning, Hyuk Mujin flinched when he saw me and stepped back.
“You startled me. What happened?”
“What?”
“What do you mean, what? You look like a walking corpse. Didn’t you sleep?”
“Nah. I slept a little.”
That was a lie. I hadn’t slept a wink. I had spent the entire night perched on a rock, staring at the System Window.
Eagerly awaiting the moment that had finally drawn near.
System Achieve Fame 500 (497/500)
I never knew the number one could feel so precious.
In a voice that seemed to have aged overnight, I muttered,
“I’m going, I’m going, now I’m going home...”
“Now you’re even talking to yourself. Have you lost your mind?”
Hyuk Mujin clicked his tongue, then his eyes widened.
“What are those? I’ve never seen them before.”
“These?”
I pointed in turn at the old book and the small box resting on the rock.
“One’s a martial arts manual. The other’s an elixir.”
“Gasp. Really?”
I listlessly explained to the guy whose eyes were halfway out of their sockets.
“The manual contains a Supreme Peak martial art, and if you absorb the elixir properly, it’ll give you half a jiazi.”
“What?”
“But if you take the elixir wrong, apparently you’ll burn to death. Want it?”
“Ah. Sure...”
Judging by his unimpressed face and the way his lips were sticking out a mile, he didn’t believe a damn word I was saying.
Well, if someone suddenly came at me with a Supreme Peak martial art and a thirty-year Fireball elixir, I’d assume it was a joke too.
“You really won’t eat it? It’s good stuff.”
“Oh, I’m fine. Learn plenty of that Supreme Peak martial art, and make sure you chew your elixir thoroughly.”
“I don’t need this kind of thing anymore.”
“Of course not. You’re the Hidden Dragon.”
Normally, I would have smacked him in the back of the head. Right now, I didn’t feel much of anything.
Is this how a short-timer sergeant feels?
At the same time, I felt strangely wistful. Maybe it was an aftereffect of everything I’d been through. I had only been here for a little over a month, yet it felt as though a whole year had passed.
I began tracing back through my memories.
I first opened my eyes at Honghwaru.
That was where I met Wolhwa for the first time and realized I was trapped in this game. Even now, thinking about that moment gave me goose bumps.
I really thought I was going to lose my mind.
It had taken me three days just to decide to go to the Jin Family of Taiyuan. And the guy I met there was this one—Hyuk Mujin.
Smack!
“Argh! Why did you hit me?”
“Hmm. Just thinking about the old days.”
“What old days?”
“Nope. Not telling. Now hurry back.”
“What are you, some back-alley thug? Just because your martial arts are a bit stronger, you think you can bully people like this?”
As Hyuk Mujin threw a fit, everyone turned to look at us. Even the reconnaissance-squad members who had been watching from the sidelines joined in.
“What are you two talking about?”
“Dunno. The deputy captain must have done something wrong.”
“Hey, I didn’t do anything!”
“This is Murim. Being weak is a crime.”
“But should we really be acting like this?”
At someone’s words, silence fell for a moment.
“True. Waiting here is our mission, but...”

The tension and fear they had been suppressing with forced smiles rose to the surface. Even I, who would soon be returning to the real world, felt uneasy whenever Jin Wikyung’s face came to mind. How much worse must it be for these guys?
There was only one thing I could say.
“I trust my hyung.”
Hyung.
This time, I put my heart into the word.
Jin Wikyung had been my greatest source of strength in this place. Maybe I simply wanted to shake off that unease, even if only by saying it aloud.
The tension eased from everyone’s faces.
“We feel the same.”
Hyuk Mujin slipped in as well.
“I trust the Captain more.”
“Wow. Deputy Captain, you’re awfully quick to switch sides.”
“You little bastards. Is there anyone here who doesn’t owe the Captain their life?”
“Well, when you put it that way, what can we say?”
“I trust the Captain too. Honestly, I knew all along, even when you were pretending to be a thug. I thought, Ah, that man is the Hidden Dragon. I could tell right away.”
It felt strange.
Even dried squid gives up water if you squeeze it hard enough. Who knew I’d feel something like this toward NPCs in a game?
Well, honestly... it doesn’t feel bad.
Suddenly, I found myself wondering about Jin Wikyung, somewhere beyond those mountains. Had the battle started? If so, which side was winning?
And I wasn’t the only one thinking about it.
“By now, the battle must have started.”
It was Gwak Jun of the Samdo Sect. Unlike before, he was dressed in black martial robes.
Was that what he was wearing before?
When he noticed me looking, Gwak Jun shrugged.
“I like this sort of thing. It’s easy to move in, and even if a little blood splatters on it, no one can tell. You agree, don’t you?”
The last question wasn’t directed at us. It was meant for the Samdo Sect martial artists under his command. Every last one of them had changed into black, and they nodded without a word.
“Apparently they do.”
Gwak Jun smiled in satisfaction, then turned to me.
“Well, shall we set out too?”
What the fuck is this bastard talking about right now?

paragraphs: The first thing I felt was confusion.
“Set out?”
Gwak Jun answered.
“Yes. Our side needs to get moving too, or we won’t make it in time.”
At those cryptic words, Hyuk Mujin stepped forward.
“You there, from the Samdo Sect. You seem to have the wrong idea. Our mission is to wait here in the rear with the Young Master.”
“Oh, is that so?”
Gwak Jun’s eyes went round. At his reaction, the reconnaissance-squad members nodded with looks that said, That figures.
“Looks like I had it wrong.”
“It happens. Sure it does.”
But I thought otherwise.
What do you mean, it happens?
There were twenty Samdo Sect martial artists left in the rear. Gwak Jun was their leader.
Would a guy like that mix up his orders?
He was unpleasant, no question, but he didn’t look that stupid.
Dread crept over me.
“That’s a problem. The mission I received is a little different.”
“How is it different?”
As I spoke, I pressed down firmly on Hyuk Mujin’s foot. He horsed around dozens of times a day, but he wasn’t an idiot. His eyes widened as he caught my signal.
“Captain, please move your foot. It hurts.”
For fuck’s sake.
Gwak Jun’s mouth curled as he watched me stare in disbelief.
“You catch on fast. Or are your subordinates just idiots? Well, anyway. I’ll tell you exactly what that person said.”
The smile vanished from Gwak Jun’s face. With the cold, emotionless gaze of a killer, he continued.
“Eliminate everyone and join the main force.”
Clang-clang-clang!

The instant the words left his mouth, dozens of sword flashes shot into the air. Killing intent and tension hung between the twenty martial artists Gwak Jun led and the reconnaissance-squad members, who drew their swords half a beat later.
“Have you bastards lost your minds...?”
Hyuk Mujin ground his teeth and glared at them.
“You dare betray our family? Are you that desperate to die?”
“Betray? Die? You’re badly mistaken.”
A sneer tugged at Gwak Jun’s mouth.
“We never betrayed anyone, and we aren’t going to die. Least of all to trash like you.”
“You son of a—!”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes went wild as he threw himself at Gwak Jun.
Or tried to.
“Stay put.”
“Captain?”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes flew wide.
“They’re the Samdo Sect! They’re nothing but Second Rate sect husks! Let us smash them right now and—”
“No.”
“What?”
“They’re not dregs.”
Their sharp aura and murderous eyes were nothing like those of the ordinary martial artists I’d seen from small and mid-sized sects. The System turned my suspicion into certainty.
System Lv.30
That was their average Level according to Qi Sense.
Every last one of them was a First Rate martial artist. Damn it. I’d spent three days with these people and hadn’t noticed a thing.
I’d been too fixated on Logout.
That was what I got for letting my guard down. I bit my lip and looked at them—or, more precisely, at the thick grass behind them.
The movement had been extremely faint, but it couldn’t escape my eyes.
Someone’s hiding there.
They were outside the range of Qi Sense, so I couldn’t confirm it, but my instincts told me I was right. Spies, and an ambush on top of that. Thorough bastards.
“You lot. Who are you really?”
“What is that supposed to mean?”
“Where is the real Samdo Sect?”
The Samdo Sect was only a small or mid-sized sect. As Hyuk Mujin had said, they were Second Rate husks. People like these couldn’t have been whipped up overnight.
Don’t tell me.
“Did you come from the Mount Heng Sword Sect?”
Gwak Jun let out a short laugh.
“The Mount Heng Sword Sect? Well, I suppose you could think that.”
Damn it. A third faction.
Logout was right in front of me, and this had to happen now...
Shit. Just my fucking luck.
I was scared shitless. The more I shrank back, the more triumphant Gwak Jun became.
“It’s too late for regrets. The grand plan was set in motion long ago.”
“Urgh.”
Gwak Jun declared in a voice brimming with delight,
“Today... Shanxi Murim will welcome a new master.”
Ding.

System — A Quest has been created. Quest Slay the Assassins Someone who has long awaited the right moment has made their move. First, defeat the assassins sent by the traitor! Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Objective: Slay the Assassins (0/20) Reward: EXP and Fame Chain Quest Failure: Death
I blinked. Had I misread the Quest Window?
Twenty?
Why twenty? There were enemies lying in ambush back there too.
Just as the question occurred to me, the grass shook. The ambushers charged toward us with a battle cry.
“Kweeeek!”
That was a strange battle cry. No, wait. Wasn’t that an animal?
As I stood there blankly, an alert rang in my ears to announce that Qi Sense had activated.
System Lv.1 Water Deer
What the hell?
“Water deer?”
A herd of water deer brushed past us and vanished beyond the hill. A sudden appearance. A quick exit.
Gwak Jun drew his sword with an oddly deflated look on his face.
“Attack!”
The twenty enemies approached slowly. Still reeling from the water deer, I called to Hyuk Mujin.
“Hey.”
“What?”
“They’re all First Rate, you know?”
“What? Really?”
Hyuk Mujin jumped.
“Yeah. You know Lee Seogeun, the second son of the Mount Heng Sword Sect? Imagine twenty of him.”
“Twenty Lee Seogeuns?”
His reaction was strange. Hyuk Mujin thought it over for a moment, then tossed out a single remark.
“They’re all going to die, aren’t they?”
Gwak Jun thought,
This isn’t how it was supposed to go.
His gaze was locked on one man. Jin Taekyung, the Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, known as a Supreme First Rate martial artist.
Every time his spear moved, blood spurted and Gwak Jun’s men fell.
Even if they weathered one blow, the second or third always finished them. Every one of them was a First Rate martial artist trained for at least ten years.
What the hell is he?

He was clearly a spearman, but he didn’t care whether the gap closed or not. Whenever it looked like there wasn’t even room to swing the spear, daggers and axes popped out from somewhere and stabbed and jabbed at anything in reach.
It put an acrobat troupe’s tricks to shame.
Where the hell are all those weapons coming from?
He hadn’t even seen them appear. He had no idea what kind of technique it was. This wasn’t a matter of martial arts or internal energy.
Jin Taekyung himself was simply strong.
The information was wrong.

Twenty men weren’t nearly enough. They should have brought twice that number. According to the information Gwak Jun had received, Jin Taekyung was nothing more and nothing less than a lucky greenhorn.
And what the hell are those men?

The nine said to be Jin Taekyung’s subordinates advanced slowly with their backs to one another, paying no attention to what their leader was doing up ahead. Individually, their skills were sorely lacking, but together, they formed an iron wall.
Thud. Crack!
“Gaaah!”
“Stab them! Stab them!”
“Come in! Come in!”
Gwak Jun’s lips trembled.

They had no honor as martial artists. In the middle of this melee they piled on three or four at a time and hacked away, and even his First Rate subordinates couldn’t avoid ending up as meat on a skewer.
“You bastards...!”
Anger drove out his fear of Jin Taekyung. Just as Gwak Jun, beside himself with fury, was about to hurl himself into the fight—
Whoooosh—
A violent gale erupted at the center of the battlefield.

Jin Taekyung’s spear tore through the wind and shattered the swords. Hundreds of sword fragments rode the gale and swept forward, tearing into the owners of those swords and anyone else who failed to react in time.
Pupupupupup!
Thud.
A martial artist with sword fragments buried all over his body pitched forward. Of the ten or so men caught in One Annihilation, he was the only one who managed even that much of a sound.
Someone swallowed hard, their throat bobbing.
For that moment, friend and foe alike fell silent. No one dared even think of raising a sword to fight.
One person was the exception, of course.
“One Annihilation. This thing is awesome.”
The instant Gwak Jun heard that mutter, he gave up on everything.
It’s all over.
Even if the grand plan succeeded, he had failed. All that remained was the meaningless choice between dying to Jin Taekyung and dying to that person.
I have to run. Far away, somewhere no one can find me.
But Gwak Jun never got the chance to leave in search of a second life. Just as he turned, a savage voice stopped him.
“Stay right there if you don’t want to die very painfully.”
Jin Taekyung added in a slightly gentler voice,
“If you answer well, I’ll kill you gently.”
Gwak Jun’s face went white.
Crunch!
“Ghk.”
I felt it.
Two or three ribs had probably broken, and the wind had been knocked clean out of him.
He held up pretty well for a Level 40, but that was his limit.
“I told you not to run.”
“If I were him, I would’ve run too.”
Covered in blood and dust, Hyuk Mujin stared at me like I was some kind of beast.
“If you’re going to tell him you’ll kill him gently, you might as well say you’ll coat your spearhead with Golden Sore Medicine before you stab him.”
“Want me to stab you?”
“Now that I think about it, you’re right. A blade hurts less if it hits you gently, doesn’t it? So I suppose you can die gently. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”
I smacked him once on the back of the head, then hauled Gwak Jun to his feet.
“Let’s try this again. Who are you?”
Ptooey.
I easily dodged the bloody phlegm. With a high Agility stat, you could even avoid spit flying at you from point-blank range.
That was a useful life hack.
Of course, I had a useful life hack for Gwak Jun too. For example:
“If you get hit in the solar plexus while your ribs are broken, it hurts a lot.”
Thump.
“Gaaaaah!”
“So? Your answer?”
“S-Samdo Sect.”
When I raised my fist again, Gwak Jun shouted,
“The Samdo Sect! We really are the Samdo Sect! I’m telling you the truth!”
Hyuk Mujin frowned.
“He’s lying. The Samdo Sect was founded thirty years ago. In truth, it’s closer to a martial arts school than a sect. They’re highly respected for taking in wandering orphans and teaching them.”
“So?”
“Couldn’t these bastards have killed all the Samdo Sect’s disciples and taken their places?”
“Taken their places? Pfft.”
A deflating sound escaped Gwak Jun’s mouth. He was laughing.
“You still don’t understand? The Samdo Sect was founded according to that person’s will. As if any of you could have guessed at a grand plan thirty years in the making. Heh heh.”
“Thirty years?”
It was an unimaginably long time. Only a handful of people could have lain low for that many years while plotting to seize Shanxi Province.
Only one person came to mind.
The Head Elder?
Why would he do such a thing?

The Head Elder was the one who had pulled Jin Wikyung to his feet while he blamed himself before the children’s bodies. He was also the one who had halted every political maneuver and actively cooperated.
Thanks to him, the Jin Family of Taiyuan had united and made it this far...
Wait.
My head spun.
Could it be?
“Hyuk Mujin. How many martial artists are there from the small and mid-sized sects that recently joined us?”
“If you add the Samdo Sect and the Gunggui Sect together, well over a hundred.”
“And under the Head Elder?”
“If you mean the Head Elder’s faction, probably close to half the main force... Ah!”
Hyuk Mujin and the reconnaissance-squad members gaped as they grasped the situation.
If my guess was right and the Head Elder was a traitor, everything fit.
Helping Jin Wikyung had been nothing more than preparation for today.
So he could take everything in a single battle.
He had helped Jin Wikyung and united the family’s strength for this very day.
Suddenly, I remembered what Gwak Jun had said before the fight.
That one line about Shanxi Province getting a new master. It no longer sounded like nonsense.
The main force is in danger.
I had to tell Jin Wikyung.
“We’re moving out. Right now!”
I shouted and was about to turn.
“Already too late.”
Gwak Jun grinned, baring his bloodstained teeth.
“Too late for me, too late for you bastards, and too late for the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect. The grand plan has already begun.”
At the same time, blood gushed out. From his eyes, nose, and mouth—from every opening.
Gwak Jun’s head slowly drooped.
Hyuk Mujin spoke with a sickened look on his face.
“He severed his own heart meridian.”
Gwak Jun’s death meant one thing.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System — Defeated Lv.40 Gwak Jun! — Slay the Assassins (20/20) — Quest Slay the Assassins complete! — Level up! — Fame increases by 50!
Quest complete, a level-up, and a Fame increase.
After all those notifications, a single message appeared.
System — All conditions for Logout have been met. — Logging out in 3 seconds. 3, 2...
Strength drained from my whole body. It felt as if I were floating.
Hyuk Mujin caught me, his face filled with alarm.
“Captain!”
His voice crackled with static. My vision blurred, and my body slipped beyond my control.
Not now. Not like this...
Of all times.
And then—
System — 1.
Darkness crashed in.
