Reasons I didn’t particularly want to discuss.
Im Kkeokjeong spoke in a concerned voice.
“You’re in a noncombat position today, so you should be fine... but be careful.”
“I will.”
His words left me with a strange feeling.
They reminded me of someone who, until recently, had constantly been telling me to be careful.
But the sentimentality didn’t last.
“Is everyone ready?”
Team Leader Choi appeared, and my jaw dropped.
No way.
“Is that a Red Drake leather set?”
“Hmm.”
Team Leader Choi’s face stiffened.
I’d only ever seen gear like that in luxury catalogs, and the words had slipped out before I could stop them.
“Ah, sorry...”
“It’s nothing special.
It was merely crafted using five types of magic and B-grade Magic Gems.”
“Not that I’m emphasizing the point, but its materials include five types of magic and B-grade Magic Gems.”
“Ah.
Right.”
“Red Drake leather is popular for its distinctive sheen, but it only looks impressive.
It isn’t particularly useful.”
Team Leader Choi moved, his face still stiff.
A faint red glow flashed across him.
“But it is exceptionally beautiful.”
“Let’s head downstairs.”
Team Leader Choi left the waiting room first.
Im Kkeokjeong sidled over to me.
“That guy loves it when someone recognizes his equipment.”
“I mean, I get that, but... what’s with him?”
“No idea.
He’s an equipment nut.
There’s even a rumor that he blew his entire fortune on that set and sleeps in it every night.”
So that bastard’s a nutjob too.
I sighed inwardly and prayed that today’s raid would end without incident.
“This isn’t the same number of people you registered.”
The civil servant looked uncomfortable.
Fair enough.
We were supposed to enter soon, and the party still wasn’t all there.
How much longer are we supposed to wait?
Only six people had gathered in front of the Gate.
Excluding me, the porter, that left just five combatants.
Since this was an E-rank Gate, we needed at least five more Hunters of the same rank... but those Peace Guild bastards were nowhere in sight.
No wonder the official was annoyed.
“You should’ve notified us in advance if you were adding personnel.”
Huh?
What did he just say?
Adding personnel?
“I’m sorry.”
At Team Leader Choi’s curt apology, the official picked up his pen and drew several lines through the paperwork.
“It’s not a major problem since we can amend it... but please be more careful next time.”
“Yes.”
Not a major problem, my ass.
There aren’t any people!
I poked Im Kkeokjeong in the ribs.
“Hyung.
When are the others getting here?”
“What others?”
“The Peace Guild members.”
“Team Leader Choi’s right there.”
“What?”
“Oh, did I forget to tell you?
The Peace Guild is new, so it doesn’t have many people.
There are only three of us, including the Guild Master.
Hahaha!”
...You’re laughing?
“Come on, hyung.”
“I know, punk.
But you don’t need to worry.”
Im Kkeokjeong patted my shoulder and pointed at Team Leader Choi, who was signing the paperwork.
“That man’s a C-rank Hunter.”
“Oh.
C-rank...”
I shut my mouth.
If Team Leader Choi was a C-rank Hunter, there was no problem.
No, he was far better than ten E-rank Hunters.
He was a mid-rank Hunter, in a completely different league from a low-rank Hunter like me.
I should’ve realized the moment I saw him wearing that luxury gear.
The man was walking around with a high-end apartment wrapped around his body.
Most low-rank Hunters couldn’t afford armor like that even if they cleaned out their entire fortunes ten times over.
A faint halo seemed to shine around Team Leader Choi’s back.
“Please verify the signature.”
Even the way he handed the pen back to the official looked elegant.
Every little movement seemed to ooze wealth.
So this is the dignity of a C-rank Hunter.
That’s fucking cool.
I wanted to become sworn brothers with him.
To pledge brotherhood beneath the Gate—a gay oath, no, a Gate oath.
“All right, then.
Let’s go in...
What is it?”
Team Leader Choi looked at me, startled.
“No.
I just thought you looked cool.”
“Excuse me?”
“Your equipment.
I said it looks cool.”
At that moment, the corner of Team Leader Choi’s mouth twitched.
“It’s nothing special.
It was merely crafted using five types of magic and B-grade Magic Gems...”
A nutjob I wanted to befriend.
I stepped toward the Gate.
Whoosh—
A familiar sensation enveloped me.
The cool, viscous energy unique to magical power.
Then the scenery changed.
“It’s a cave.”
Just as Team Leader Choi said, the raid site was a cave.
The moisture-laden walls were damp, and a faint darkness shrouded our surroundings.
“Mr.
Taekyung.
Take out a flashlight.”
“Yes.”
I quickly set down my backpack.
It was a porter’s bag Team Leader Choi had handed me just before we entered the Gate.
It looked ordinary on the outside, but it was an expensive item enchanted with both space expansion and weight-reduction magic.
“Here’s the flashlight.”
I handed it over as requested, though in my experience, flashlights weren’t the best option.
They were convenient, but if the light suddenly went out, your eyes wouldn’t be adjusted to the darkness.
It was much better to wait a little and let your eyes get used to the darkness...
Click.
“Let there be light.
Light.”
Whoosh.
A ball of light the size of a soccer ball shot from the flashlight and plastered itself against the cave ceiling.
“...Magic?”
“It has a built-in spell that activates as soon as the incantation is spoken.
It lasts quite a while, so it should be good for another three or four hours.
It’s a limited-edition item I purchased from Company M...”
Im Kkeokjeong summed it up.
“It’s crazy expensive.”
Was it my imagination, or had Team Leader Choi’s face darkened slightly?
Maybe it was just the shadows.
Either way, the raid had become much easier thanks to him.
Money really is the best.
Capital ruled the world, and Gates were no exception.
People with money fought in comfort using enchanted equipment.
People without it carried torches.
“Take your positions.”
At Team Leader Choi’s command, everyone moved at once.
Im Kkeokjeong and another E-rank Hunter took the lead as tanks, with Team Leader Choi behind them.
I, the porter, and the two ranged dealers stood at the very back.
“Move.”
We began advancing slowly.
The bright magical light illuminated the path ahead.
I want one.
“Kiiiieet!”
The creatures crouching in the darkness emerged with shrill cries.
Green skin, squat bodies, and grotesque limbs.
They were Hobgoblins, an evolved form of ordinary goblin.
About thirty of them.
With only five combatants, this would be a difficult fight.
But having a C-rank Hunter changes everything.
On top of that, the other four were veteran E-rank Hunters with at least ten-odd years of experience each.
I hung well back and watched the battle.
“Ranged!”
Arrows flew the instant Team Leader Choi gave the order.
One shot, one kill.
The arrows buried themselves in vital points, dropping the unshielded Hobgoblins one after another.
“Kiit!”
“Oh, look.
Shield-bearers.
What do we do?”
“Hold.”
Team Leader Choi issued his next command.
“Tanks, advance.”
The tanks moved forward in thick full-body armor, tower shields raised.
Im Kkeokjeong and the other man were both hulking giants over 190 centimeters tall.
The sight of them alone was intimidating.
“Kiiiieet!”
But monsters were monsters for a reason.
Trusting in their numbers, the Hobgoblins charged like a swarm of bees.
But—
“Well, look at you.”
Bam!
The big, beautiful tower shields sent them flying back as bloody pulp.
Seizing the momentum, Im Kkeokjeong swung his mace like a flyswatter, shattering limbs and crushing skulls with every blow.
“You punk!
You punk!”
...What was this, whack-a-mole?
Veterans, all right.
All four of them stayed within their roles without overextending themselves, steadily whittling down the enemy numbers.
Knowing when to fall back and when to push in was combat intelligence born of plenty of experience.
“Everyone, hold your positions.”
And then one man.
The man who had been directing the flow of battle until now moved.
“I’ll take care of the rest.”
A red streak flashed across his armor as he plunged into the twenty remaining Hobgoblins.
Slash—
A head soared into the air along a clean arc.
It happened so quickly that the monsters couldn’t even react.
“Kiiie?”
Slash.
Slash.
Slash.
The blade never stopped.
Merciless and efficient, it pierced and severed one vital point after another.
This was no longer a battle.
It was a massacre—one man slaughtering more than twenty monsters.
So this is a C-rank Hunter.
His speed.
His strength.
I could see it all.
And I could feel it.
He really is strong.
As a mere F-rank, I couldn’t even dream of matching him.
He was a mid-rank Hunter, three full ranks above me.
A broad river and a towering wall that effort alone could never overcome.
Yet at the same time, a question arose.
What if this were Murim?
Team Leader Choi was unquestionably strong.
He had the abilities befitting a C-rank Hunter and plenty of experience.
But if this were Murim... if he were a martial artist...
I’d be stronger.
His movements were fast and powerful, but that was all.
He hadn’t learned martial arts, nor did he use his mana efficiently.
At best, he was First Rate.
In Murim, that was exactly where he would stand.
But this is reality.
I bit my lip without realizing it.
A mid-rank Hunter and a bottom-rank Hunter.
While the mid-rank Hunter wore expensive equipment and slaughtered monsters, the lowest-rank Hunter could only stare blankly.
As a porter.
“Kiiieet...”
The last Hobgoblin fell.
Team Leader Choi pulled his sword from its chest, and our eyes met.
“Mr.
Taekyung.
Please handle the byproducts.”
“Mr.
Taekyung?”
I wanted to tell him that I was stronger than him.
But in the end, I couldn’t.
Because this was my reality.
“...Thank you for your hard work.”
I used to be stronger than you.

chapters.title: Chapter 43
paragraphs: Slice.
A razor-sharp dagger sank into a Hobgoblin corpse.
Fluids splattered and a foul stench filled the air, but I didn’t stop. I discarded the heads, neatly cut the hides from their backs and bellies, and stacked them in a pile.
“You’re quite skilled.”
“...Thank you.”
It was Team Leader Choi. The kindness in his voice made me feel guilty. How childish was I, getting jealous of someone like him?
Especially when I’d dragged up an illusion I’d already decided to forget.
What am I, going through puberty?
I finished the job with my face burning red.
A little over ten minutes, so about twenty seconds per corpse? Even Im Kkeokjeong sidled over, drawn by the speed, and his mouth fell open.
“Damn, have you been doing nothing but this?”
“Plenty of people can do this much.”
“Plenty, my ass. You’re a total professional.”
Hmm. That made me a little proud.
I’d played modest a second ago, but Im Kkeokjeong was right. There weren’t many Hunters who could butcher this cleanly at this speed.
“I’m just fast with my hands.”
I’d worked factory jobs back in school. I’d even glued eyes onto dolls. In a way, I’d started doing this kind of work before I ever became a Hunter.
“I kept it up during raids, too.”
“You switched over to doing this full-time?”
“No. I did both. It was a side job.”
“A side job?”
Team Leader Choi, who’d been listening quietly, cut in.
“Uh, yes.”
“What exactly did you do?”
“I’d use the breaks after each fight to process the corpses.”
“Do you receive additional pay?”
“Of course. It’s still work.”
“How long have you been doing it?”
“The whole time. From the beginning until now.”
Im Kkeokjeong was floored.
“You relentless bastard. I couldn’t do it.”
“You get used to it. It helps build stamina, too.”
“Your life’s on the line, and you’re building stamina? Hahaha. Team Leader Choi, didn’t I tell you? There’s nobody who works as relentlessly as this kid.”
You told him that?
“Hmm.”
Instead of answering, Team Leader Choi studied me for a moment, then turned away.
“Now that the work is done, shall we get moving again?”
What was that reaction supposed to mean? As I stood there bewildered, Im Kkeokjeong gave me an unreadable smile.
“Keep working hard.”
No, seriously. What’s going on?
The raid went smoothly. The E-rank Hunters had fought together for so long that they moved as one. Once they thinned out the monsters, Team Leader Choi took over.
Slash—
Every swing of his sword sent up a fountain of blood.
I watched every second of the battle unfolding before me.
He really can fight.
Of course, I couldn’t help thinking about Murim.
I’d seen real martial arts with my own eyes—and even learned them. Not the dance-like moves I practiced in the city park at dawn.
...Wait.
No way. But what if?
It was ridiculous. There was no way it would work, but I could at least try.
It won’t work. It won’t... but it would be nice if it did.
Just as I was about to cautiously take a step—
“Mr. Taekyung. Please handle the cleanup.”
Team Leader Choi’s voice snapped me back to my senses.
I’ve completely lost it.
I’d let myself get distracted in the middle of a raid.
Get a grip.
Whatever I wanted to try later, the raid came first for now.
That was the least courtesy I owed my teammates—and the principle that would keep me alive.
“Yes. Coming!”
I ran over like the wind and started taking the corpses apart.
Team Leader Choi and Im Kkeokjeong hovered nearby throughout the entire break, as if they weren’t tired at all.
This is seriously getting on my nerves.
Im Kkeokjeong came over again at the next break, right on cue.
“Taekyung. How long have you been using a spear?”
“Seven years.”
“Wow. That practically makes you a master. A real master.”
He came back during the break after that, too.
“Taekyung. You said you graduated top of your training class, right?”
“Yes. But I was only first among the F-ranks, so it doesn’t mean much.”
“You punk. That’s still impressive. I graduated dead last.”
“You’re impressive too, hyung. But I need to get back to work.”
“Oh, right.”
Then he came back during the next break, and the next, and the one after that.
“Taekyung. Taekyung. Taekyung.”
“Hyung, I think my cochlea just ruptured.”
“How many years did you say you worked at your old Guild?”
“Ah.”
I wanted to switch classes and become a mage right then and there, just so I could cast a silence spell on the man’s mouth.
This is driving me crazy.
There was only one way out: finish the work before blood actually started pouring from my ears. I clenched my teeth and kept my hands moving.
Slice. Slice. Slice.
“Taekyung.”
Save me.
I sent a distress signal to Team Leader Choi, who was sitting nearby, but he answered by quietly slipping away.
“The work’s done.”
I stood and shouldered the bag, now noticeably heavier than before. Hobgoblins were generous monsters. Poison-resistant hides, a few usable weapons—and they had even dropped two E-grade Magic Gems.
The hides are in good condition, and there are two Magic Gems. This could be worth a decent amount.
Team Leader Choi had contributed the most, so he’d probably take about half. But with so few people, it was still a profitable deal for the other team members.
Not me, of course. According to the contract, the 300,000-won base pay was all I would get.
If he’s in a good mood, maybe he’ll throw in a little extra.

Team Leader Choi was a fairly generous employer. He was a C-rank Hunter far beyond my level, yet he always spoke to me politely. His personality was a little unusual, but by the standards of this industry, he was practically a saint.
And he’s skilled enough to trust.
Thanks to him, we’d made it this far at a steady, rapid pace.
Only the final section of the Gate remained.
The Boss Zone.
If we opened the stone gate in front of us, the Gate’s boss monster and the mana field that would send us outside should be waiting beyond it.
“Man, all that work made me hungry.”
“Let’s finish this quick and go get some gukbap. Taekyung, you’re coming too, right? You too, Team Leader Choi.”
“No, thank you. I’ll order sushi separately.”
Talking about food with the Boss Zone right in front of us. And then there was the guy planning to order sushi by himself.
Should we really be this relaxed?
Of course, I had no room to talk. I’d already earned a full day’s pay just by carrying luggage and butchering monsters between fights.
Until I found a job with a new Guild, I couldn’t ask for anything more than Team Leader Choi calling me regularly. A sweet gig like this? I’d do it a hundred times over.
“Well, shall we head in?”
“Yes.”
At Team Leader Choi’s answer, Im Kkeokjeong slammed his tower shield into the stone gate.
Boom!
The gate blew apart, and stone dust and dirt poured down. I followed the others into the Boss Zone.
And there...
—Keuruk.
It stood.
A shaman?
That was the first word that came to mind.
An old Hobgoblin wearing a robe covered in strange patterns. It held a withered staff in one hand and a sharp dagger in the other.
—Karruk. Chwi. Akto.
Despite the deafening crash of the doors breaking apart, it continued muttering without so much as a glance our way. With each syllable, black energy rose from the corpses scattered around it.
Wait. Corpses?
I hadn’t imagined it. Nearly a hundred dead Hobgoblins lay sprawled across the altar. Looking closer, they were the monsters we should have been fighting in the Boss Zone.
What the hell is going on?
Everyone, myself included, froze at the unfamiliar sight.
Team Leader Choi’s voice cracked like thunder.
“Get outside! Now!”
At that moment, the unknown old Hobgoblin turned its head.
Clink.
Its staff shook lightly.
—Mita. Allo.
The air shuddered.
Magic was taking form.
“Behind the shields!”
The tanks hurriedly raised their tower shields.
But that was the wrong call.
It hadn’t cast an attack spell.
Boom. Boom. Boom!
“It’s behind us! The passage is being blocked!”
“Run! Hurry!”
Damn it. Too late.
As if the clock had been turned back, the shattered stone gate stood intact again.
And it didn’t stop there.
The rubble on the floor rose into two, then three layers of walls, and vines from the cave walls wrapped around them, binding them tight.
“Everyone, out of the way!”
It was Im Kkeokjeong. His muscles had swollen like they were about to burst—probably a Strength Enhancement Skill. Tower shield in hand, he charged the stone gate.
“Haaah!”
Bang! Crack!
“...Goddamn it.”

Im Kkeokjeong dropped his heavily cracked tower shield, his face blank with disbelief. An E-rank Hunter had used a Skill and still failed to break through. All he had managed to do was wreck his shield.
Enhancement magic?
Whatever it was, one thing was certain.
An old Hobgoblin capable of magic this powerful had to be at least one or two tiers above the monsters we had faced so far.
And...
Whoosh!
There was someone among us who could fight it.
When did he—?
Team Leader Choi was already rushing toward the creature, as if he’d known from the start that we wouldn’t be able to reopen the passage.
“The wind takes hold. Haste.”
His body slid forward. More than a hundred meters vanished in an instant. With five paces left, the sword came free from Team Leader Choi’s waist.
Whoosh!
A full-power attack from a C-rank Hunter.
But the old Hobgoblin merely gave him a sinister grin.
—Karruk. Chwi. Akto.
The change happened in an instant.
Whoosh—
The hundred-odd corpses scattered across the altar shriveled, then dispersed like sand. The black energy, fully pulled out of them, gathered into one mass and smashed into Team Leader Choi’s side.
Thud!
“Ghk.”
Team Leader Choi bounced back fast. With a twisted face, he said,
“We have to stop it. Right now.”
“...That thing?”
It was already too late.
Only a few seconds ago, it had been nothing more than energy given form. Now it was rapidly taking shape.
A hulking body nearly three meters tall. Muscles swollen to the point of bursting. A monster wielding an enormous greatsword.
“What the hell is that...?”
Someone muttered in a daze. Like me, they had clearly never seen anything like it.
Only Team Leader Choi knew what the creatures were.
“A Hobgoblin Great Warrior. A C-rank Rare Monster.”
The fact that something so huge was a Hobgoblin was shocking enough, but it was nothing compared to what came next.
A C-rank Rare Monster?
Fuck, why is that thing showing up here?

Rare Monsters were creatures that appeared only infrequently within a given Gate. And since that Great Warrior was C-rank, it was something neither I nor the other team members should ever have encountered in our lives.
...Of course, not anymore.
“You want us to fight that thing?”
“Those things.”
Team Leader Choi pointed at the old Hobgoblin.
“A Hobgoblin Priest. Also a C-rank Rare Monster.”
“Ah, fuck...”
The curse slipped out before I could stop it. Im Kkeokjeong asked, his face rigid,
“What are our chances? Give it to me straight.”
“If we take out the Priest first, we have a chance. But to do that...”
Boom. Boom.
Team Leader Choi trailed off.
The Great Warrior was coming toward us.
One step. Then another.
The cave floor shook.
“We need to hold that thing back for a little while.”
Who?
“Us?”
“No. All of you.”
“Kuwooooh!”
The Great Warrior’s roar sent a stalactite dropping from the cave ceiling.
Team Leader Choi turned with a resolute look I’d never seen on him before.
“The wind takes hold. Haste.”
Hey, you bastard.

I’d do it a hundred times over.
“Well, shall we head in?”
“Yes.”
At Team Leader Choi’s answer, Im Kkeokjeong slammed his tower shield into the stone gate.
Boom!
The gate blew apart, and stone dust and dirt poured down.
I followed the others into the Boss Zone.
And there...
—Keuruk.
It stood.
A shaman?
That was the first word that came to mind.
An old Hobgoblin wearing a robe covered in strange patterns.
It held a withered staff in one hand and a sharp dagger in the other.
—Karruk.
Chwi.
Akto.
Despite the deafening crash of the doors breaking apart, it continued muttering without so much as a glance our way.
With each syllable, black energy rose from the corpses scattered around it.
Wait.
Corpses?
I hadn’t imagined it.
Nearly a hundred dead Hobgoblins lay sprawled across the altar.
Looking closer, they were the monsters we should have been fighting in the Boss Zone.
What the hell is going on?
Everyone, myself included, froze at the unfamiliar sight.
Team Leader Choi’s voice cracked like thunder.
“Get outside!
Now!”
At that moment, the unknown old Hobgoblin turned its head.
Clink.
Its staff shook lightly.
—Mita.
Allo.
The air shuddered.
Magic was taking form.
“Behind the shields!”
The tanks hurriedly raised their tower shields.
But that was the wrong call.
It hadn’t cast an attack spell.
Boom.
Boom.
Boom!
“It’s behind us!
The passage is being blocked!”
“Run!
Hurry!”
Damn it.
Too late.
As if the clock had been turned back, the shattered stone gate stood intact again.
And it didn’t stop there.
The rubble on the floor rose into two, then three layers of walls, and vines from the cave walls wrapped around them, binding them tight.
“Everyone, out of the way!”
It was Im Kkeokjeong.
His muscles had swollen like they were about to burst—probably a Strength Enhancement Skill.
Tower shield in hand, he charged the stone gate.
“Haaah!”
Bang!
Crack!
“...Goddamn it.”
Im Kkeokjeong dropped his heavily cracked tower shield, his face blank with disbelief.
An E-rank Hunter had used a Skill and still failed to break through.
All he had managed to do was wreck his shield.
Enhancement magic?
Whatever it was, one thing was certain.
An old Hobgoblin capable of magic this powerful had to be at least one or two tiers above the monsters we had faced so far.
And...
Whoosh!
There was someone among us who could fight it.
When did he—?
Team Leader Choi was already rushing toward the creature, as if he’d known from the start that we wouldn’t be able to reopen the passage.
“The wind takes hold.
Haste.”
His body slid forward.
More than a hundred meters vanished in an instant.
With five paces left, the sword came free from Team Leader Choi’s waist.
Whoosh!
A full-power attack from a C-rank Hunter.
But the old Hobgoblin merely gave him a sinister grin.
—Karruk.
Chwi.
Akto.
The change happened in an instant.
Whoosh—
The hundred-odd corpses scattered across the altar shriveled, then dispersed like sand.
The black energy, fully pulled out of them, gathered into one mass and smashed into Team Leader Choi’s side.
Thud!
“Ghk.”
Team Leader Choi bounced back fast.
With a twisted face, he said,
“We have to stop it.
Right now.”
“...That thing?”
It was already too late.
Only a few seconds ago, it had been nothing more than energy given form.
Now it was rapidly taking shape.
A hulking body nearly three meters tall.
Muscles swollen to the point of bursting.
A monster wielding an enormous greatsword.
“What the hell is that...?”
Someone muttered in a daze.
Like me, they had clearly never seen anything like it.
Only Team Leader Choi knew what the creatures were.
“A Hobgoblin Great Warrior.
A C-rank Rare Monster.”
The fact that something so huge was a Hobgoblin was shocking enough, but it was nothing compared to what came next.
A C-rank Rare Monster?
Fuck, why is that thing showing up here?
Rare Monsters were creatures that appeared only infrequently within a given Gate.
And since that Great Warrior was C-rank, it was something neither I nor the other team members should ever have encountered in our lives.
...Of course, not anymore.
“You want us to fight that thing?”
“Those things.”
Team Leader Choi pointed at the old Hobgoblin.
“A Hobgoblin Priest.
Also a C-rank Rare Monster.”
“Ah, fuck...”
The curse slipped out before I could stop it.
Im Kkeokjeong asked, his face rigid,
“What are our chances?
Give it to me straight.”
“If we take out the Priest first, we have a chance.
But to do that...”
Boom.
Boom.
Team Leader Choi trailed off.
The Great Warrior was coming toward us.
One step.
Then another.
The cave floor shook.
“We need to hold that thing back for a little while.”
Who?
“Us?”
“No.
All of you.”
“Kuwooooh!”
The Great Warrior’s roar sent a stalactite dropping from the cave ceiling.
Team Leader Choi turned with a resolute look I’d never seen on him before.
“The wind takes hold.
Haste.”
Hey, you bastard.

chapters.title: Chapter 44
paragraphs: “Just hold out for five minutes.”
With that, Team Leader Choi shot off like the wind. For better or worse, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior didn’t give him so much as a glance.
“He’s coming this way.”
At my words, everyone nodded blankly.
“He is.”
Boom, boom, boom!
“He’s running this way.”
“Defensive formation—!”
The team snapped into formation. I gripped my spear and moved as ordered. Between the tanks and the ranged dealers. Dead center—that was my spot.
No, for fuck’s sake. I’m a porter...
Even if my life was going to go sideways, did it have to go this sideways?

They say an unlucky bastard can fall over backward and still break his nose. For 300,000 won, I’d run into two mid-grade Rare Monsters. This wasn’t just a broken nose. This was a broken nose and a cracked skull.
—Kuwaaaaah!
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior charged with a roar. Nearly three meters of muscle and green hide—overwhelming all by itself.
Why is that greatsword so damn huge?
The thought of that thing swinging at me made me swallow hard.
“Can we stop it?”
“We’ll have to try.”
Im Kkeokjeong planted his tower shield in the ground and shouted.
“Archers! Don’t hold back on mana! Pour it on!”
Swish, swish, swish!
Mana-charged arrows shot straight at the Great Warrior. They had enough force to punch through most shields, but...
Thunk, thunk.
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior gave its greatsword a casual swing and chopped every one of them in half. Even if they’d hit, I doubted they could have pierced that thick hide.
“Aim for the vitals! Keep shooting and slow it down!”
Then the Great Warrior’s eyes burned red. Once it drew up its magical power, its strength and speed were on a whole different level.
“Kuwooooooh!”
With a booming roar, the green giant leaped into the air.
Im Kkeokjeong screamed.
“Scatter!”
Before anyone had time to think, we threw ourselves aside.
Boom!
The greatsword smashed the ground to pieces. A blast of air sent dust whipping around us like a tornado.
“Ghh.”
“Cough, cough.”
Groans and coughing broke out beyond the curtain of dust. I crouched as low as I could and thought,
What kind of monster is that?
It couldn’t compare to that guy from two years ago, but a chill still ran down my spine. In a fight like this, an F-rank Hunter like me was nothing but baggage.
I have to get as far away as I can while I have the chance.
Everything was lost in the haze. Nobody could tell friend from foe. This was my opening.
I stayed low and moved slowly, spear in one hand while the other felt through empty air.
Then—
Tap.
My fingertips hit something solid. Very hard, and wet.
It had to be the cave wall.
Already?
I’d thought I was farther away, but I must have been closer than I expected.
Fine by me. If I followed the wall, I could—
Squish.
What was this now? I carefully probed the unpleasantly squishy thing.
There’s fur, too. A person?
Maybe it was the head of someone who’d passed out. I held my breath and whispered,
“Kkeokjeong hyung?”
No answer.
“Who is it?”
This time, I got a reply.
Right above me.
“Grrr.”
A gust of wind swept through from somewhere and cleared the dust. I slowly looked up and saw a pair of gleaming red eyes.
“Grrk.”
I looked back down. Between thighs as thick as pillars and hard as stone, my dainty little hand was clamped around something.
I groaned under my breath.
“Ah, fuck...”
It was male instinct. Unbearable nausea. Disgust at myself. The next moment, my fingers loosened of their own accord.
Slide.
My limp hand slid down as the greatsword rose with force.
“Grrk.”
“I let go! I let go, so why are you doing this?!”
“Kuwooooooh!”
Goddammit.
I wrung out every last bit of strength I had and ran.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior had completely lost it. It chased me like a lunatic, hacking in every direction with its greatsword.
Whoosh—
“Aaaaah!”
That one was actually close. I ducked at the last second, and the greatsword skimmed over my head and wrecked the cave wall.
“Taekyung!”
“Shoot!”
The team poured on arrows and throwing weapons, but...
“Kuwaaaaargh!”
It wasn’t enough to pull the Great Warrior’s attention. Its eyes had already rolled back.
I rolled, then rolled again, and cursed my luck.
I should’ve just popped it.
Instinct had beaten reason. A man’s need to get his hand off that even one second sooner.
Whoosh!
The greatsword barely missed. It had been one close call after another, yet I still hadn’t let the C-rank Rare Monster land a single clean hit.
Maybe it’s because I’ve seen so much hell in Murim.
It sounded insane, but it was true. I could see its attacks. Moving half a beat ahead was what kept me alive.
Boom!
Of course, one hit from that thing and I’d be a goner.
“Taekyung, this way!”
I turned toward the voice. The team was waiting there in a defensive formation again.
“Fall back!”
Im Kkeokjeong charged the Great Warrior chasing me. Blue mana sheathed the tower shield, packed with enough force to smash most low-grade monsters to pieces.
“Hah!”
With a short shout, Im Kkeokjeong brushed past me. And then—
Crunch. Thud.
Something broke, and he shot backward at a vicious speed.
He flew a good ten meters, slammed into the wall, and vomited a gush of blood.
“Gweeehk.”
Was this for real?
I was stunned. The rest of the team, on the other hand, looked grimly determined.
“No! Kkeokjeong hyung!”
“We’ll buy time! Take hyung and get out!”
Then the greatsword sent another tank flying, tower shield and all.
Boom!
“Agh!”
“Jongmin!”
“We’ll buy time! Take Jongmin and hyung and get out!”
Thud!
“Aaargh!”
“Seokho!”
Smack!
That was the sound of the team being wiped out. The last member had charged in with a dagger, taken a knuckle to the skull, and gone flying. He twitched, then passed out.
At least they were all still breathing. Small mercies.
—Grrr...
Scratch that.
I kept my eyes on the monster and shouted,
“Team Leader!”
A fierce battle was still raging at the altar in the distance.
A tired voice came through the explosions.
“What?!”
“Are you still not done? It feels like it’s been more than five minutes!”
Boom! Boom! Fwoosh!
Lightning struck, and flames surged. Team Leader Choi screamed,
“Three more minutes!”
Anyone who didn’t know better might have taken him for a soccer referee. His bold call for extra time left me speechless.
—Karruk, karruk.
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior came toward me slowly. A cruel smile hung on its wide-split mouth. I eased back in time with its steps.
“That’s right. Come on. Come on.”
No choice. Same as before: run like hell and stall.
—Grrk.
But the Great Warrior didn’t play along.
“Huh?”
Its bulging eyes rolled toward the teammates sprawled unconscious on the ground. I had a very bad feeling about this.
“Don’t tell me...”
That was exactly it.
My heart dropped as I watched its back heading for Im Kkeokjeong.
“Hey! Hey, you!”
It ignored me completely.
Now I was the one in a panic.
If I leave it like this, they’re all dead.
I had to get its attention somehow. I grabbed one of the rocks scattered around me and threw it at the monster’s head.
Thwack!
Direct hit.
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior turned and glared at me.
“Yeah. Come here.”
—Grrr.
Its narrowed eyes flicked between me and Im Kkeokjeong. Then it started running at Im Kkeokjeong.
Boom, boom, boom!
“You crazy bastard!”
At this rate, Im Kkeokjeong and the rest of the team would all be wiped out. I was the only one who could stop it.
Stop that thing? Me?
A one-on-one fight against a C-rank Rare Monster.
A fight I could never win. But...
Ah, fuck.
I was already charging at it. Sometimes you had to fight even when you had no chance.
This was one of those times.
“You son of a bitch!”
Whoosh—!
The instant I thrust my spear at its broad back—
—Kururuk.
The green giant turned like it had been waiting for me. A smug smile curled its lips. The greatsword swept horizontally, shooting toward my side like a streak of light.
That’s what you were after.
My mind went white. Could I even block that? Had I made the wrong call out of some pathetic sense of guilt and heroism?
But the die was already cast.
I have to hold.
There are times you have to fight with your life on the line. This was one of them.
Please!
I clenched my teeth and wrenched the iron spear around to intercept it. At the same time, the greatsword smashed into the shaft.
Rrrrk—
A roar of impact. Then enormous pressure. The greatsword cleaved straight through the iron spear and my waist—
The iron spear was fine. So was my waist. All that had happened was my feet had been pushed back a little.
A very, very little.
What was this?
—G-Grrk?
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior’s face flushed bright red. It pulled the greatsword back and hammered the iron spear again. Even through the confusion, I tightened my grip and blocked.
Boom!
My body slid back.
Maybe thirty centimeters?
—...Grrk.
The Hobgoblin Great Warrior’s eyes met mine in the air between us. I’d been through this somewhere before.
That’s right. The duel with Lee Seogeun. It was exactly like this.
I’d freaked out at his Level and thought I was dead, only to find out he was a total pushover. How was I supposed to forget a moment that absurd?
But I had the System backing me there.
This was reality. I was an F-rank Hunter with nothing. No System, not a damn thing.
How is this even...
Ding.
“Huh?”
I froze. For that instant, I couldn’t see or hear a thing.
This can’t be. This is actually insane.
Ding.
System Synchronization complete. All systems are inherited.
And yet, it actually happened.
“Ha... hahaha.”
A laugh slipped out of me like I’d lost my mind. The Hobgoblin Great Warrior stared at me like I was the crazy one.
System Lv. 45 Hobgoblin Great Warrior
Right. So that was how it was.
“I don’t know what the hell just happened...”
I grinned at the monster.
“But you’re fucking dead.”
Gurgle.

A wrinkled hand clutched at a throat. But the old goblin had neither the strength to stop the blood pouring out like a waterfall nor the time to spit out the spell still sitting on the tip of its tongue.
“What a nuisance.”
With that from Team Leader Choi, the light went out of the Hobgoblin Priest’s eyes.
I’m tired.
But he turned around at once. He still had work to do. Who knew how brutal a fight it would take to bring down another C-rank Rare Monster—
Slash—
“Kwaaaaargh!”
Team Leader Choi thought he was seeing things. That same Hobgoblin Great Warrior was screaming. With one arm severed, it staggered backward.
Who did that?
He watched the fight, forgetting that he was supposed to help. Ghostlike movement. A spearhead flowing like water as it carved the green giant to pieces.
Wait. A spear?
Of everyone here today, only one person used a spear.
The porter—no, Jin Taekyung?
That was him.
The F-rank Hunter who’d been hauling a backpack and skinning hides!
“What on earth...”
Team Leader Choi’s mouth slowly fell open.
“What’s going on?”

A spearhead flowing like water as it carved the green giant to pieces.
Wait.
A spear?
Of everyone here today, only one person used a spear.
The porter—no, Jin Taekyung?
That was him.
The F-rank Hunter who’d been hauling a backpack and skinning hides!
“What on earth...”
Team Leader Choi’s mouth slowly fell open.
“What’s going on?”

chapters.title: Chapter 45
paragraphs: Slash.
The red eyes blinked, almost docile. So even a C-rank Rare Monster—the terrifying Hobgoblin Great Warrior—could make a face like that.
Why hadn’t I noticed before?
With that passing thought, I shook the blood from my spearhead. At the same moment—
Thud.
Something heavy hit the ground. The Great Warrior saw what it was and instinctively shuffled backward.
Well, fair enough. Its right arm had been severed cleanly below the elbow.
I thought you’d be a little different.
The Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique. Yeah, I’d used it to slip inside the creature’s reach. The Great Warrior reflexively swung its right arm, but there was nothing left to swing.
“Forgot already?”
I pressed the spearhead against the Great Warrior’s side and ripped it upward. The blade, charged with internal energy, split its tough hide and muscle.
Slash—
Its left arm fell away in a spray of green blood.
Both arms gone in an instant, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior let out a roar of rage and pain.
—Kuwaaaaaargh!
But I couldn’t let my guard down. Even without arms, it was still more than dangerous enough with its body alone.
“Yeah. Come at me.”
Before I’d even finished speaking, its massive frame charged.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
As expected, this thing’s entire body was a weapon. Like the monster it was, it possessed primal senses and strength that far surpassed a human’s.
Swish. Slash.
A hooked claw grazed my forearm. A chunk of flesh tore away, and blood poured out. Without flinching, I blocked the heel descending toward the crown of my head.
Thud. Crunch.
The ground beneath my feet began to sink.
Incredible strength. At this rate, I might be buried standing up.
If I didn’t have internal energy, that is.
I drew up every last bit of internal energy in my dantian. Power flooded through every limb. As my spear shaft slowly rose, the Great Warrior’s eyes wavered.
Too late.
It might have been different if the creature had been whole, but after losing both arms, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior was no longer a match for me.
—Grrr.
In the end, it was the first to back off. By then, the fight was as good as over.
I pressed forward and thrust my spear.
Jin Family’s Spear Technique. First form.
The movements engraved into my body and mind unfolded in rapid succession.
Thrust. Cut. Block and strike with the shaft. Simple on their own, but the order and the angles made countless combinations.
That was my definition of martial arts.
Clang! Clang!
Swish. Swish-swish-swish!
Second form. Third form. Fourth...
The hooked claws, once as hard as steel, were sliced away. With every step the creature retreated, another wound opened and more blood spilled.
Before long, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior’s back struck the wall.
“Grrrk...”
A C-rank Rare Monster. A creature that had once seemed impossible to fight. But the will to resist had long since vanished from its red eyes.
“Time to go.”
Shunk.
Ghk. With a final death rattle, the hulking green body slid down the wall.
And then—
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv. 45 Hobgoblin Great Warrior! Level Up!
The System notification rang out. I’d thought I would never hear or see one again...
The System, out of nowhere?
But I wasn’t the only one confused.
“...Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
Team Leader Choi had already dealt with the Priest. His pupils shook as if an earthquake had struck while he looked back and forth between me and the Great Warrior’s corpse.
“What... are you?”
Good question. I wanted to know too.
Heh heh. Heh heh heh.
“A Rare Monster?”
The cigarette dropped from the government official’s mouth.
He looked like a born civil servant, so this couldn’t have been welcome news. Sure enough, his gaze darted anxiously over us.
“W-what rank?”
Team Leader Choi wearily shook the Priest’s staff.
Clank.
“C-rank Rare. Hobgoblin Priest.”
“C-rank?! For fuck’s—”
Hey, save the swearing. There’s one more.
I kicked the Hobgoblin Great Warrior’s greatsword, which I’d been using as a walking stick. The official turned at the dull clang.
“And that?”
“Buy one, get one more. C-rank Rare. Hobgoblin Great Warrior.”
“Two mid-grade Rare Monsters? In an E-rank Gate?”
I got the reaction. This had to at least make some kind of sense.
The official spent a while looking back and forth between us and the equipment before finally nodding with a miserable expression.
“I’ll contact my superiors first.”
“Hey, mister. Hold on.”
Im Kkeokjeong had regained consciousness at some point. I was supporting him, and he’d suffered severe injuries, including at least five broken bones.
“Call a healer. A pretty unnie.”
The E-rank trio dropped onto the ground as well.
“And potions! Potions! Give us the good stuff!”
“For fuck’s sake, how did you people even manage this Gate?!”
“All our gear’s smashed too! Huh? What are you going to do about this?!”
What did they think he was going to do? The government would compensate them for everything.
There was an actual law requiring it to cover every item consumed inside the Gate, along with medical expenses and compensation.
In other words, this was all a show to squeeze out a little more.
Tsk, tsk. Even so, people are watching.
That was when I felt a piercing stare from beside me.
“...Mr. Taekyung.”
It was Team Leader Choi.
“What are you doing?”
He stared at me in confusion. More precisely, at the hand holding my dagger.
Grrrk.
The dagger, charged with internal energy, carved long gashes through my seven-year-old leather armor until it was too badly damaged to use.
“Team Leader Choi.”
I heaved a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.
“That Hobgoblin Great Warrior was incredibly strong. I escaped with my life, but every piece of equipment I owned was destroyed.”
“The armor that protected me for seven years. Now even my spear...”
“The spear looks perfectly—”
At that moment, I planted one foot on the middle of the spear and slowly pressed down.
Before the majesty of my three-digit Strength stat, the iron spear bent like taffy.
“Looks perfectly fine? This?”
Team Leader Choi shut his mouth.
Team Leader Choi was called away by the officials dispatched to take charge, and the other four were moved to an ambulance for treatment.
Instead of the musty break room, I was left alone in a spacious, comfortable office. Now that the moment had finally arrived, my heart began to pound.
St-Status Window?
At that half-doubtful call, the System answered.
Ding.

System Status Window Lv. 33 Jin Taekyung Job: First Rate Martial Artist Fame: 0 Titles: 2 (Title effects active) - Novice Trainee (Training speed +10%) - Gambler (Combat-related stats +10% in one-on-one matches) Strength: 120 Stamina: 125 Agility: 121 Intelligence: 20 Charm: 20 Internal Energy: 15 years Remaining Points: 30 Synchronization is complete. Titles and Fame have changed.
“Fuck. It really appeared.”
I stared blankly at the Status Window for a moment before noticing something strange.
The Status Window... changed?
Two things jumped out first: my Fame had been reset to zero, and a Title was missing. The final line gave me a rough idea why.
Because this isn’t Murim?
All five hundred Fame I’d accumulated had been earned as a martial artist in Murim. The missing Title, Scion of a Prestigious Family, made sense for the same reason.
Well, I’m not the son of some prestigious family here. And I’m sure as hell no Hidden Dragon.
If I earned a Title here, it would probably be something like Scion of the Common Folk. Or Earthworm instead of Hidden Dragon.
“How much else changed?”
For about ten minutes I turned every System function on and off and tested them. The only thing that had changed was the Status Window.
No. There was one more.
The Quest Window.
Ding.

System Quest Traitor You have discovered the traitor’s identity. Rejoin the main force, warn them of the traitor, and lead the battle to victory! Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Eliminate the traitor (Incomplete) Win the battle (Incomplete) Reward: Vast EXP and Fame Valuable iron chest Failure: Death
It was the Chain Quest I’d received after defeating Gwak Jun and the assassins. My thoughts grew tangled.
Does it want me to go back? To Murim?
I knew now. The Murim I’d experienced wasn’t an illusion or a game. As wildly unrealistic as it sounded, Murim was probably...
Creak.
I turned at the sudden sound. Team Leader Choi stood in the doorway.
“Let’s go, Mr. Taekyung.”
It seemed the discussion had wrapped up. I put the thought aside and rose.
“The others...?”
“They should be on their way to the hospital by now. They’ll need to stay there for about a week. You don’t need to worry.”
I wasn’t particularly worried. Combat-type Hunters had sturdy bodies, and they’d received potions and healing magic. They would be back on their feet soon enough.
And...
“How did it go?”
“They’ll contact us again within a few days. An investigator will probably visit you as well.”
An investigator.
Not the sort of person I ever wanted to deal with again. But that wasn’t the answer I wanted, so I asked once more.
“What about the other matter?”
“Hmm.”
Team Leader Choi regarded me with a strange expression, like he was examining some fascinating animal.
Did he tell them the truth?
I didn’t want my strength exposed. Especially not now, when I still had no idea why the System had appeared in reality or how any of this was connected to Murim.

An F-rank Hunter single-handedly killing a C-rank Rare Monster was unprecedented. A needle in a bag would eventually poke through, but I’d spent my whole life being the opposite of that—never standing out at all. I couldn’t help being cautious.
So I had asked him:
“Could you keep what concerns me a secret?”
It must have been a difficult request from Team Leader Choi’s perspective. I was asking him to give a false statement for someone he’d only just met.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Yes.”
His grave voice made my heart sink.
Then he said, “Let’s get something to eat.”
“What?”
“Look.”
Team Leader Choi held out his wrist. A gleaming Magic Gem digital watch showed two in the afternoon.
“It’s an N Company model carved from a solid C-rank Magic Gem. It’s enchanted with reinforcement magic, so in an emergency, you can even use it as a shield—”
So that’s what he meant.
“...Let’s go.”
The man was impossible to read.
“Let’s get some meat. Do you like Hanwoo?”
“Hanwoo?”
“Yes. Highest grade.”
And he was rich too.
“I never get to eat it.”
This wasn’t just any beef. It was Hanwoo. Top-grade Hanwoo, at that.
System or whatever—first, I needed to fill my empty stomach.

chapters.title: Chapter 46
paragraphs: Sizzle.
The meat hit the grill. Thick, red, and marbled with white streaks like snowflakes—it was the finest Hanwoo beef.
The shape, the sound, the smell. All of it was intoxicating. The only thing I didn’t like was the price...
“Will this be enough? Let’s order more after we eat. Some special cuts, too.”
A rich C-rank Hunter was paying, so whatever.
How long had it been since I’d last had Hanwoo?
Food in Murim was spicy, salty, and bland. And even then, more days than not, I couldn’t eat properly. For thirty days, my stomach had been abused with beef jerky, fasting pills, and rice balls.
Chomp. Chomp-chomp.
The best thing about beef was how quickly you could eat it. As soon as it looked more or less done, it went straight into my mouth.
Every chew felt like walking on clouds. This piece, that piece, that one too—every last one tasted like heaven.
“Hnnngh.”
Team Leader Choi watched me with that peculiar look of his.
“Would you like some more?”
“No. I should hold back on overeating.”
“We’re on our twenty-fifth serving...”
“Twelve servings each isn’t all that much.”
“I’ve only eaten three.”
“Oh, can we order some yukhoe?”
“Rice, too.”
And so the storm of a meal finally came to an end. At last, Team Leader Choi spoke.
“I told them I killed both the Priest and the Great Warrior.”
“Oh. Thank you.”
“Don’t mention it. Let’s call it a fair deal. If anything, I have something to thank you for as well.”
A fair deal.
He wasn’t wrong. I’d bought myself time to think, and he would gain a reputation. After all, he had led five low-rank Hunters and killed two mid-grade Rare Monsters.
The fact that no one had died in the process would be a huge boost to the Guild’s publicity, too.
What if Synchronization hadn’t restored my strength?
Who knew? Someone probably would have died. Maybe none of us would have made it out alive.
“You were already thinking along those lines.”
He wasn’t just some eccentric. Not with instincts that sharp.
I smiled awkwardly.
“It works out well for both of us.”
“Good for both of us. Both of us...”
Team Leader Choi muttered to himself, then abruptly asked,
“Would you like to join the Guild?”
“Pffft!”
Team Leader Choi lifted the tablecloth and blocked the water, then smoothly produced a business card with practiced elegance.
Peace Guild, Team 1 Leader Choi Minwoo
What the hell was this? For a second I was completely thrown.
“Y-you’re making me a recruitment offer? Right now?”
“That’s right. We’re always looking for talent.”
I took the card and found myself strangely moved.
It seemed like only yesterday that I’d been bowing like a shrimp at job interviews...
Live long enough and you really do see everything.
An actual recruitment offer—and he was even treating me like talent. F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung, you’d come a long way.
“Our Guild is still new, and we don’t have many members, but we’re excellent where it counts. For example...”
Team Leader Choi elegantly swirled his wineglass. When had he even ordered that?
“Our finances are extremely solid.”
“Ooh, finances!”
“Which means our employee benefits are excellent.”
“Ooh, benefits backed by solid finances!”
“Our Guild Master is a B-rank Hunter.”
“Ooh, a high-ranking Hunter—the source of those solid finances!”
“And there’s no need to worry about restructuring.”
“Ooh, job security!”
Team Leader Choi asked with an affluent smile,
“Will you join us?”
I scratched my head.
“No. That’s a little...”
“...Pardon?”
“I have circumstances that make it difficult at the moment. I need some time.”
If I followed my heart, I’d sign the contract right away—signature, seal, thumbprint, even a kiss mark.
But what if the System disappears tomorrow?
I’d be dead broke.
Overnight, I’d go from being called talent to being called a human disaster.
“Is it a money problem?”
Money was always a problem.
But this was more important. I couldn’t let the wad of cash dangling in front of me blind me into making a snap decision.
“It’s difficult to explain. I’m sorry, but this isn’t something I can decide right now...”
“One hundred million won.”
“A hundred million?”
“Just the signing bonus. The rest will match the minimum terms for a C-rank Hunter.”
That was dangerous. This time, it was really dangerous.
But I resisted with superhuman patience. Hadn’t I learned long ago that life was never that easy?
That money might come back to choke me.
“I’m sorry.”
Team Leader Choi looked at me quietly, then nodded.
“I’ll wait to hear from you.”
One person left, and one remained.
Team Leader Choi—no, Choi Minwoo—silently stared at the seat Jin Taekyung had vacated, then took out his phone.
Beep. Beep. Click.
“—You bastard, are you psychic? I was just about to call you.”
“How did that thing I asked about turn out?”
“—I looked into it because you asked, but... is there something about this Jin Taekyung guy?”
“That’s what I called you to find out. So? What did you learn?”
“—It’s a dime-a-dozen case. Awakened at twenty, seven years ago, and assessed as F-rank. There’s a record of him graduating at the top of his class from the Hunter training center...”
Jin Taekyung’s past seven years spilled from the other end of the phone. Then, at one point, Choi Minwoo’s eyebrows twitched.
“What? The Sangdong Station Mutated Gate?”
“—Yeah. You know about that incident, right?”
How could he not? It had happened only two years ago, so Choi Minwoo remembered it clearly.
“—He was the only survivor. I checked that part myself, and it surprised me, too.”
Choi Minwoo tipped his glass of water. Thinking he’d grabbed a lead on how an F-rank Hunter had killed a mid-grade Rare Monster alone made his throat burn.
“And?”
“—He took six months off. The Hunter Administration kept sending investigators, and I guess he spent the time trying to pull himself together. You know how serious the incident was.”
“And then?”
“—That’s it. He went back to his Guild, ran Gates his ass off for a year and a half, then got fired. That was exactly three days ago.”
“Why was he fired?”

“—Technically, restructuring, but what kind of restructuring does a tiny little Guild like that need? The incident probably had a lot to do with it. They kept looking over their shoulders at the Administration, then finally pushed him out. He must’ve been uncomfortable for them to keep around.”
“That’s all?”
“—As far as I can tell. Want me to send you the file separately?”
“Send it now. I’m hanging up.”
“—Hey, hey!”
Click.
Choi Minwoo tapped his long fingers against the table.
Jin Taekyung. F-rank Hunter. The sole survivor of the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate.
And...
At least a C-rank Hunter.
That was the absolute minimum. The image of Taekyung driving a C-rank Rare Monster into a corner alone, with overwhelming strength and skill, kept flickering before his eyes.
And yet he’s F-rank.
There were only two possibilities. Either he had been hiding his strength, or he had recently reawakened.
Choi Minwoo suspected the latter, but even that defied common sense.
Countless Hunters retired without ever rising a single rank.
A reawakening that took someone from F-rank to C-rank was, without question, extraordinarily rare.
This isn’t some game. What the hell is he?
Choi Minwoo shook his head. He felt as if he’d been bewitched by a ghost.
I’ll have to look into him some more.
As he rose from his seat, the restaurant owner approached and held out the bill.
“That will be 1,937,000 won.”
Now he really felt as if he’d been bewitched by a ghost.
“Fuck. I’m screwed.”
I dropped to the ground in the filthy recycling area. The one thing that should have been there was nowhere in sight.
“It’s gone. It’s gone. My capsule is gone.”
I’d been anxious ever since parting ways with Team Leader Choi. But I hadn’t expected someone to take it in less than half a day. I shouted into the empty air.
“Who the fuck took it?!”
And an answer came back.
“Me, you son of a bitch.”
Jinho was smoking on the roof of the goshiwon building, in the same spot where I’d seen him that morning. He exhaled a wistful stream of smoke and continued.
“I spent ten years crying, regretting it, and making vows...”
“You want me to make you cry and regret it for real?”
“You’re no fun. You haven’t seen this movie, have you?”
“Quit joking around. This is serious.”
“What, did you come up empty today?”
“No.”
My voice drained of strength as I went on.
“The capsule.”
“Some bastard took my capsule.”
“Cough! Cough-cough!”
Maybe he’d inhaled the cigarette smoke wrong. Jinho hyung coughed like a maniac before he finally managed to speak.
“D-didn’t you throw it away because you didn’t need it?”
“I did.”
Until the System came back.
I hadn’t expected the situation to change this much in just a few hours.
I should’ve kept it for one more day.
Where was I even supposed to start looking? I let out a deep sigh.
“Hyung, you didn’t happen to see who took it, did you?”
“Uh... well.”
Jinho scratched his head.
“If I saw it, then I saw it. If I didn’t, then I didn’t.”
Was that supposed to be an answer, or was it just crap?

“Look, it’s not like I’m hoping for a finder’s fee or anything...”
It definitely sounded like he wanted a finder’s fee.
Anyway, that wasn’t the point. I shot to my feet and asked,
“You saw them? You’re sure?”
“If I had to choose, I’d say I did.”
“Who? Where did they go?”
“I’m not asking for a finder’s fee, but roughly how much were you thinking?”
“...One hundred thousand won?”
“Oh, dear. Maybe I’m getting old. My memory’s a little hazy.”
“For fuck’s sake.”
“Right, then. Good luck in this heat.”
“The finder’s fee is one hundred and eighty thousand won.”
Apparently satisfied with the amount, Jinho beamed.
“Your capsule. I picked it up.”
It took me exactly three seconds to understand.
What a goddamn daylight robber.
I was speechless. He’d really stabbed me in the back like this?
“But there wasn’t anywhere suitable to put it. My room’s too small, you know.”
“So?”
“I put it back in your room. I did good, right?”
How could I hit this man so thoroughly that word would spread about what a fine job I’d done?
My fists trembled.
“It really is here.”
The capsule occupied half the studio as if nothing had happened. All I could do was let out a hollow laugh.
Should I call this lucky?
Of all the people who could have taken it, it had been Jinho.
I opened the lid, picked up the user manual that had been tossed onto the worn seat, and flipped to the last page.
Main Features A customized capsule for one person! Once a user is registered, the capsule becomes permanently bound to that user and remains so until their death.
...Come on. No way.

What the hell is this thing?

The reason I’d thrown the capsule into the recycling area that morning was so I could forget everything. My life was already dry enough; I wanted to write it off as one nightmare and keep living my life as I was.
But things were different now.
Because I have the System.
The System...

“Item check.”
Ding.
Just as I thought. The corners of my mouth had just begun to rise when—
System This Item cannot be read.
“...It can’t be read?”
That had never happened before.
Is it because I’m not in Murim?
Flustered, I started checking random objects around the room. The television, a ballpoint pen, even my pillow. Every time, the System displayed accurate information.
There was only one exception.
It couldn’t read the capsule.
“Wow. This is driving me nuts.”
Just in case, I picked up the user manual. The result was the same.
Ding.
System This Item cannot be read.
I flopped onto the bed. I stared blankly at the old, yellow-stained ceiling and thought.
What’s going on?
None of this made sense yet. But one thing was certain.
I’ve become stronger. Incomparably stronger.
Power had soaked into every fiber of my body. Internal energy writhed in my dantian.
Synchronization had given me strength. Strength far beyond that of an F-rank Hunter. Strength enough to defeat a C-rank Rare Monster alone.
Would you like to join the Guild?
It was the first recruitment offer I’d ever received. But I refused. When someone recognized me, fear had come before joy.
Can’t blame me.
I’d endured seven years with the label of F-rank Hunter. I was a caterpillar that had spent its whole life crawling through the dirt, only to suddenly sprout wings called the System.
Of course I was afraid.
But what if I can keep using this power? What if I can keep using the System?
My heart pounded at the mere thought.

At the same time, the past seven years flashed through my mind. The name F-rank, stamped on me like a brand despite all the insane effort I’d put in. Even the memories from two years ago, when I’d trembled at other people’s contempt, at the guilt and the helplessness.
“Fuck...”
I couldn’t take it anymore. I shot to my feet, raced out of the goshiwon, and flagged down a passing taxi.
“Where would you like to go?”
I already knew my destination.
“Take me to the Bucheon Branch of the Hunter Association.”
A Hunter rank reassessment.
F-rank Hunter. I’d start by breaking the loathsome shackle that had tormented me for so long.
Let’s give it a shot.
As I clenched my fist, the taxi driver said,
“This is a Seoul taxi.”
“Oh.”

sentences.text: Sizzle.
The meat hit the grill.
Thick, red, and marbled with white streaks like snowflakes—it was the finest Hanwoo beef.
The shape, the sound, the smell.
All of it was intoxicating.
The only thing I didn’t like was the price...
“Will this be enough?
Let’s order more after we eat.
Some special cuts, too.”
A rich C-rank Hunter was paying, so whatever.
How long had it been since I’d last had Hanwoo?
Food in Murim was spicy, salty, and bland.
And even then, more days than not, I couldn’t eat properly.
For thirty days, my stomach had been abused with beef jerky, fasting pills, and rice balls.
Chomp.
Chomp-chomp.
The best thing about beef was how quickly you could eat it.
As soon as it looked more or less done, it went straight into my mouth.
Every chew felt like walking on clouds.
This piece, that piece, that one too—every last one tasted like heaven.
“Hnnngh.”
Team Leader Choi watched me with that peculiar look of his.
“Would you like some more?”
“No.
I should hold back on overeating.”
“We’re on our twenty-fifth serving...”
“Twelve servings each isn’t all that much.”
“I’ve only eaten three.”
“Oh, can we order some yukhoe?”
“Rice, too.”
And so the storm of a meal finally came to an end.
At last, Team Leader Choi spoke.
“I told them I killed both the Priest and the Great Warrior.”
“Oh.
Thank you.”
“Don’t mention it.
Let’s call it a fair deal.
If anything, I have something to thank you for as well.”
A fair deal.
He wasn’t wrong.
I’d bought myself time to think, and he would gain a reputation.
After all, he had led five low-rank Hunters and killed two mid-grade Rare Monsters.
The fact that no one had died in the process would be a huge boost to the Guild’s publicity, too.
What if Synchronization hadn’t restored my strength?
Who knew?
Someone probably would have died.
Maybe none of us would have made it out alive.
“You were already thinking along those lines.”
He wasn’t just some eccentric.
Not with instincts that sharp.
I smiled awkwardly.
“It works out well for both of us.”
“Good for both of us.
Both of us...”
Team Leader Choi muttered to himself, then abruptly asked,
“Would you like to join the Guild?”
“Pffft!”
Team Leader Choi lifted the tablecloth and blocked the water, then smoothly produced a business card with practiced elegance.
Peace Guild, Team 1 Leader Choi Minwoo
What the hell was this?
For a second I was completely thrown.
“Y-you’re making me a recruitment offer?
Right now?”
“That’s right.
We’re always looking for talent.”
I took the card and found myself strangely moved.
It seemed like only yesterday that I’d been bowing like a shrimp at job interviews...
Live long enough and you really do see everything.
An actual recruitment offer—and he was even treating me like talent.
F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung, you’d come a long way.
“Our Guild is still new, and we don’t have many members, but we’re excellent where it counts.
For example...”
Team Leader Choi elegantly swirled his wineglass.
When had he even ordered that?
“Our finances are extremely solid.”
“Ooh, finances!”
“Which means our employee benefits are excellent.”
“Ooh, benefits backed by solid finances!”
“Our Guild Master is a B-rank Hunter.”
“Ooh, a high-ranking Hunter—the source of those solid finances!”
“And there’s no need to worry about restructuring.”
“Ooh, job security!”
Team Leader Choi asked with an affluent smile,
“Will you join us?”
I scratched my head.
“No.
That’s a little...”
“...Pardon?”
“I have circumstances that make it difficult at the moment.
I need some time.”
If I followed my heart, I’d sign the contract right away—signature, seal, thumbprint, even a kiss mark.
But what if the System disappears tomorrow?
I’d be dead broke.
Overnight, I’d go from being called talent to being called a human disaster.
“Is it a money problem?”
Money was always a problem.
But this was more important.
I couldn’t let the wad of cash dangling in front of me blind me into making a snap decision.
“It’s difficult to explain.

“One hundred million won.”

“Just the signing bonus.

That was dangerous.
This time, it was really dangerous.
But I resisted with superhuman patience.
Hadn’t I learned long ago that life was never that easy?
That money might come back to choke me.
“I’m sorry.”
Team Leader Choi looked at me quietly, then nodded.
“I’ll wait to hear from you.”
One person left, and one remained.
Team Leader Choi—no, Choi Minwoo—silently stared at the seat Jin Taekyung had vacated, then took out his phone.
Beep.
Beep.
Click.
“—You bastard, are you psychic?
I was just about to call you.”
“How did that thing I asked about turn out?”
“—I looked into it because you asked, but... is there something about this Jin Taekyung guy?”
“That’s what I called you to find out.
So?
What did you learn?”
“—It’s a dime-a-dozen case.
Awakened at twenty, seven years ago, and assessed as F-rank.
There’s a record of him graduating at the top of his class from the Hunter training center...”
Jin Taekyung’s past seven years spilled from the other end of the phone.
Then, at one point, Choi Minwoo’s eyebrows twitched.
“What?
The Sangdong Station Mutated Gate?”
“—Yeah.
You know about that incident, right?”
How could he not?
It had happened only two years ago, so Choi Minwoo remembered it clearly.
“—He was the only survivor.
I checked that part myself, and it surprised me, too.”
Choi Minwoo tipped his glass of water.
Thinking he’d grabbed a lead on how an F-rank Hunter had killed a mid-grade Rare Monster alone made his throat burn.
“And?”

You know how serious the incident was.”
“And then?”

He went back to his Guild, ran Gates his ass off for a year and a half, then got fired.

The incident probably had a lot to do with it.
They kept looking over their shoulders at the Administration, then finally pushed him out.
He must’ve been uncomfortable for them to keep around.”
“That’s all?”

Click.

Jin Taekyung.
F-rank Hunter.
The sole survivor of the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate.

At least a C-rank Hunter.
