chapters.title: Chapter 47
paragraphs: The Hunter Association.
The name had first appeared some thirty years ago, when the Great Cataclysm ended.
The first-generation Hunters who survived that blood-soaked catastrophe raised their flag, and over the years, the Hunter Association grew into an organization of tremendous stature.
Gulp.

I swallowed as I stared up at the Association building towering before me. Its sheer size and height made it stand out even in this dense forest of skyscrapers. Though it was an ordinary weekday, countless people streamed in and out.
How many years has it been?
Every Awakened underwent rank measurement under the Association’s supervision.
I was no different. Thinking of twenty-year-old Jin Taekyung walking in here with his heart full of excitement almost made me laugh—like hell it did.
Now that I’m actually here, I’m incredibly nervous.
I entered the lobby on stiff legs. The place was the size of a playing field and packed with people. Following the electronic signs posted throughout the lobby, I found the place I wanted.
Measurement Waiting Room
On the clerk’s instructions, I filled out the paperwork and went inside. Dozens of people were waiting to be measured.
Thud.
The door shut, and everyone’s eyes shot into me like arrows.
I can’t breathe. This is suffocating.
Even the air was different here. A taut tension pressed down on the entire waiting room.
One measurement decides your whole Hunter life.
I was no exception. I’d once been so nervous that I farted in front of an examiner. That pretty much said it all.
I was waiting my turn, lost in thought, when—
“Jin Taekyung?”
A familiar voice came from behind me. I slowly turned my head.
There he was.
“I thought it might be you. Sure enough.”
A potbellied, middle-aged man with a bulbous nose. A face I couldn’t forget no matter how hard I tried.
...Team Leader Kim?
Kim Sangshik. A founding member and team leader of Sopung Guild, where I’d spent years. He could be summed up in one word.
Former boss.
“Wow, I never expected to run into you here. Good to see you.”
Team Leader Kim thrust out his hand with a hearty laugh. I hesitated for a moment, then shook it.
“Likewise. It’s been a while.”
“What do you mean, a while? It’s only been a few days.”
“Those few days felt pretty long to me.”
I’d said it thinking of Murim, but Team Leader Kim would take it another way. After all, he was the one who’d handed me my dismissal only a few days ago.
“It’s because it’s summer. My days have felt long lately too.”
“Really?”
Watching him slip past the remark like a sly old fox, I let out a dry laugh.
He was always an amusing man.
In more ways than one.
“So what brings you here?”
“I had some business. What about you, Team Leader?”
“Came to scout. Heard there was a decent one this time.”
They’d fired me for staff cuts in a restructuring. And he was here to scout.
“I see.”
That was all I had to say. It was the same tired story everyone knew, and it was already over. I had no lingering attachment to it.
“What about you? Why are you here? Don’t tell me you’re trying to get reassessed.”
“Yes.”
Team Leader Kim smiled.
“Nice try, but isn’t that a waste of money? A reassessment isn’t cheap. Must be a burden for an F-rank Hunter.”
“I thought I’d give it a try anyway. Just in case.”
“You should save your money while you’re young. What’s going to change if you keep clinging to something that’ll never work?”
“Who knows? I think this time might be different.”
“It’s not that easy—”
“Team Leader.”
“Huh? What?”
I smiled gently.
“That’s enough.”
Team Leader Kim’s smile cracked.
“What?”
“I said that’s enough. I’m out of the Guild now, so stay out of my business.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
What did it mean?
“You know exactly what I mean.”
“All that ‘It couldn’t be helped,’ ‘At least you survived,’ and ‘Forget about it and make a fresh start.’ You pretended to comfort me while chipping away at me behind my back.”
“Weren’t you the first one to tell the Guild Master to fire me? Did you think I wouldn’t find out?”
Kim Sangshik was a half-baked, petty little man.
Short on both humanity and ability.
Even inside Gates, he was always too busy saving his own skin. His reputation within the Guild was rock-bottom.
“Who did you put in my place after firing me? How much did they pay you to get them in?”
“Hey, Jin Taekyung.”

Team Leader Kim pressed down on my shoulder and growled. He might not look it, but he was one of only three D-rank Hunters in Sopung Guild. With that kind of strength, he could toy with an F-rank Hunter like me using one hand.
But—
“Take your hand off.”
I didn’t even blink. It wasn’t only the System that had synchronized. My martial arts, my stats, and even my steel-like Muscles and Bones had come with it.
“I’ll count to three. Take your hand off.”
“You little bastard. I’ve been putting up with you, but—”
I didn’t hesitate.
“One. Two.”
Three.
The instant I seized Kim Sangshik’s wrist—
Clack.
“Would the next group please come in? Numbers twenty-one through thirty!”
An Association examiner entered with a file in hand, and we sprang apart without waiting for the other to move first. Getting on the Association’s bad side wouldn’t do either of us any good.
“Consider yourself lucky.”
“Who? Me, or you?”
Kim Sangshik’s flushed face looked downright ridiculous.
So did the Level Window I picked up through Qi Sense.
System Lv. 24 Kim Sangshik
“Meeting you was disgusting. Let’s never see each other again.”
I rose without a shred of regret. My waiting number was thirty.
My steps toward the examiner were no longer stiff.
“Number twenty-one. Please come forward.”
A tense-looking Awakened stood before the measuring device. Made from an A-rank Magic Gem, it scanned his entire body and converted the mana inside him into numbers.
Bzzzzzt—
The examiner checked the reading.
“Amount of mana distributed throughout the body: F-rank.”
The Awakened’s face turned ashen. But it was too soon to despair. He still had a second chance.
“Try moving your mana. Concentrate as hard as you can and imagine firing it into the measuring device.”
They were testing his mana control. Realizing it wasn’t over yet, the Awakened gritted his teeth and strained with every ounce of strength he had—
Pfffft.
Looking ready to vomit, the examiner said, “Control ability: F-rank.”
“Please! Just let me try one more time!”
“No. Next.”
The line moved quickly.
Everyone was E-rank or F-rank. One guy wasn’t even Awakened.
“This is a scam! A scam! That measuring device is made in China, isn’t it? Huh? You bastards!”
“Handle him.”
At the examiner’s command, the security Hunters waiting nearby dragged the fraudster away. Even if that guy miraculously Awakened someday, he’d probably end up on the Association’s blacklist.
“Next. Number thirty.”
Here it came.
I took a deep breath and stepped forward. The examiner glanced at the file in his hand.
“This is a reassessment?”
“Yes.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, you were rated F-rank seven years ago... You’re aware that reassessments carry a separate fee, correct?”
From his tone, he might as well have been telling me not to waste my money and to go home while I still could.
The usual attitude toward an F-rank Hunter.
Do they think I’m a beggar?
I was used to it. That didn’t make it any less insulting. When I glared at him, the examiner gave a short laugh.
“I’m only mentioning it in case you weren’t aware, but the fee is two million won.”
“...The price went up?”
“It has been a few years.”
Fuck. I didn’t know that.
How much was in my account right now...?
“Then we’ll begin the measurement.”
Nervous, I closed my eyes.
And the next moment—
Bzzzzzt.
A wave of magical power rolled out of the measuring device and swept through my whole body.
My fifteen years of internal energy responded with a shudder.
What rank will I get?
C-rank? No, I’d be happy with D-rank. But more than ten seconds passed, and the examiner still said nothing.
“Uh... Why is it doing this?”
“What’s wrong?”
Flustered, he looked back and forth between the device and me, then cleared his throat.
“There seems to be some kind of error... We’ll move on to the next step for now.”
I had no idea what was happening, but strangely, it didn’t feel ominous.
I’ve got a good feeling about this.
My heart pounding, I drew up my internal energy.
Ssshhh.
At the call of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, fifteen years of internal energy surged up and shot toward the measuring device.
At the lobby entrance—
“Well done.”
Kim Sangshik patted a young man on the shoulder. As of today, the promising young man had officially been rated D-rank.
He would soon join Sopung Guild and be assigned to Kim Sangshik’s team. Thinking of the day to come, Kim Sangshik smiled proudly.
“Father and son on the same team. That’s my boy.”
“What are you talking about? I’m not even an official Hunter yet. I still have to go through the training center.”
“Don’t worry. Your father already took care of it.”
“Wait, really? Didn’t you say the Guild didn’t have any openings?”
“There’s always a way.”
He didn’t mention that he’d made room by firing the lowest-ranked Hunter, who had long been a thorn in his side.
“Anyway, get plenty of rest this week. Starting next week, we’ll go to work together—”
Kim Sangshik’s face suddenly twisted.
“What’s wrong?”
“...Nothing. Go wait in the car.”
Once his son had left, Kim Sangshik rolled up his shirtsleeve.
His wrist was already swollen blue-black. The sight made him grind his teeth.
“Jin Taekyung, you fucking bastard.”
He’d disliked that bastard from the start. An F-rank Hunter had no business being deputy team leader, and he’d hated the way Taekyung acted like a brother to the former team leader, who was now dead.
That bastard should’ve fucking died with him back then.
The unfortunate accident two years ago had been a stroke of extraordinary luck for Kim Sangshik.
After being sidelined over several sex scandals, he’d returned triumphantly as team leader. A few days ago, he’d even managed to get Jin Taekyung thrown out.
But did that bastard really reawaken?
Kim Sangshik stared down at his throbbing wrist.
It had lasted only an instant, but the strength he’d felt had been tremendous. Taekyung might have reawakened as an E-rank—or perhaps even a D-rank.
“No. Reawakening isn’t child’s play.”
Maybe he’d simply gotten weaker because he hadn’t exercised lately. Kim Sangshik was muttering to himself, his thoughts in turmoil, when—
“Breaking news from the measurement room.”
“Did someone promising show up?”
“They say a big fish surfaced. C-rank.”
“C-rank? That’s not bad, but is it really enough to call him a big fish?”
“His mana control is supposedly A-rank.”
“What? A-rank? Get your hooks into him, now!”
“Yes, this is Choi Minsu from Sangdong Guild. The reason I’m calling is...”
A stir spread among the scouts prowling the lobby entrance like hyenas.
Most had been sent by small and midsized Guilds, but the handful representing major Guilds were already moving quickly.
C-rank alone is impressive, and he’s gifted with mana control on top of it?
This was a jackpot.
Kim Sangshik’s mind snapped into focus. He cast every thought of Jin Taekyung aside and pulled out his phone.
“Hey, Team Leader Kim. Did that business go well?”
The deep voice on the other end belonged to Sopung Guild’s Guild Master.
Kim Sangshik spoke urgently.
“Guild Master, it’s chaos here. A C-rank just appeared, and they say his mana control is on the level of a high-ranking Hunter.”
“What? Where did a guy like that come from?”
“Exactly. The major Guilds always snatch them out from under us, but it looks like they were a step late this time.”
“Good. So that’s how it is...”
Huff. Huff.
Rough breathing came through the phone, as though the Guild Master were excited. Even the way he addressed Kim Sangshik changed.
“Sangshik. You hold on to that guy no matter what. Tell him we’ll meet any conditions he wants.”
“How high can we go?”
“Don’t worry about the money. Add plenty on top of whatever the others offer. The major Guilds will back off if they decide he isn’t profitable enough. It’s not like they’re desperate for him.”
“Yes, yes.”
“I’m on my way. Keep him there until I arrive. If you pull this off... you know what that means, right?”
After ending the call, Kim Sangshik clenched his fist.
We’ve got this!
He was an old hand at this business. Holding on to a newly Awakened rookie would be easy.
This was a world where money could put even ghosts to work.
Double whatever everyone else offers. I’ll offer him twice as much, no matter what.
The commotion grew louder. The elevator was descending from the third floor, where the measurement room was located.
“He’s coming!”
“Hey, stop shoving!”
Some twenty scouts crowded around the elevator doors like a swarm of ants. Kim Sangshik muscled his way to the front and readied his business card.
Ding.
At last, the elevator doors opened.
Kim Sangshik bowed low and launched into his prepared speech.
“Hello. I’m Team Leader Kim Sangshik of Sopung Guild. We are a prestigious Guild with a long tradition here in Bucheon—”
“That’s the first time I’ve ever heard anyone call Sopung a prestigious Guild.”
“...What?”
At the familiar voice, Kim Sangshik slowly raised his head.
Their eyes met.
At the same time, Kim Sangshik’s buttonhole-sized eyes went wide.
“Y-you...”
Jin Taekyung grinned.
“We meet again, Mr. Kim Sangshik.”

sentences.text: The Hunter Association.
The name had first appeared some thirty years ago, when the Great Cataclysm ended.
The first-generation Hunters who survived that blood-soaked catastrophe raised their flag, and over the years, the Hunter Association grew into an organization of tremendous stature.
Gulp.
I swallowed as I stared up at the Association building towering before me.
Its sheer size and height made it stand out even in this dense forest of skyscrapers.
Though it was an ordinary weekday, countless people streamed in and out.
How many years has it been?
Every Awakened underwent rank measurement under the Association’s supervision.
I was no different.
Thinking of twenty-year-old Jin Taekyung walking in here with his heart full of excitement almost made me laugh—like hell it did.
Now that I’m actually here, I’m incredibly nervous.
I entered the lobby on stiff legs.
The place was the size of a playing field and packed with people.
Following the electronic signs posted throughout the lobby, I found the place I wanted.
Measurement Waiting Room
On the clerk’s instructions, I filled out the paperwork and went inside.
Dozens of people were waiting to be measured.
Thud.
The door shut, and everyone’s eyes shot into me like arrows.
I can’t breathe.
This is suffocating.
Even the air was different here.
A taut tension pressed down on the entire waiting room.
One measurement decides your whole Hunter life.
I was no exception.
I’d once been so nervous that I farted in front of an examiner.
That pretty much said it all.
I was waiting my turn, lost in thought, when—
“Jin Taekyung?”
A familiar voice came from behind me.
I slowly turned my head.
There he was.
“I thought it might be you.
Sure enough.”
A potbellied, middle-aged man with a bulbous nose.
A face I couldn’t forget no matter how hard I tried.
...Team Leader Kim?
Kim Sangshik.
A founding member and team leader of Sopung Guild, where I’d spent years.
He could be summed up in one word.
Former boss.
“Wow, I never expected to run into you here.
Good to see you.”
Team Leader Kim thrust out his hand with a hearty laugh.
I hesitated for a moment, then shook it.
“Likewise.
It’s been a while.”
“What do you mean, a while?
It’s only been a few days.”
“Those few days felt pretty long to me.”
I’d said it thinking of Murim, but Team Leader Kim would take it another way.
After all, he was the one who’d handed me my dismissal only a few days ago.
“It’s because it’s summer.
My days have felt long lately too.”
“Really?”
Watching him slip past the remark like a sly old fox, I let out a dry laugh.
He was always an amusing man.
In more ways than one.
“So what brings you here?”
“I had some business.
What about you, Team Leader?”
“Came to scout.
Heard there was a decent one this time.”
They’d fired me for staff cuts in a restructuring.
And he was here to scout.
“I see.”
That was all I had to say.
It was the same tired story everyone knew, and it was already over.
I had no lingering attachment to it.
“What about you?
Why are you here?
Don’t tell me you’re trying to get reassessed.”
“Yes.”
Team Leader Kim smiled.
“Nice try, but isn’t that a waste of money?
A reassessment isn’t cheap.
Must be a burden for an F-rank Hunter.”
“I thought I’d give it a try anyway.
Just in case.”
“You should save your money while you’re young.
What’s going to change if you keep clinging to something that’ll never work?”
“Who knows?
I think this time might be different.”
“It’s not that easy—”
“Team Leader.”
“Huh?
What?”
I smiled gently.
“That’s enough.”
Team Leader Kim’s smile cracked.
“What?”
“I said that’s enough.
I’m out of the Guild now, so stay out of my business.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
What did it mean?
“You know exactly what I mean.”
“All that ‘It couldn’t be helped,’ ‘At least you survived,’ and ‘Forget about it and make a fresh start.’ You pretended to comfort me while chipping away at me behind my back.”
“Weren’t you the first one to tell the Guild Master to fire me?
Did you think I wouldn’t find out?”
Kim Sangshik was a half-baked, petty little man.
Short on both humanity and ability.
Even inside Gates, he was always too busy saving his own skin.
His reputation within the Guild was rock-bottom.
“Who did you put in my place after firing me?
How much did they pay you to get them in?”
“Hey, Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Kim pressed down on my shoulder and growled.
He might not look it, but he was one of only three D-rank Hunters in Sopung Guild.
With that kind of strength, he could toy with an F-rank Hunter like me using one hand.
But—
“Take your hand off.”
I didn’t even blink.
It wasn’t only the System that had synchronized.
My martial arts, my stats, and even my steel-like Muscles and Bones had come with it.
“I’ll count to three.
Take your hand off.”
“You little bastard.
I’ve been putting up with you, but—”
I didn’t hesitate.
“One.
Two.”
Three.
The instant I seized Kim Sangshik’s wrist—
Clack.
“Would the next group please come in?
Numbers twenty-one through thirty!”
An Association examiner entered with a file in hand, and we sprang apart without waiting for the other to move first.
Getting on the Association’s bad side wouldn’t do either of us any good.
“Consider yourself lucky.”
“Who?
Me, or you?”
Kim Sangshik’s flushed face looked downright ridiculous.
So did the Level Window I picked up through Qi Sense.
System Lv.
24 Kim Sangshik
“Meeting you was disgusting.
Let’s never see each other again.”
I rose without a shred of regret.
My waiting number was thirty.
My steps toward the examiner were no longer stiff.
“Number twenty-one.
Please come forward.”
A tense-looking Awakened stood before the measuring device.
Made from an A-rank Magic Gem, it scanned his entire body and converted the mana inside him into numbers.
Bzzzzzt—
The examiner checked the reading.
“Amount of mana distributed throughout the body: F-rank.”
The Awakened’s face turned ashen.
But it was too soon to despair.
He still had a second chance.
“Try moving your mana.
Concentrate as hard as you can and imagine firing it into the measuring device.”
They were testing his mana control.
Realizing it wasn’t over yet, the Awakened gritted his teeth and strained with every ounce of strength he had—
Pfffft.
Looking ready to vomit, the examiner said, “Control ability: F-rank.”
“Please!
Just let me try one more time!”
“No.
Next.”
The line moved quickly.
Everyone was E-rank or F-rank.
One guy wasn’t even Awakened.
“This is a scam!
A scam!
That measuring device is made in China, isn’t it?
Huh?
You bastards!”
“Handle him.”
At the examiner’s command, the security Hunters waiting nearby dragged the fraudster away.
Even if that guy miraculously Awakened someday, he’d probably end up on the Association’s blacklist.
“Next.
Number thirty.”
Here it came.
I took a deep breath and stepped forward.
The examiner glanced at the file in his hand.
“This is a reassessment?”
“Yes.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung, you were rated F-rank seven years ago...
You’re aware that reassessments carry a separate fee, correct?”
From his tone, he might as well have been telling me not to waste my money and to go home while I still could.
The usual attitude toward an F-rank Hunter.
Do they think I’m a beggar?
I was used to it.
That didn’t make it any less insulting.
When I glared at him, the examiner gave a short laugh.
“I’m only mentioning it in case you weren’t aware, but the fee is two million won.”
“...The price went up?”
“It has been a few years.”
Fuck.
I didn’t know that.
How much was in my account right now...?
“Then we’ll begin the measurement.”
Nervous, I closed my eyes.
And the next moment—
Bzzzzzt.
A wave of magical power rolled out of the measuring device and swept through my whole body.

C-rank?

chapters.title: Chapter 48
paragraphs: “Y-you? What are you doing here?”
“Good question. What am I doing here?”
“Then, could it be...?”
“What do you mean, ‘could it be’? It is.”
Kim Sangshik’s face turned dark and sallow, like a man suffering from shit poisoning.
Seeing him like that felt like finally passing ten years’ worth of constipation. Ah, so this was a shitgasm.
“Anyway, let’s take a step back. We’re not the only ones here, you know.”
I stepped forward, and Kim Sangshik retreated weakly.
The other scouts surrounded me, business cards in hand.
“We’re from Sangdong Guild. We promise you the best possible treatment.”
“Instead of doing this here, why don’t we move somewhere private and talk...”
Recruitment offers poured in from every direction. Within moments, I had dozens of business cards in my hands.
So this is what it feels like.
It felt strange. Surreal. Things I hadn’t experienced once in seven years were unfolding right before my eyes.
In just half a day, the world around me had changed.
No.
I’m the one who changed.
People said C-rank was where you started being a real Hunter in this business. Exceptional abilities, a high salary, and recognition from society as a mid-level Hunter.
It finally sank in that I had set foot on that path.
And...
This was only the beginning.
With the System’s power, I could keep growing.
That was how I would step onto a new path faster than any other Hunter.
“Sir, name your terms and we’ll meet them, no matter what.”
“Ah, sure. I’ll contact you later.”
“You mean it, right? We’ll be waiting!”
No. Don’t wait. I’m not going to call.
“All right, everyone, calm down.”
Association security guards stepped in to hold back the scouts who refused to leave me alone.
They normally wouldn’t go this far for a C-rank Hunter, but my case was so unusual that it seemed to be attracting a lot of attention.
Well, I did jump all the way to C-rank from a single reawakening.
It wasn’t a bad feeling. No—it felt good.
Suppressing the smile that kept tugging at my lips, I left the Association. Even then, one person followed me out.
“Jin Taekyung! No, Mr. Taekyung!”
“Heh.”
I looked at Kim Sangshik and swallowed a hollow laugh.
Only thirty minutes ago, he’d been calling me a bastard. Now I was suddenly Mr. Taekyung.
“What do you want?”
“I’m sorry about earlier. Really. And I’m sorry about everything that happened before, too.”
Kim Sangshik rambled on, confessing every wrong he’d ever done me. Once his untimely confession was over, he finally got to the point.
“So let’s forget all that and treat this as business.”
“Business.”
I rolled the word around on my tongue.
It sounded nice. It felt awful. All the more so because the business partner in question was Kim Sangshik and Sopung Guild.
“You know how it is, Mr. Taekyung. Unless you’re dealing with a major Guild, they’re all more or less the same.”
“I know. I also know that even the major Guilds will reach out to a C-rank Hunter.”
“I’m telling you to think carefully. They’re not desperate. Major Guilds can find C-rank Hunters without much trouble, so they’ll treat you accordingly.”
Kim Sangshik kept going, spraying spit as he talked.
“No matter how much anyone else offers, we’ll top it. The Guild Master has already approved it, so you can count on that.”
Sopung Guild had been in steady decline for several years.
Given the situation, the Guild Master seemed scared shitless.
And this guy’s no different.
His standing in the Guild was already at rock bottom, and now the F-rank Hunter he’d fired on a whim a few days ago had reawakened as a C-rank.
The corners of my mouth rose at the thought of what would happen once the Guild Master, a man notorious for his temper, found out.
“Just look at it positively. Actually, forget standing around here. Why don’t we go somewhere decent and talk it out honestly? The Guild Master is on his way here right—”
“Mr. Kim Sangshik.”
At my quiet voice, Sangshik fell silent.
“If you want to recruit me, tell the Guild Master this. Don’t leave out a single word.”
“Tell him what?”
“I’ll think about it if he gets rid of one man I can’t stand the sight of.”
It was obvious who I meant.
Leaving Kim Sangshik behind with his face twisted in fury, I got into a taxi.
Yeah. That should do it.
I sank deep into the soft seat.
The rank reassessment. Running into old bad blood. An indescribable rush, and at the same time a sense of relief.
“Where would you like to go?”
“Hope Goshiwon at Songnae Station.”
The taxi driver looked at me and chuckled.
“Oh, you’re that passenger from earlier.”
“Ah.”
Goddamn Seoul taxis.
“What’s gotten into you? You actually bought beef.”
We spread out a mat and set up a grill on the goshiwon roof. Jinho hyung gazed contentedly at the meat as it cooked.
“All right. In recognition of your sincerity, I’ll forget about the finder’s fee.”
“I wasn’t planning to pay you anyway.”
“Are you some kind of thug?”
“Right back at you.”
We sat across from each other, sipping soju.
“But where did you get the money? Just this month, you were whining about how hard up you were.”
“Today’s pay.”
“How much could that possibly be? Did getting fired from the Guild make you give up on life?”
“How much?”
I couldn’t help letting out a little laugh.
“Oh, now you’re laughing?”
“Of course I am. You’re treating ten million won like pocket change.”
Jinho froze.
“How much?”
“Ten million won.”
“You made ten million won from one day’s work?”
“A little more came in, but that’s for now.”
“You didn’t...”
Jinho swallowed hard. He caught on fast. I gave him a meaningful smile.
“That’s right. Today, I—”
“Did you sell an organ?”
Should I kill him?
I let out a long sigh, then downed my drink.
“Tell me the truth. As the goshiwon manager, I have a duty to know.”
If you only heard that, you’d think he was the prime minister, not a goshiwon manager.
“I earned it at a Gate.”
“Show me proof. I only believe what I see with my own eyes.”
“Suit yourself. Here.”
I handed him my phone. The message had arrived while I was on my way back from the Association after the reassessment.
The sender was...
“Designer-Brand Junkie? Who’s this?”
“The Team Leader I ran the raid with today.”
“He must be rich. I want to become sworn brothers with him.”
This guy and I really did think alike.
A moment later, Jinho’s eyes widened as he read the message.
“Ten million three hundred thousand won? Am I reading this right?”
“Probably.”
According to the contract, I was supposed to receive three hundred thousand won. Team Leader Choi had added another ten million.
And there’s still a balance left.
The Hobgoblin Priest and Hobgoblin Great Warrior were C-rank Rare Monsters. Team Leader Choi had added that he was looking for buyers for their equipment, hides, and Magic Gems.
“We’ll make an additional payment as soon as they’re sold.”
The next thing I knew, I was at a nearby supermarket, sweeping up every piece of beef I could get my hands on.
Jinho stared blankly between me and the phone in his hand.
“Where the hell have you been, and what did you do?”
“It’s a long story.”
Jinho hyung chuckled and gripped the scissors.
“The story’s long, but your life’s about to be short?”
Where was I even supposed to begin?
I had decided not to tell him anything more about the capsule.
It seemed better to let him keep believing it was an absurd lie.
“Two Rare Monsters showed up at the Gate today, and...”
At a life-or-death moment, the luck of a reawakening had come, and I’d been able to take them down. Then I told him about the Association.
It was a hastily stitched-together story, but Jinho bought it.
“So you’re a C-rank Hunter now?”
“The reassessment process takes a few days, so technically, not yet.”
“Same thing, you idiot.”
His face was dazed and his voice hoarse.
Jinho hyung stared at me for a long moment. Moisture gathered in his eyes.
What’s gotten into this guy?
“...Don’t tell me you’re crying?”
“The fuck I am. What kind of bullshit is that?”
He turned away with an unnecessary curse, but he couldn’t hide the single tear that slipped down. I watched him out of the corner of my eye as he roughly rubbed his face with his sleeve.
“Hyung?”
“Turn the meat over. It’s burning.”
“Don’t change the subject.”
“I said it’s burning!”
“Okay, okay.”
Sizzle.
As I turned the meat, I felt flustered, yet something tickled deep in my chest.
Come to think of it, I’ve known Jinho for a long time.
Six years? Seven? I wasn’t sure. I’d never counted. Whenever I came back to the goshiwon after a hard day, he was always there.
Sometimes I wondered if this was what it would have felt like to have a real older brother. We had lived like brothers, like friends.
“Hey.”
Jinho broke the awkward silence. For no reason, I flipped the meat again.
“Yeah? What?”
“Good for you.”
“...Yeah.”
His quiet voice followed.
“You worked hard.”
Those few words were enough.
Something surged up from deep inside me. All the emotions and memories that had piled up over the past seven years came rushing in at once.
“Congratulations on becoming a C-rank Hunter. I guess I can’t make fun of you anymore.”
“Hyung...”
“Taekyung...”
“Hyung!”
“Taekyung!”
We hugged each other tightly across the grill. Jinho hyung whispered in my ear, his voice shaking.
“Do you remember what I said earlier?”
“I know how you feel, hyung. Thank you.”
“Not that. The finder’s fee.”
“...What?”
“Make sure you pay me. Hyung’s having a hard time these days.”
“You make a lot of money now.”
Should I really kill him?
I staggered back to my room and threw myself onto the bed.
I let out a little laugh, thinking of the one person who was probably cleaning up the roof while grumbling.
You really can’t let your guard down around him.
That was so like Jinho. The way he congratulated me, and the joke at the end.
I knew it was all just his way of expressing himself.
You worked hard.
Those words kept circling in my head. It was embarrassing to admit, but for a moment there, I had almost cried.
Yeah. I did work hard.
After my father died, I never stopped running. I worked part-time jobs while finishing high school, then kept enduring for the sake of my sick mother and little sister.
At some point, all of it had simply become a given.
And then—
Ding.
System You have been afflicted with the Status Effect Dead Drunk. - You can detoxify yourself by circulating your qi.
Something that wasn’t a given had entered my life.
It had all started with that unidentified piece-of-junk game capsule.
“A game capsule, huh?”
I didn’t even know what to call it anymore. It had made me a C-rank Hunter, so should I call it a gift from God?
No. Maybe it was a gift from the devil.
Is this really okay?
Even after the best day of my life, the thought still occurred to me for one simple reason.
Nothing comes for free.
That was the world I knew. Everything came with a price tag. Whether you could see it or not, sooner or later, you had to pay.
How much does the System cost?
A hundred billion won? A quadrillion won? Maybe even more?
I laughed weakly as my eyelids grew heavy.
Oh, right. I was dead drunk.
Chirp. Chirp-chirp.
Outside the window, the grass insects were crying loudly. My vision darkened, and sleep poured over me.
That night, I dreamed.
I dreamed that somewhere deep in the mountains, someone was shaking me awake.
“Captain! Captain!”

There was something about that voice that made me want to punch its owner just from hearing it. At the same time, it sounded familiar, and part of me wanted to see who it belonged to, but I was too sleepy to open my eyes.
“What do we do?”
“We have to tell the main force at once...”
“Why is Captain suddenly like this now of all times...”
It felt like listening to a broken radio. The voices crackled with static and kept cutting out.
I’m sleepy...
As my consciousness drifted farther away, I heard a quiet but distinct voice.
“Youngest, stay alive.”
But when I woke the next day, I couldn’t remember any of it.

What are you doing here?”
“Good question.
What am I doing here?”
“Then, could it be...?”
“What do you mean, ‘could it be’?
It is.”
Kim Sangshik’s face turned dark and sallow, like a man suffering from shit poisoning.
Seeing him like that felt like finally passing ten years’ worth of constipation.
Ah, so this was a shitgasm.
“Anyway, let’s take a step back.
We’re not the only ones here, you know.”
I stepped forward, and Kim Sangshik retreated weakly.
The other scouts surrounded me, business cards in hand.
“We’re from Sangdong Guild.
We promise you the best possible treatment.”
“Instead of doing this here, why don’t we move somewhere private and talk...”
Recruitment offers poured in from every direction.
Within moments, I had dozens of business cards in my hands.
So this is what it feels like.
It felt strange.
Surreal.
Things I hadn’t experienced once in seven years were unfolding right before my eyes.
In just half a day, the world around me had changed.
No.
I’m the one who changed.
People said C-rank was where you started being a real Hunter in this business.
Exceptional abilities, a high salary, and recognition from society as a mid-level Hunter.
It finally sank in that I had set foot on that path.
And...
This was only the beginning.
With the System’s power, I could keep growing.
That was how I would step onto a new path faster than any other Hunter.

“Ah, sure.
I’ll contact you later.”
“You mean it, right?
We’ll be waiting!”
No.
Don’t wait.
I’m not going to call.

Association security guards stepped in to hold back the scouts who refused to leave me alone.
They normally wouldn’t go this far for a C-rank Hunter, but my case was so unusual that it seemed to be attracting a lot of attention.
Well, I did jump all the way to C-rank from a single reawakening.
It wasn’t a bad feeling.
No—it felt good.

No, Mr.
Taekyung!”

Now I was suddenly Mr.
Taekyung.

Kim Sangshik rambled on, confessing every wrong he’d ever done me.

“So let’s forget all that and treat this as business.”
“Business.”
I rolled the word around on my tongue.
It sounded nice.
It felt awful.
All the more so because the business partner in question was Kim Sangshik and Sopung Guild.
“You know how it is, Mr.
Taekyung.
Unless you’re dealing with a major Guild, they’re all more or less the same.”
“I know.
I also know that even the major Guilds will reach out to a C-rank Hunter.”
“I’m telling you to think carefully.
They’re not desperate.
Major Guilds can find C-rank Hunters without much trouble, so they’ll treat you accordingly.”
Kim Sangshik kept going, spraying spit as he talked.
“No matter how much anyone else offers, we’ll top it.
The Guild Master has already approved it, so you can count on that.”
Sopung Guild had been in steady decline for several years.
Given the situation, the Guild Master seemed scared shitless.
And this guy’s no different.
His standing in the Guild was already at rock bottom, and now the F-rank Hunter he’d fired on a whim a few days ago had reawakened as a C-rank.
The corners of my mouth rose at the thought of what would happen once the Guild Master, a man notorious for his temper, found out.
“Just look at it positively.
Actually, forget standing around here.
Why don’t we go somewhere decent and talk it out honestly?
The Guild Master is on his way here right—”
“Mr.
Kim Sangshik.”
At my quiet voice, Sangshik fell silent.
“If you want to recruit me, tell the Guild Master this.
Don’t leave out a single word.”
“Tell him what?”
“I’ll think about it if he gets rid of one man I can’t stand the sight of.”
It was obvious who I meant.
Leaving Kim Sangshik behind with his face twisted in fury, I got into a taxi.
Yeah.
That should do it.
I sank deep into the soft seat.
The rank reassessment.
Running into old bad blood.
An indescribable rush, and at the same time a sense of relief.
“Where would you like to go?”
“Hope Goshiwon at Songnae Station.”
The taxi driver looked at me and chuckled.
“Oh, you’re that passenger from earlier.”
“Ah.”
Goddamn Seoul taxis.
“What’s gotten into you?
You actually bought beef.”
We spread out a mat and set up a grill on the goshiwon roof.
Jinho hyung gazed contentedly at the meat as it cooked.
“All right.
In recognition of your sincerity, I’ll forget about the finder’s fee.”
“I wasn’t planning to pay you anyway.”
“Are you some kind of thug?”
“Right back at you.”
We sat across from each other, sipping soju.
“But where did you get the money?
Just this month, you were whining about how hard up you were.”
“Today’s pay.”
“How much could that possibly be?
Did getting fired from the Guild make you give up on life?”
“How much?”
I couldn’t help letting out a little laugh.
“Oh, now you’re laughing?”
“Of course I am.
You’re treating ten million won like pocket change.”
Jinho froze.
“How much?”
“Ten million won.”
“You made ten million won from one day’s work?”
“A little more came in, but that’s for now.”
“You didn’t...”
Jinho swallowed hard.
He caught on fast.
I gave him a meaningful smile.
“That’s right.
Today, I—”
“Did you sell an organ?”
Should I kill him?
I let out a long sigh, then downed my drink.
“Tell me the truth.
As the goshiwon manager, I have a duty to know.”
If you only heard that, you’d think he was the prime minister, not a goshiwon manager.
“I earned it at a Gate.”
“Show me proof.
I only believe what I see with my own eyes.”
“Suit yourself.
Here.”
I handed him my phone.
The message had arrived while I was on my way back from the Association after the reassessment.
The sender was...
“Designer-Brand Junkie?
Who’s this?”
“The Team Leader I ran the raid with today.”
“He must be rich.
I want to become sworn brothers with him.”
This guy and I really did think alike.
A moment later, Jinho’s eyes widened as he read the message.
“Ten million three hundred thousand won?
Am I reading this right?”
“Probably.”
According to the contract, I was supposed to receive three hundred thousand won.
Team Leader Choi had added another ten million.
And there’s still a balance left.
The Hobgoblin Priest and Hobgoblin Great Warrior were C-rank Rare Monsters.
Team Leader Choi had added that he was looking for buyers for their equipment, hides, and Magic Gems.
“We’ll make an additional payment as soon as they’re sold.”
The next thing I knew, I was at a nearby supermarket, sweeping up every piece of beef I could get my hands on.
Jinho stared blankly between me and the phone in his hand.
“Where the hell have you been, and what did you do?”
“It’s a long story.”
Jinho hyung chuckled and gripped the scissors.
“The story’s long, but your life’s about to be short?”
Where was I even supposed to begin?
I had decided not to tell him anything more about the capsule.
It seemed better to let him keep believing it was an absurd lie.
“Two Rare Monsters showed up at the Gate today, and...”
At a life-or-death moment, the luck of a reawakening had come, and I’d been able to take them down.
Then I told him about the Association.
It was a hastily stitched-together story, but Jinho bought it.
“So you’re a C-rank Hunter now?”
“The reassessment process takes a few days, so technically, not yet.”
“Same thing, you idiot.”
His face was dazed and his voice hoarse.
Jinho hyung stared at me for a long moment.
Moisture gathered in his eyes.
What’s gotten into this guy?
“...Don’t tell me you’re crying?”
“The fuck I am.
What kind of bullshit is that?”
He turned away with an unnecessary curse, but he couldn’t hide the single tear that slipped down.
I watched him out of the corner of my eye as he roughly rubbed his face with his sleeve.
“Hyung?”
“Turn the meat over.
It’s burning.”
“Don’t change the subject.”

Sizzle.

Come to think of it, I’ve known Jinho for a long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 49
paragraphs: Early morning.
I eased my eyes open.
Ding.
System Exiting Sleep Mode.
The System notification came with a sigh of relief.
“Phew.”
Thank goodness. It hadn’t all been a dream.
It had only been one day, but yesterday had changed my life. If I’d woken up as Jin Taekyung, F-rank Hunter, reality would have felt like a nightmare.
I rustled my way up—and that was when it hit.
System Afflicted with the Status Effect Hangover.
“Urgh.”
Last night’s aftermath was no joke. I clutched my spinning head and sat cross-legged on the mattress.
According to the System, circulating my qi could detoxify me, too.
System Beginning Qi Circulation.

Following the formula of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, I guided my internal energy. The moment I began circulating my qi, the headache started to fade. About ten minutes later, the message I’d been waiting for appeared.
System Hangover disappears.
But I didn’t stop. I knew that ending the circulation abruptly midway would make it less effective.
Something I learned in Murim.
A full hour passed before I finally uncrossed my legs. My head was clear, and my body brimmed with energy.
The problem was...
Why am I taking in so little qi?
To increase my internal energy, I had to draw in qi from outside, store it within myself, and circulate it. But during my first attempt in reality, strangely little qi had entered my body.
And it’s murky, too.
It was like a tiny serving of bland food that took forever to arrive. I frowned.
Maybe it’s the pollution?
Since internal energy was based on pure natural qi, that was possible. Compared to Murim, the natural environment of modern society was in dire shape.
Or maybe it’s the location.
A single room in a decades-old goshiwon was hardly a nature-friendly place. It stank, and the facilities were run-down.
Despite being the goshiwon manager, Jinho hyung was always questioning what this place had originally been.

“Maybe it used to be a torture chamber. During the Great Cataclysm, they probably dragged monsters in, tapped them on the balls with a knife, and asked where the Demon King was. They would’ve given up the location of the Demon King’s parents, too.”
...You had to give him credit for his imagination.
He should be sleeping by now, right?
He treated getting up in the morning as a disgrace, so there was no need to check. I was wondering whether to go grab breakfast when—
Bzzzt.
A text arrived on my phone.
└ 〈 Designer-Brand Junkie └ Designer-Brand Junkie └ Do you have some time?
The sender was Designer-Brand Junkie—or rather, Team Leader Choi.
A glittering chandelier. Stylishly dressed people. Soft classical music playing in the background.
I couldn’t tell whether our meeting place was a café or a high-end restaurant.
“May I take your order?”
Shit. Even the waiter here looks like a celebrity.
He had a model’s proportions and the face of a handsome Greek god.
Is this how everyone turns gay?
While I was experiencing an identity crisis, Team Leader Choi calmly placed his order.
“One Black Ivory, please. What about you, Mr. Taekyung?”
The Greek god turned toward me.
Something about the atmosphere made me feel like I shouldn’t order a caramel macchiato.
“I’ll have the same.”
The coffee that arrived a little later was decent enough.
“It’s good. This is Black... what was it?”
“Black Ivory.”
Even after hearing the name again, I still had no idea what it meant. I just accepted it and moved on.
I muttered my honest take.
“It looks expensive. Do they use good beans?”
“It’s elephant dung.”
“Oh.”
I quietly set down my cup. Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh, then spoke.
“Congratulations.”
The congratulations came out of nowhere, but I immediately understood what he meant.
He was talking about yesterday’s rank reassessment.
“You’re fast. It’s personal information—the Association wouldn’t have opened all of it.”
“C-rank reawakened Hunters are rare. Besides, I saw what happened yesterday with my own eyes. How could I not know?”
Fair enough.
As I nodded, Team Leader Choi held something out to me. A single envelope lay neatly on the table.
“What is this?”
“You’ll know when you look.”
Don’t tell me—money?
I checked the contents. Instead of a check, tiny printed letters packed the page.
“It’s a contract.”
“These are the best terms our Guild can offer. Give it a read.”
I was already reading it, from the first line to the last. Every clause brought another surprise.
“This doesn’t look like a C-rank contract.”
After seven years in this business, I’d seen plenty and heard even more.
Yet even I had never seen a contract this generous.
“They’re good terms even among B-rank contracts.”
“Then why offer them to me...?”
“Because I trust myself.”
“What?”
“I trust my instincts and my eye for people. That’s why I want to sign you, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi set down his empty cup.
“Will you sign?”
Honestly, I was wavering. A lot.
It wasn’t only the terms. Someone had recognized me and wanted me this badly. I wanted to nod right then.
That was why I hesitated longer today than I had yesterday. By the time I finally made my decision, the coffee had gone cold.
“I’m sorry.”
My reason was the same as yesterday.
Under the contract, I would have to work as a Hunter affiliated with the Guild for at least one year.
I was grateful for the offer, but... I couldn’t rush this.
“Have you already signed with someone else? Or are you planning to?”
“No. I just need more time.”
“Time.”
Team Leader Choi sighed.
“I suppose it can’t be helped.”
I was about to apologize again when he said,
“Here’s my second offer.”
“Pardon?”
Team Leader Choi pulled another envelope from his jacket. Still dazed, I took it and checked the contents.
“A provisional contract?”
“You have a rough idea of what that is, right?”
Of course I did. I knew it well.
If the Manpower Office was day labor, a provisional contract with a Guild was temp work. You’d be attached to the Guild for a short stretch, basically a mercenary.
“You won’t turn this one down too, will you?”
It wasn’t quite as generous as the formal contract, but the terms were still excellent. More importantly, the contract period had been left blank.
“Write down whatever period you want.”
“Oh. Right.”
I took the pen he offered, still somewhat dazed.
After thinking it over, I wrote seven days. A week should be enough time to see whether the System would last.
Once I’d signed, Team Leader Choi held out his hand.
“I look forward to working with you.”
“That’s my line.”
As we shook hands firmly, it finally sank in that I’d taken my first step as a C-rank Hunter.
Even if it’s only a provisional contract.
My chest swelled with emotion.
“Should I come in tomorrow?”
“No.”
Team Leader Choi tapped his watch.
“Starting now.”
Vroom.
Team Leader Choi’s car was a large military vehicle. He looked like the type to collect expensive supercars, so this was unexpected. I only understood why after we arrived at the Gate.
“Pick something.”
“Pick what?”
“Equipment.”
Team Leader Choi pressed a small button, and a trunk large enough for five grown men to lie down in appeared.
“I had it modified for work. Leaving all this at home felt kind of off.”
I stared into the trunk with my mouth hanging open.
Holy crap.

Equipment worth at least several million won was neatly stacked and sorted inside. Armor and weapons were only the beginning. There were all kinds of potions and even disposable magic scrolls that most people considered too expensive to use. He had everything.
“...Is all of this yours, Team Leader?”
“For now. Some were gifts, and I bought some because they looked nice.”
Ah. So he bought equipment because it looked nice.
How rich do you have to be to think like that?
C-rank Hunters made good money, but Team Leader Choi’s spending was already beyond that. He must have been rich enough that money was never a concern.
Gulp.
“I think I’d rather rent something. If I borrow yours and it gets damaged, it’d be a little...”
“They’re out of fashion, so it doesn’t matter.”
Ah. So he even cared whether equipment was fashionable.
I gave up thinking about it around there and picked my equipment.
The System made the process easy.
Item check.
Ding.

System Item Window Lizardman Hunter’s Leather Set Type: Armor Grade: First Rate Restriction: None Description: Made by skinning a Lizardman and using its hide whole. Scale Armor activates when the full set is equipped.
This looks pretty good.
It was light, and the leather was both tough and hard.
As soon as I put on the entire set, the Scale Armor effect activated.
“Oh.”
Green scales rose from the leather, forming a dense layer over my entire body. Team Leader Choi nodded when he saw me.
“You picked a good one. You’ve got a good eye.”
It’s the System that’s good.
I smiled awkwardly and rummaged through the weapons. Come to think of it, I’d only ever seen Team Leader Choi use a sword, but there were more than five types of weapons in the trunk alone.
They’ve all been used, too.
I could see traces of the effort he’d put into finding the weapon that suited him.
A little later, I found myself holding a spear.
System Item Window Lizardman Slayer’s Harpoon Type: Weapon Grade: First Rate Restriction: None Description: On a successful attack, Bleeding has a high chance of activating.
Anyone who saw me would think I had a Lizardman fetish.
The spear completed my equipment selection. Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh.
“What’s so funny?”
“I was just thinking that things are going well.”
“Pardon?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
I had no idea what he meant, but I followed him to the front of the Gate. Instead of an Administration staffer, some man was standing there.
“You’ve arrived.”
He bowed at a perfect ninety-degree angle. Even more surprising was how naturally Team Leader Choi accepted it.
“How’s the Gate?”
“Yes. I received your call yesterday and restricted access.”
“Thank you for your hard work.”
“Not at all, Young Master.”
That term could be used by a woman to address her husband’s unmarried younger brother, but there was no way this man was Team Leader Choi’s sister-in-law...
So Team Leader Choi was the young master of some rich family.
No wonder.
I should have realized it the moment I saw him decked out in luxury equipment from head to toe.
And being fashion-conscious enough to care about equipment design? You couldn’t pull that off unless you’d been born with one hell of a gold spoon.
That guy has everything.
The man who had everything turned to me.
“All right. Let’s go in.”
“Right now?”
“The equipment is taken care of. Is there a problem?”
His tone made it sound so obvious that I looked around.
There was me, Team Leader Choi, and the unfamiliar middle-aged man. That was everyone.
“What about the other team members?”
“They’re right here. The team members.”
“Oh, I see. He’s going in too, right?”
The middle-aged man cut in, his voice heavy.
“I’m not.”
“Then...?”
“It’s just the two of us. There’s no one else.”
Team Leader Choi’s answer left me dumbfounded.
“No one else?”
“No.”
“Not even one person?”
“We’re not bringing so much as a dog.”
Look at how decisive he was. Who was he, Judge Bao?
“So the two of us are clearing the Gate alone?”
“Why not? It’s only a D-rank Gate.”
“This is my first D-rank Gate.”
“I’ve been to plenty.”
No, fuck...
A D-rank Gate wasn’t some neighborhood discount store.
“If it’s just the two of us, I’m backing out.”
To raid a D-rank Gate safely, you needed a team of ten D-rank Hunters. I could use the System, and I’d learned martial arts, but that didn’t eliminate every danger.
“I know what you’re thinking, Mr. Jin Taekyung. But let me tell you one thing.”
Team Leader Choi continued in a relaxed voice.
“I’m a reawakened Hunter, too.”
“Reawakened? I thought you were C-rank, Team Leader...”
“C-rank was what I received when I was first measured. My reawakening happened afterward.”
Meaning his abilities were at least B-rank.
The odds were slim, but he could be even higher.
A B-rank Hunter.
If that was true, the situation changed. Just the two of us also meant a bigger cut for me.
“If you want to go back, I won’t stop you. I can go in alone. It wouldn’t be the first or second time.”
He walked in and out of D-rank Gates alone on the regular?
“Then take care. Starting tomorrow, we’ll look for E-rank Gates.”
That sealed it.
I grabbed his shoulder as he turned away.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“I want to... raid.”
Team Leader Choi smiled warmly.
“Let’s do our best.”

It hadn’t all been a dream.
It had only been one day, but yesterday had changed my life.
If I’d woken up as Jin Taekyung, F-rank Hunter, reality would have felt like a nightmare.
I rustled my way up—and that was when it hit.
System Afflicted with the Status Effect Hangover.
“Urgh.”
Last night’s aftermath was no joke.
I clutched my spinning head and sat cross-legged on the mattress.
According to the System, circulating my qi could detoxify me, too.
System Beginning Qi Circulation.
Following the formula of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, I guided my internal energy.
The moment I began circulating my qi, the headache started to fade.
About ten minutes later, the message I’d been waiting for appeared.
System Hangover disappears.
But I didn’t stop.
I knew that ending the circulation abruptly midway would make it less effective.
Something I learned in Murim.
A full hour passed before I finally uncrossed my legs.
My head was clear, and my body brimmed with energy.
The problem was...
Why am I taking in so little qi?
To increase my internal energy, I had to draw in qi from outside, store it within myself, and circulate it.
But during my first attempt in reality, strangely little qi had entered my body.
And it’s murky, too.
It was like a tiny serving of bland food that took forever to arrive.
I frowned.
Maybe it’s the pollution?
Since internal energy was based on pure natural qi, that was possible.
Compared to Murim, the natural environment of modern society was in dire shape.
Or maybe it’s the location.
A single room in a decades-old goshiwon was hardly a nature-friendly place.
It stank, and the facilities were run-down.
Despite being the goshiwon manager, Jinho hyung was always questioning what this place had originally been.
“Maybe it used to be a torture chamber.
During the Great Cataclysm, they probably dragged monsters in, tapped them on the balls with a knife, and asked where the Demon King was.
They would’ve given up the location of the Demon King’s parents, too.”
...You had to give him credit for his imagination.
He should be sleeping by now, right?
He treated getting up in the morning as a disgrace, so there was no need to check.
I was wondering whether to go grab breakfast when—
Bzzzt.
A text arrived on my phone.
└ 〈 Designer-Brand Junkie └ Designer-Brand Junkie └ Do you have some time?
The sender was Designer-Brand Junkie—or rather, Team Leader Choi.
A glittering chandelier.
Stylishly dressed people.
Soft classical music playing in the background.
I couldn’t tell whether our meeting place was a café or a high-end restaurant.
“May I take your order?”
Shit.
Even the waiter here looks like a celebrity.
He had a model’s proportions and the face of a handsome Greek god.
Is this how everyone turns gay?
While I was experiencing an identity crisis, Team Leader Choi calmly placed his order.
“One Black Ivory, please.
What about you, Mr.
Taekyung?”
The Greek god turned toward me.
Something about the atmosphere made me feel like I shouldn’t order a caramel macchiato.
“I’ll have the same.”
The coffee that arrived a little later was decent enough.
“It’s good.
This is Black... what was it?”
“Black Ivory.”
Even after hearing the name again, I still had no idea what it meant.
I just accepted it and moved on.
I muttered my honest take.
“It looks expensive.
Do they use good beans?”
“It’s elephant dung.”
“Oh.”
I quietly set down my cup.
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh, then spoke.
“Congratulations.”
The congratulations came out of nowhere, but I immediately understood what he meant.
He was talking about yesterday’s rank reassessment.
“You’re fast.
It’s personal information—the Association wouldn’t have opened all of it.”
“C-rank reawakened Hunters are rare.
Besides, I saw what happened yesterday with my own eyes.
How could I not know?”
Fair enough.
As I nodded, Team Leader Choi held something out to me.
A single envelope lay neatly on the table.
“What is this?”
“You’ll know when you look.”
Don’t tell me—money?
I checked the contents.
Instead of a check, tiny printed letters packed the page.
“It’s a contract.”
“These are the best terms our Guild can offer.
Give it a read.”
I was already reading it, from the first line to the last.
Every clause brought another surprise.
“This doesn’t look like a C-rank contract.”
After seven years in this business, I’d seen plenty and heard even more.
Yet even I had never seen a contract this generous.
“They’re good terms even among B-rank contracts.”
“Then why offer them to me...?”
“Because I trust myself.”
“What?”
“I trust my instincts and my eye for people.
That’s why I want to sign you, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi set down his empty cup.
“Will you sign?”
Honestly, I was wavering.
A lot.
It wasn’t only the terms.
Someone had recognized me and wanted me this badly.
I wanted to nod right then.
That was why I hesitated longer today than I had yesterday.
By the time I finally made my decision, the coffee had gone cold.
“I’m sorry.”
My reason was the same as yesterday.
Under the contract, I would have to work as a Hunter affiliated with the Guild for at least one year.
I was grateful for the offer, but...
I couldn’t rush this.
“Have you already signed with someone else?
Or are you planning to?”
“No.
I just need more time.”
“Time.”
Team Leader Choi sighed.
“I suppose it can’t be helped.”
I was about to apologize again when he said,
“Here’s my second offer.”
“Pardon?”
Team Leader Choi pulled another envelope from his jacket.
Still dazed, I took it and checked the contents.
“A provisional contract?”
“You have a rough idea of what that is, right?”
Of course I did.
I knew it well.
If the Manpower Office was day labor, a provisional contract with a Guild was temp work.
You’d be attached to the Guild for a short stretch, basically a mercenary.
“You won’t turn this one down too, will you?”
It wasn’t quite as generous as the formal contract, but the terms were still excellent.
More importantly, the contract period had been left blank.
“Write down whatever period you want.”
“Oh.
Right.”
I took the pen he offered, still somewhat dazed.
After thinking it over, I wrote seven days.
A week should be enough time to see whether the System would last.
Once I’d signed, Team Leader Choi held out his hand.
“I look forward to working with you.”
“That’s my line.”
As we shook hands firmly, it finally sank in that I’d taken my first step as a C-rank Hunter.
Even if it’s only a provisional contract.
My chest swelled with emotion.
“Should I come in tomorrow?”
“No.”
Team Leader Choi tapped his watch.
“Starting now.”
Vroom.
Team Leader Choi’s car was a large military vehicle.
He looked like the type to collect expensive supercars, so this was unexpected.
I only understood why after we arrived at the Gate.
“Pick something.”
“Pick what?”
“Equipment.”
Team Leader Choi pressed a small button, and a trunk large enough for five grown men to lie down in appeared.
“I had it modified for work.
Leaving all this at home felt kind of off.”
I stared into the trunk with my mouth hanging open.
Holy crap.
Equipment worth at least several million won was neatly stacked and sorted inside.
Armor and weapons were only the beginning.
There were all kinds of potions and even disposable magic scrolls that most people considered too expensive to use.
He had everything.
“...Is all of this yours, Team Leader?”
“For now.
Some were gifts, and I bought some because they looked nice.”
Ah.
So he bought equipment because it looked nice.
How rich do you have to be to think like that?
C-rank Hunters made good money, but Team Leader Choi’s spending was already beyond that.
He must have been rich enough that money was never a concern.
Gulp.
“I think I’d rather rent something.
If I borrow yours and it gets damaged, it’d be a little...”
“They’re out of fashion, so it doesn’t matter.”
Ah.
So he even cared whether equipment was fashionable.
I gave up thinking about it around there and picked my equipment.
The System made the process easy.
Item check.
Ding.
System Item Window Lizardman Hunter’s Leather Set Type: Armor Grade: First Rate Restriction: None Description: Made by skinning a Lizardman and using its hide whole.
Scale Armor activates when the full set is equipped.
This looks pretty good.
It was light, and the leather was both tough and hard.
As soon as I put on the entire set, the Scale Armor effect activated.
“Oh.”
Green scales rose from the leather, forming a dense layer over my entire body.
Team Leader Choi nodded when he saw me.
“You picked a good one.
You’ve got a good eye.”
It’s the System that’s good.
I smiled awkwardly and rummaged through the weapons.
Come to think of it, I’d only ever seen Team Leader Choi use a sword, but there were more than five types of weapons in the trunk alone.
They’ve all been used, too.
I could see traces of the effort he’d put into finding the weapon that suited him.
A little later, I found myself holding a spear.
System Item Window Lizardman Slayer’s Harpoon Type: Weapon Grade: First Rate Restriction: None Description: On a successful attack, Bleeding has a high chance of activating.
Anyone who saw me would think I had a Lizardman fetish.
The spear completed my equipment selection.
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh.
“What’s so funny?”
“I was just thinking that things are going well.”
“Pardon?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
I had no idea what he meant, but I followed him to the front of the Gate.
Instead of an Administration staffer, some man was standing there.
“You’ve arrived.”
He bowed at a perfect ninety-degree angle.
Even more surprising was how naturally Team Leader Choi accepted it.
“How’s the Gate?”
“Yes.
I received your call yesterday and restricted access.”
“Thank you for your hard work.”
“Not at all, Young Master.”
That term could be used by a woman to address her husband’s unmarried younger brother, but there was no way this man was Team Leader Choi’s sister-in-law...
So Team Leader Choi was the young master of some rich family.
No wonder.
I should have realized it the moment I saw him decked out in luxury equipment from head to toe.
And being fashion-conscious enough to care about equipment design?
You couldn’t pull that off unless you’d been born with one hell of a gold spoon.
That guy has everything.
The man who had everything turned to me.
“All right.
Let’s go in.”
“Right now?”
“The equipment is taken care of.
Is there a problem?”
His tone made it sound so obvious that I looked around.
There was me, Team Leader Choi, and the unfamiliar middle-aged man.
That was everyone.
“What about the other team members?”
“They’re right here.
The team members.”
“Oh, I see.
He’s going in too, right?”
The middle-aged man cut in, his voice heavy.
“I’m not.”
“Then...?”
“It’s just the two of us.
There’s no one else.”
Team Leader Choi’s answer left me dumbfounded.
“No one else?”
“No.”
“Not even one person?”
“We’re not bringing so much as a dog.”
Look at how decisive he was.
Who was he, Judge Bao?
“So the two of us are clearing the Gate alone?”
“Why not?
It’s only a D-rank Gate.”
“This is my first D-rank Gate.”
“I’ve been to plenty.”
No, fuck...
A D-rank Gate wasn’t some neighborhood discount store.
“If it’s just the two of us, I’m backing out.”
To raid a D-rank Gate safely, you needed a team of ten D-rank Hunters.
I could use the System, and I’d learned martial arts, but that didn’t eliminate every danger.
“I know what you’re thinking, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
But let me tell you one thing.”
Team Leader Choi continued in a relaxed voice.
“I’m a reawakened Hunter, too.”
“Reawakened?
I thought you were C-rank, Team Leader...”
“C-rank was what I received when I was first measured.
My reawakening happened afterward.”
Meaning his abilities were at least B-rank.
The odds were slim, but he could be even higher.
A B-rank Hunter.
If that was true, the situation changed.
Just the two of us also meant a bigger cut for me.
“If you want to go back, I won’t stop you.
I can go in alone.
It wouldn’t be the first or second time.”
He walked in and out of D-rank Gates alone on the regular?
“Then take care.
Starting tomorrow, we’ll look for E-rank Gates.”
That sealed it.
I grabbed his shoulder as he turned away.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“I want to... raid.”
Team Leader Choi smiled warmly.
“Let’s do our best.”

chapters.title: Chapter 50
paragraphs: My mouth fell open at the sight before me.
Amid the hot, humid air, wetlands stretched endlessly through dense forest.
“This is a D-rank Gate...”
I knew higher-ranked Gates contained larger spaces. I just hadn’t expected the difference to be this extreme.
“Big, isn’t it?”
I forgot all about being angry and answered.
“Yeah. Big enough to be daunting.”
“This is about average. Once you reach B-rank Gates, you even have to hire a separate guide.”
“...Feels like we need one now.”
“We’ll be fine today.”
Team Leader Choi pulled out a laminated sheet and showed it to me.
“What’s that?”
“A map. They gave it to me when the rights were transferred.”
A map. Then we wouldn’t have to worry about getting lost—
“Wait. What did you just say?”
“I said it was a map.”
“No, not that. What you said after that.”
“You mean the transfer of rights?”
Yeah, you. That.
“What does that mean?”
“Exactly what it sounds like.”
Team Leader Choi spoke as if it were no big deal.
“This Gate is mine.”
“What?”
“More precisely, I hold the exclusive rights to it.”
Maybe it was the wetlands. Sweat beaded on my palms, and my throat went bone-dry.
I swallowed a dry gulp.
Exclusive rights to a Gate?
In Korea, Gates were national property.
Since the Great Cataclysm, Magic Gems had become a core energy source, and Gates were essentially diamond mines that never ran dry. Yet this guy held the exclusive rights to one.
Who the hell is he?
I knew he was some rich family’s young master, but I hadn’t realized he was this rich.
“Let’s get moving.”
Team Leader Choi strode ahead. His back looked dazzling.
Ah, that golden radiance. The scent of untouchable wealth.
I’ll bury my bones in your Guild.
I swore it then and there.
The wetlands were a maze.
Without a capable guide like Team Leader Choi, I would have wandered for a long time. How long had we been walking when—
- Keeiik.
The cry grew clearer as I drew up my internal energy.
A monster had appeared.
At least twenty.
According to Team Leader Choi’s explanation on the way here, the monsters in this Gate were swamp Lizardmen.
They lived in several colonies under a single tribe, and this seemed to be one of them.
“This is the small colony closest to the entrance. There should be about twenty, so let’s take them out quickly and move on.”

Team Leader Choi hacked through the vines as he advanced. He was usually a pretty-faced young master, but once actual combat began, he was no joke. Watching him barrel forward like an eight-ton truck with a broken steering wheel, I could practically smell the machismo.
He’s fucking cool.
I felt like we could sweep aside not just thirty Lizardmen, but a hundred, as long as Team Leader Choi was with me.
Now I understood why people got high-level players to carry them in online games.
“Keiik!”
Maybe that was why I didn’t feel particularly nervous when I came face-to-face with Lizardmen for the first time.
Mostly, I was fascinated to see monsters I’d only ever encountered in photos and videos.
“Oh, they’re big.”
Even the smallest of the twenty stood a head taller than me.
They were at least two meters tall, with lean muscles and thick tails that made them look even larger.
Still not as big as the Hobgoblin Great Warrior I fought yesterday, though.
These hideous basketball prospects didn’t seem too happy to see us.
- Keiik!
- Keet! Keet!
Dozens of harpoons flashed in their hands. I watched them approach from the front, spreading out to surround us.
“No archers.”
“Swamp Lizardmen mostly use harpoons. They might throw them, so be careful.”
“Yep.”
As expected of a lizard expert. He even stood there with his arms casually folded.
“Keiik!”
They had closed to within twenty meters. I grinned at Team Leader Choi.
“These guys have no fear.”
“That’s a Lizardman trait. They’re reckless, and they prefer a head-on fight.”
“Aha.”
In the meantime, the distance shrank to ten meters. Team Leader Choi’s folded arms were starting to bother me.
“I think it’s about time we started fighting.”
“Guess we should.”
“...Ah. Right. We should.”
Whoosh!
Then three or four harpoons tore through the air. If I’d still been an F-rank Hunter, my life would have flashed before my eyes. Now I just swung my spear and batted them aside.
Clang, clang, clang!
That was when I noticed something strange.
- Kieeeik!
- Keet! Keiik!
What’s wrong with them?
Their eyes rolled back until only the whites showed, and they shrieked wildly. This went beyond hostility. It was practically hatred.
As I stood there bewildered, Team Leader Choi casually remarked,
“It’s because of your equipment.”
Equipment? What did my equipment—
Ah.
Lizardman Hunter’s Leather Set. Lizardman Slayer’s Harpoon.
Shit. Just look at those names.
If I were a Lizardman, I’d throw harpoons too.
Come to think of it, they only threw them at me.
With their people’s mortal enemy standing right in front of them, they were treating Team Leader Choi like he was invisible.
At this rate, I was going to be the only one they attacked—
No, wait.
“Did you plan this?”
“Plan what?”
“You dressed me in this so I’d pull aggro while you mopped them up. That was your strategy all along, wasn’t it?”
“I swear it wasn’t.”
Team Leader Choi’s face turned serious as he added,
“I’m going to stand back and do nothing.”
“What?”
“You’ll pull the aggro and handle the raid. Don’t get the wrong idea.”
What the hell kind of bullshit is that?
“So... you want me to fight them alone?”
“Yes.”
“While you stand there with your arms folded and watch?”
“I’ll unfold my arms.”
“No, for fuck’s sake...”
“Harpoons incoming.”
Whoosh!
Harpoons flew as green scales flashed from every direction and the Lizardmen charged.
Team Leader Choi sprang back and shouted with heroic gravity,
“You got this!”
Was this guy completely insane?
I wanted to run over and grab him by the collar, but harpoons were already flying at me from every direction.
Clang!
- Keiik!
“You bastards.”
Grinding my teeth, I drew up my Qi Sense. Soon, twenty spears sprang up over their heads.
System Lv. 40 Lizardman Tribesman
Level 40, huh?
I tightened my grip on my spear.
“You’re all dead.”
Ding.

System Damage dealt to this monster increases by 10% due to the effect of Lizardman Hunter’s Leather Set. - Damage dealt to this monster increases by 20% due to the effect of Lizardman Slayer’s Harpoon. - All Lizardmen in this Gate are hostile toward you. They will never stop until they have avenged this grudge!
At the same time, the Lizardman Slayer’s Harpoon traced a heavy arc. The forms of the Jin Family’s Spear Technique, now at Seven Stars, poured toward them.
Crunch!
- Keiik...
The yellow reptilian eyes slowly closed.
The green wetlands were soaked with the corpses and blood of the ones already dead. Not a single Lizardman was left standing.
Ding.
System Level Up! - Level Up!
Leaving the cheerful System notifications behind, I turned around.
Team Leader Choi was leaning against a tree. He’d said he would unfold his arms, but there he was with them folded again. That made me twice as pissed.
“What do you think you’re doing?”
Team Leader Choi silently stared at me, then tossed something over.
A small drink bottle filled with red liquid. A potion that restored depleted Stamina.
“So first you make me sick, then you give me medicine?”
“You look rather healthy for a sick man. You don’t have so much as a scratch.”
...That actually sounded plausible. I almost let myself be convinced.
While I hesitated, Team Leader Choi spoke.
“I’m sorry.”
He didn’t stop there. He even bowed at the waist.
It was such a formal apology that I was left with nothing to say. My anger eased, but I still wanted to know why he had done it.
“Why did you do that?”
“I needed to see what you could do.”
“Just for that?”
“It’s important to me. I need to know how you move, how many enemies you can handle, and how far we can go together.”
“So you just slipped out alone while it was crawling with monsters?”
“If I hadn’t trusted you, I wouldn’t have done it.”
I had to admit, praise felt pretty good coming from someone as capable as him.
More importantly, I didn’t get hurt, and I leveled up twice.
Trying not to sound too eager, I asked,
“So what’s the verdict?”
“Hmm.”
Team Leader Choi studied me with that peculiar look of his. At last, he spoke.
“I still don’t know.”
“What?”
“Which is why...”
Team Leader Choi pulled something out and tossed it to me.
It was a long, opaque cylinder. Liquid sloshed inside when I shook it.
“What’s this, a potion?”
“There’s a button on the bottom, right? Press it.”
Does that open it?
I tilted my head and pressed the button.
Click.
The front of the cylinder sprang wide open.
The problem was—
Fwoooosh—
Boom!
Whatever had been inside shot up like a firework and burst in midair. The pink liquid exploded outward, spreading over a wide area.
“Huh?”
What is that?
As I stared blankly, Team Leader Choi’s voice slipped into my ear.
“Pheromones.”
“Pheromones? Like perfume?”
“Something like that.”
“They were extracted from female Lizardmen.”
The instant he finished speaking, I felt a tremor from somewhere.
It was the ground. The ground was rumbling.
Team Leader Choi kindly added,
“They’re extremely potent.”
You bastard...
“Team Leader Three.”
Those were the first words the half-gray, middle-aged man had spoken in an hour. Kim Sangshik, who had spent all that time waiting while the Guild Master chain-smoked, answered immediately.
“Yes, Guild Master.”
“Curious, aren’t you? Figured I called you in first thing this morning to raise hell?”
“Ah, no, sir.”
The Sopung Guild Master smiled good-naturedly.
“You’re right.”
“What?”
“I called you to raise hell.”
“Do you know where I went today?”
The Guild Master exhaled a plume of cigarette smoke.
“The Guild Alliance breakfast meeting.”
Small and midsize Guilds were businesses too. In every region, Guild Masters held meetings to socialize and strengthen their alliances. Today had been one of those occasions.

“I went there on an empty stomach, and just as I was finally about to take a bite, that Sangdong Guild Master bastard told me something interesting. He said the C-rank who awakened recently had been one of our Guild members until a few days ago.”
“...Guild Master, that’s—”
The Guild Master raised a hand, cutting Kim Sangshik off.
“I thought it was bullshit. The Sangdong Guild Master might be a rude bastard, but he’s not the type to make up stories. Especially not at an alliance meeting.”
“I-I’ll look into it again!”
“Team Leader Three? No. No need.”
The Guild Master flung a crumpled bundle of papers across the room.
“I already looked into it myself.”
Kim Sangshik recognized the crumpled papers for what they were: someone’s personal file.
He recognized the name on it too.
“Jin Taekyung. Team Leader Three knows that name too, right?”
Fuck.
Kim Sangshik squeezed his eyes shut as the Guild Master tapped the ash from his cigarette.
“I know how you feel, Team Leader Three. You’re a founding member of the Guild, after all. You’re allowed to fire one bottom-tier Hunter you don’t like. Stick your beloved son in the vacancy. Right?”
“Yes. Yes, sir.”

“But the F-rank loach you treated like dirt and kicked out turned into a dragon and came back, huh? I even made a point of telling you to recruit him, but if you told the truth I’d obviously raise hell. You’d get a reputation for having dog eyes that can’t even recognize someone. So you filed a false report, right?”
Sizzle.
The Guild Master crushed out his cigarette. As the embers scattered, the last of his patience vanished with them.
“Team Leader Three. No, Sangshik. Have we been together about twenty years?”
Kim Sangshik answered uneasily.
“Twenty-one years, Guild Master.”
“That’s not what I meant.”
“...Yes, hyung.”
“Good. That sounds much better. Keep calling me that from now on.”
“What?”
“I’ve carried you for twenty-one years. I’ve done more than enough. I’ll speak to the rest of Team Three separately, so you’re leaving the Guild as of today.”
“H-hyung.”
“Shut your mouth, leave quietly, and I won’t block your path. Once you’re out, do whatever you want.”
The Guild Master’s voice was packed with tightly suppressed fury.
Kim Sangshik realized he had no other choice.
Leave? Leave the Guild?
He had spent more than twenty years at this job. And now he was being told to leave over something like this. Cast aside without a second thought.
Fuck...
He clenched his teeth and walked out of the office.
One last blow came after him.
“Hey, HR. Process two terminations today. Kim Sangshik and Kim Sangho.”
For the next few days, Sopung Guild was in an uproar over the rare event of a father and son being forced out at the same time.
Along with that, the latest news about the bottom-tier Hunter who had recently left became the hottest topic in the Guild.
“They say he’s C-rank now. Reawakening.”
“Oh my, Mr. Taekyung? The Taekyung I know?”
“That’s what I’m telling you. He hit the jackpot. Apparently Kim Sangshik went to recruit him without even realizing who he was and got flat-out rejected.”
“He found every excuse he could to fire him, and now he’s reaping what he sowed. I heard Team Leader Kim’s been going around claiming he was wrongfully dismissed and badmouthing the Guild Master.”
“He still hasn’t come to his senses. Man, I’m jealous, though. When will I ever get to live a life like that?”
“Honestly, Taekyung deserves it. He worked so hard that luck finally found him.”
“Deserves it, my ass. Then are the rest of us all just living it up? It’s luck. All luck.”
Half envy and half jealousy, the conversations always ended with the same question.
“Where is Mr. Taekyung now, and what’s he doing?”
